Overall I have been pretty happy with the Maxcam Charger. I bought it because I wanted something I could use to store my extra batteries as well as charge them, and it serves that purpose well. The build quality leaves little to be desired, and the matte finish scratches off with the smallest abrasions. The light from each battery indicator also bleeds into the next indicator, so it can be difficult to distinguish the status of each of the batteries. I used it with the new GoPro hero 8 batteries and it worked. The one issue I am most concerned about is the fit of the battery in the charger. It doesn’t feel secure in the slot the same way it does when you slid it into the GoPro, and if you turn the charger upside down with the door open, all the batteries would fall out. This isn’t an issue at the moment as the door has a decent clicking closure, but I am afraid that over time as the tolerances start to relax and the foam at the base of the charger starts to weaken, the battery may have enough play to disconnect from the charging foot if, for example, the charger is being used upside down. The LED indicators can also be difficult to see from certain angles as they are recessed into the unit quite a bit. They also bleed into each other making the red (for not yet charged) look like a yellow/orange when it is next to a green LED. I still think this is the best design on the market for charging multiple GoPro batteries, but I do wish they had invested a bit more money/time into the build quality.

Also, I wanted to have the porch lights on either side of the door match each other.I resolved all of these issues by purchasing new porch lights, one with a GFCI outlet, along with an outlet to bulb converter. Now I'm struggling to find the right speaker volume that plays clearly, and also figure out why the microphone doesn't pick up sounds while using the two way communication feature. I'm also having a problem with the playback speed of recordings, using the Wansview app. There is a button to choose 1x, 2x, and 4x speeds, but no matter which I choose, it always seems to be played back at 2x (or maybe 4x, but not 1x). Hopefully I can resolve these last issues. I'll follow up when/if I do. 6/22/23 - The tech support folks updated my camera's firmware, and afterwards, playback speed is 1x, but I can't seem to get it playback at 2x or 4x now. 6/27/23 - Tech support somehow fixed the playback speed, sort of. Regardless of the initial setting, it always starts at 1x. Changing to 2x or 4x while playing back is how to get it to work. Unfortunately, the biggest problem is that it is not sending notifications. The camera notices motion, records it as an alert, but doesn't send a notification. So, I can't use it to ward off solicitors from selling stuff to my mom who has alzheimers disease. Even when notifications were working (last week?), there are either too many false alarms, or it misses people altogether, even though there is a "people" setting. Perhaps that works better if you buy a subscription for the cloud service, but I'm trying to maintain a secure network, and avoid cloud subscriptions. 7/13/2023 - The company has refunded my purchase price for the camera, and allowed me to keep it. Unfortunately, as long as the problem with notifications and person detection remain broken, the camera is of little value to me.

I cannot complain about the picture but I also understand there are customers out there that are much more nuanced and demanding in their opinion of picture quality. I am simply not one of those people. What I will say is that I'm lowering my 5 star review to 3 stars. This monitor has an annoying habit of powering up (even if nothing is connected to it) and saying 'no input found' and then 'entering power saving mode'. No matter what I do, this will not cease, so these messages continue 24/7 year round even when the PC is powered down and there are no HDMI or other connections. I'm convinced that this constant powering up and down will reduce the lifespan of the product. It cannot be healthy. There are no settings to control this and there is no reference in the manual. I've researched this on the Viotek customer service site FAQ. I've also reached out to Viotek customer service and it they never replied. Bottom line, this is a budget monitor, it is effective. Don't expect it to last long or have stellar support from Viotek. If you can live with that, then its a good budget choice. 3/11/2021 So just one day after leaving my last update on this monitor both DP inputs are dead. The HDMI still work (but for how long) and I will need to replace this monitor. Calling Viotek, they open at 9:30am EST, I've been unable to reach anyone and their VM is full so you cannot leave a message. I have a three year warranty on this and it was purchased less than 1 year ago. I've used their contact us on their website (the same method that I did several months ago with no response) so I'll see if they respond. I initially had this at FIVE Stars, lowered to it THREE stars yesterday and now they're down to TWO stars as of today. Again this is not a great purchase, if you're looking for reliability go for Samsung or another brand that will provide better support. Also I will upgrade this if they actually live up to their warranty agreement to resolve this.

I'll start with the TLDR: This mobo isn't worth the silicon wasted to create it. "New Company". Buyer beware! Ordered this to downsize old gaming rig to a small form mobo and move it into a much smaller case to use it for watching twitch/youtube while I game on my main pc. I've got a working i7 and 1600Mhz DDR 3 ram that I am transplanting onto this new mobo, which according to the displayed specs is valid. This starts off with me receiving an email this morning stating that they are a new start up and don't have a manual printed out, but attached is a copy of the manual. The attached jpgs (not PDFs) are of 2 pages of a manual that is horribly written and are almost incomprehensible and I've built a few dozen computers in the past 5 years alone. The motherboard is horribly labeled as well. The back panel port cover is not properly cut and does not fit properly into any case (I tried it in 3 different cases from different manufacturers) as well as the ports don't properly line up with the cover. After getting all of the parts installed I booted it up for the first test. It would start up for a second and then shut off. There are no POST LEDs, display panel, or POST speaker to give any sort of POST error codes. Of course without a manual the error codes would have been useless regardless. I took everything apart and put it back together again and I finally get to see the POST screen displayed and I get some post codes down at the bottom. The system then crashes. I boot it up again and it crashes on a different code. Being diligent I took everything apart and built it again and swapped around ram. Regardless of what I did, I would get a crash with a random POST code on the screen each time which indicates it's a mobo issue and not the other hardware. In the email with the "manual" they also indicated that they are a start up company and to not contact Amazon if there is an issue because Amazon will remove them from the market. This right here should have been my first huge red flag. I will be requesting a full refund from Amazon and will never buy from this company again.

I bought this for an off-label purpose: to fix an incompatibility between the Asus XT8 mesh router and Verizon's FiOs. The problem—which shows up in online rants, but doesn't seem to be acknowledged by either Verizon or Asus—is that the Asus router gets really slow upload speeds when used with FiOs. One workaround is to use Verizon's router, and to use the Asus mesh nodes in bridge mode—just to deliver wifi. People who didn't have their Verizon router anymore found that a cheap router from Amazon often worked just as well. Then some clever person discovered the problem was a missing feature in the Asus router: a protocol called "flow control," which seems to work as a kind of data traffic cop. Perhaps this is included in most cable modems, but not the Verizon ONT. So to work well with FiOs, a router needs this protocol built in. I then discovered that network switches (like this one) include an implementation of flow control. So I decided to try sticking it between the ONT and my router. This is not where a network switch is supposed to go, so I had low expectations. But for $17, why not try? Well, it worked. Download speeds are as fast as ever (about 3% faster than promised) and now upload speeds are equally fast. At least with a wired connection. Without the switch installed, they maxed out at about 1/3 this speed. By the way, I got the cheap version of this—5 ports and no configuration options. Just plug it in and let it do its thing. I don't believe there's any way to make use of the 3 remaining ports. If you were able to, they wouldn't be behind your router/firewall, so beware.

Review of Toshiba TF-55A810U21 55-inch Smart 4K UHD with Dolby Vision and DTS TruSurround TV - Fire TV Edition - Limited Version Purchase Date: 29 MAY 2020 Initial Review Date: 4 JUN 2020 Initial Impressions I had an older 49in TV which had a backlight failure, so I was looking for a TV of equal or slightly greater size. I found this TV on Amazon and took a shot on it. When it arrived, it was packaged quite well. I took it out of the box and plugged it in immediately after checking the screen with a flashlight for damage during shipment. The TV powered on and the screen was not broken; a good start. I mounted the TV (it includes the screws to do so and recommends an M6 screw on the back of the unit) and found out you cannot do this mounting on your own. I had to hold the TV while my son connected all the inputs into the back of it. This TV is bulky, weighing around 32lbs. I was afraid that I would break it trying to get it mounted. Thankfully, I didn’t. Once mounted, we turned on the TV and began the initial setup. I plugged in an ethernet cable into the back of the TV (Ethernet still provides more stability and speed than Wi-Fi) and waited as it updated twice. I signed into my Amazon account and then began exploring the picture quality of the TV Picture Quality My old set was a 1080p 49in TV without HDR. Even without 4k content, HDR makes a remarkable difference in the quality of the image, even in resolutions as low as 720p. Without seeing it in person it’s hard to adequately describe, but there is a sense of life in the image that wasn’t there prior. Not being familiar with it, I started to get a little motion sick; but once acclimated I began to appreciate just how much more detail HDR actually gives to an image; even in older movies. Certain elements in the foreground seem to pop out, making the image look almost three-dimensional. It’s a really neat effect which is enhanced even more when 4k content is played. Fire TV Software I’m not a fan of Fire TV, having owned an original device I found that it lacks storage and it doesn’t seem to have as much polish as its competitors. However, the implantation on this TV isn’t that awful. The TV itself has 4.27GB of storage with around 2.02GB available after installing a couple of apps (YouTube TV, Disney+, Hulu, Fandango Now, Netflix). I don’t have a terrestrial antenna hooked up to the TV so I cannot comment on those features but there is a channel guide that pulls its information from Pluto TV, which I thought was a pretty cool add; especially since Pluto TV is free to use. I’d like to see more integration sources such as YouTube TV or Sling, but Pluto TV has a lot of content in and of itself. The channel guide and other quick settings can be summoned by holding down on the home button. This works when playing content or when just at the main screen of the TV. I enabled CEC so that my other devices could control the TV, but I found out that my particular model of soundbar, connected to the optical port of the TV, is unable to be controlled by the TV remote. Bummer. I’m hoping that could be addressed in a future software update, but maybe my naïveté is showing. Conclusion This TV is an excellent value for the price. Its picture quality is astounding and the Fire TV software is neat, but not anything to write home about. I’m disappointed I can’t control my soundbar with the TV remote but the picture quality of the TV more than makes up for that shortcoming.

review_text: Overall, I think these are good headphones. I've learned over the few years as I've been getting into the headphone hustle that it's incredibly difficult to find a perfect headphone...the elusive "end-game"! To that end, these headphones aren't perfect, but they're a great choice if you're looking for a fun, relaxed sound that still has audiophile clarity and resolution. However, you may have to do some pad rolling, and the headband isn't for everyone. I decided to look at these headphones because I was in the market for a fun-sounding pair of headphones that had a u-shaped frequency response; I wanted to enjoy clear trebles in the presence of strong, impactful bass, but without sacrificing on the mids too much. I also wanted them to be well-built and comfortable. These headphones get me as close as I've managed to get to completing the quest! As part of this search, I've tried the Klipsch HP-3 (they sounded amazing, but the headband was way too loose for my head and it kept feeling like they wanted to off my head) and the Fostex TR-X00 Mahogany (these also sounded great, but the mids were a bit too recessed and the built quality is not great). Out of the box, the AH-D7200 sounded muddy and the bass was too overwhelming to me. This was despite burning in the headphones for about 50 hours. I decided to do some pad rolling with ZMF pads, and so I tried out the Universe lambskin, suede, and perforated lambskin pads. In that order, I found #1 sounded largely the same as the stock pads, #2 had just slightly too much bass and just not quite enough treble, and #3 had perfect bass but the treble was too bright. So, I've settled on the ZMF Universe suedes for now; as I listen to them more, I'm finding that I'm happy with this sound! I might eventually fiddle around with using some Dekoni attenuation rings (although the rings are sized for bigger pads, so I'll have to take some scissors to them), but at this point I'm happy. I'm not sure if it's appropriate, but I'd also call these headphones bass cannons; they seem to really show off for genres like hip hop, rap, and rock. Between these and the TR-X00, I prefer the better build quality of the Denon and substantially better resolution of the mids and trebles. I'm not sure why others haven't commented about the overwhelming bass with the stock pads. I just found that it overwhelmed everything else, and pad rolling was the only thing that tamed it down. The only thing that I don't like about the headphones is the headband. The leather is nice and it feels very cushioned, but the foam they use has bumps on it on the inside (hopefully you can see them in the picture), and those bumps (3 of them, by my count) press firmly on my head and I find that pressure pretty annoying. You eventually adjust to it, but it never feels great. This drive worked perfectly upon installation and I've had no problems with it in over 2 weeks. I'm using it for Time Machine backups via an external disk attachment on a 7 year old Mac. Time Machine runs about once an hour. However, I noticed that some reviewers are complaining about the noise on this drive and I want to use my IT professional background to give some insight into what might be going on for them so that others can make an informed decision on this drive. I have the 2 TB drive. I don't personally find this drive to be loud and it's running in an external disk drive enclosure. It runs about once an hour for however long Time Machine needs to run. When the drive is in use, it does make some noise, but it can't be heard at all outside of the room it's in. I sleep in the room next to where it lives and both rooms are always open and I've never had this drive make enough noise to be heard beyond maybe 7 feet from it and it can barely be heard at that distance. So why are some people complaining rather bitterly about how loud this drive is? First of all, it's an old school mechanical drive. It will make some noise when in use. That is the nature of these drives. And the more you use them and the more filled up they get, the more likely they are to make some noise on use. It is also possible that some drives off the manufacturing line are better than others, some are worse, and some of the people who complain just by bad luck got a noisy one. I don't find the noise I'm hearing to be unusual for this type of drive. I've heard a lot worse. Also, if someone is going to use this drive with a lot of file deletions and additions, it's going to make more noise. My suggestion for people who are extremely noise sensitive is to consider paying more and using SSDs instead. They won't make any noise. This drive has worked exactly as I intended it to work and I would recommend it to others. Again, please note that this is a mechanical drive and its lifespan is expected to be much lower than that of an equivalent SSD. You should probably think about replacing it after 3-4 years whereas for a 2 TB SSD, ,in theory you could get decades of heavy use before it goes bad. That's why SSDs cost more.
Regardless of the price, these work really well and have done for over a year. The signal range is great, audio quality is brilliant and the charge is decent.

If, like me, you've got a lot of crap to plug in, but not a lot of mains power outlets, this will serve you well. First the good: The 12 3-prong outlets in the different positions allow you to plug in all sorts of weirdly shaped wall warts without eating up too many adjacent outlets. The is the reason I got this, and the sheer number of outlets made it a very attractive option. I don't think I know of another manufacturer giving this flexibility. The meh… The USB ports are a bit of a nice addition, but they're 5V, so really only good for charging small things in a reasonable time, or larger battery capacities glacially. I wouldn't plug a modern phone into it if I didn't need to, but I would plug in a wireless mouse/keyboard to charge. Now, the bad… That power switch is the cheapest, dodgiest switch I've ever encountered on a product of a reputable manufacturer. I really don't know what they're thinking. Anker offers a good value, but spend the extra dime, and get a better on/off rocker. The other thing I don't care for, but it's purely personal, and YMMV. The verdict: If you've got a lot of stuff to plug in, and the plugs are all different shapes and sizes, this power strip is a dream.

I purchased the 2TB as extended memory for my PS4. It was extremely easy to set up and works flawlessly - I have not noticed any delays or issues playing games installed on the drive. I download most digital games directly to the drive and its just as fast as downloading to the PS4's internal memory. Its nice to not have to delete games when you want to play something else. So far, I'm quite happy with this and would recommend. If you are considering purchasing this for use with your PS4 gaming console, here are the installation instructions: 1) Plug in the external drive to PS4 USB port 2) Go to Settings > Devices > USB Storage 3) Select the external memory from menu and click X on the controller 4) Format as Extended Storage. That's it. The PS4 will format the drive and ask if you want to use the external drive for downloads. To move games or other applications from the internal memory to the external memory, follow these steps: 1) Settings > Storage > System Storage > Applications 2) Select the game/application you want to move, press the Options button on the controller then select Move to Extended Storage. At this point you will have the option to select multiple applications if desired. Then click Move. It may take several minutes depending on the size of the application to transfer it to the external drive. The application/game will still show up in any folders, etc so nothing really changes in terms of appearance or access to the game. You can access the external storage by going into Setting and selecting Storage - you'll see both the internal and external drives listed. Remember - if you want to remove the drive don't just unplug it (this is true for use on a computer as well). Go to Settings > Devices > USB Storage > select external drive then choose Stop Using this External Storage. I hope this helps anyone considering using this drive for the PS4. Again, so far its worked flawlessly and I would definitely recommend.

I'm writing this review after using it 8+ hours daily for over two weeks now for work and personal time. After using it for this amount of time, I have come to really dislike this headset and plan to return it. I'm leaving this review so that others can understand what some of the issues I find with it are so they don't make the same mistake. I mostly wanted a wireless headset for casual gaming/music and also be able to use it for Zoom calls for work. The flip to mute mic was a nice added bonus and these looked cute. On top of that, all the reviews I could find at the time are mostly positive so I gave them a try. For appearance, comfort and range of connection, I'd give it 5 stars. For utility and what it's supposed to be for: audio, I'd give it negative stars if I could. Pros: 1. Lightweight, comfortable, not bulky, audio quality is ok when it's on "headphone" mode 2. Gorgeous color, I got mine in pink. 3. Battery life. Charges quickly, can last 2 full days at least on one charge even if you use it all day. Cons: 1. Bluetooth only. This part I found to be a problem in all bluetooth-only headsets. What this means is, the headset actually has 2 modes/channels of audio: a high quality, output ONLY channel for stereo music, and a very low quality, voice call optimized input/output voice channel. The headset can auto toggle between between these channels automatically but what this means is that it cannot be on both channels at once. In other words, if you need the mic in any way shape or form (e.g. you're in a discord voice channel), it will FORCE you to be in the low quality sound. So if you want to listen to music or have good audio playing from a game at the same time, it won't work. Or you can have good audio, but everytime you need to use the mic, it mutes your audio. My only work around for this was to use it as only audio out and use a separate desk mic for input. 2. Really bad static on long meeting calls. Basically EVERY meeting that I've been in during these past two weeks that have lasted at least an hour, around the hour mark there starts to be static weaved in with any audio. Every time someone talks, every syllable of sound is accompanied by really bad static, and the static stops if the call is quiet. I basically have to restart my headset every time (and lose around 5-10s of audio from the call while I do this) and it'll be working good as new again. I read that this could occur if the device is low battery but my headset has never dipped below 60% battery on any of the occasions I've used it so I don't know what causes it. 3. Does not work with zoom after laptop goes to sleep and wakes up. I noticed at the end of the work day, if I do not shut my laptop down completely and restart it before next use, Zoom will stop playing the audio to this headset. Strangely it will play sounds from other parts of the computer and Zoom settings show the mic is "active" but it doesn't actually play anything unless I restart the computer completely. It's been highly annoying to have to shut down and do a fresh boot of my work laptop every day for this. 4. Auto shuts off if no audio detected for a period of time even if there is audio playing. So like most bluetooth devices, it will go to sleep if it thinks it's inactive for a while. Usually this is fine because if I'm listening to something on youtube or a music player it knows to stay connected even for hours at a time. However, for some specific applications, like Genshin for example, if Genshin is the ONLY source of audio playing (there's background music, and game characters talking), this headset thinks there's no audio so it will go to sleep for no reason every 15min or so and then I have to manually flick it back on, or I have to keep playing a youtube video in the background to keep it awake. First, this little unit works fine. Meets the HD requirements of all the devices plugged into it, and works quietly and effortlessly in the background, as it should. I'm not adding any pictures, because the ad itself, and the many pictures already posted pretty much tell you all you need to know. The one part I am disappointed with, and prevents me giving it 5 stars is the placement of the power port. The video output port, the one that is crucial to this devices operation, also happens to be on the same side as the as the power port. Not only are those two ports on the same side, the power port is to the rear of the HDMI output port. The natural routing of all the cables is to the rear of the device (As evidenced by the first 4 input ports being at the rear). And I understand using the sides for the additional ports to keep the device compact. But with the power port to the rear of the output port (The one that goes to the TV/monitor), you cannot use a right angle adapter to direct the output cable to the rear, and instead must now allow that cable to extend straight out the side while substantially increasing the amount of space used by this device. My recommendation would be to move the power port to either the rear of the device, or forward of either of the side HDMI ports. That way a right angle adapter can be used to keep the cable management tidy, while keeping the footprint small. For those questioning why allow the power port on the side at all? The power plug is much smaller than a HDMI plug, and the power wire is much more flexible, and therefore easier to route close to the device itself than an HDMI plug.

review_text: There's nothing more I can say about these speakers' sound quality that others reviews haven't captured. For speakers with this small profile, the audio is unquestionably 5-star quality. Especially paired with a subwoofer, they may be the best desktop/tabletop speaker set you can find. Unfortunately, the speakers are significantly marred by Vanatoo's decision to not include a power switch. Instead, Vanatoo intends the speakers to turn on automatically when audio is detected. Put simply, this doesn't work. Even when the speakers correctly detect audio output, there's a short (multi-second) lag in speaker activation. This means that, if you care about the beginning of a song or podcast, you'll need to start playing audio, wait a few seconds for the speakers to recognize it and turn on, then rewind and start over. That's a bit irritating, but it's manageable. The more frustrating issue is that the speakers frequently (even several times a day) fail to correctly detect audio output at all. In these cases, I have to reach around the back of the R speaker, unplug it, and plug it back in. I've been using them for over a year, I've tested multiple audio sources, and this problem has never varied. Would I purchase these again? Maybe. With a footprint that's perfectly suited for desktop use, the sound quality is just that good. And I love the look -- an issue of personal preference, but a big plus for something that becomes a constant part of your home office and/or gaming environment. But I'm disappointed that Vanatoo would ship such a poorly implemented feature as this set's auto-on, and I'm even more disappointed that they forced it on users by eliminating a traditional power switch. It's a baffling, user-hostile flaw in what's otherwise one of the best audio products I've tried. (The manual dip switches required for speaker configuration aren't user-friendly, either. I didn't reflect that interface irritation in my scoring, however, because you'll likely only need to adjust those once, maybe not at all.)

Read speeds: North of 140 Write speeds: Lower than 30 Side Note: While it says 1tb and appears to be less on your system. It's not a lie, it's just how computers are structured. People think 1000 bits (base 10) Computer see 1024 bits (base 8) The result, 976 bits is what you see in the end. review_text: Please also see by review of the Alcatel Link Hub 4G LTE router which I got to replace a landline and DSL service, but that unit was not satisfactory because it automatically turns itself off and did not have provisions for setting the TTL. Afterwards, the hotspot data speed was reduced to 3G or about 0.6 Mbps for the rest of the month. For me, this is not ideal but may be tolerable. However, there is another somewhat more expensive solution, Spectrum for coax cable internet access and free telephone and fax via Google Voice accessed by a Obihai OBi202 2-Port VoIP Phone Adapter. So I returned the Yeacomm router and plan to get Spectrum internet service and the Obihai adapter.

Yes it runs Android and it does connect to your TV so technically the seller isn't lying when they call this product an Android TV media streaming device. This product however is not an Official Certified Google ATV product and it matters for those of you trying to use this device to replace your cable co's STB (and others). THIS device will connect to the same Google Play Store that your tablet and mobile device connects to which means you will get Apps or App versions intended for touch screen tablets and mobile devices which makes for a horrible user experience on TV's when trying to use this device as your replacement STB if the App works at all. True Google ATV media appliances (which this device is NOT) and sticks will say Certified Google ATV product and they will connect to a version of Google Play designed for authentic Google Android TV products such as STB's (set top boxes), televisions and some Google ATV Sticks ensuring that your device gets the proper App and you get the experience you are expecting. If the App you want to run on your media streaming device to be connected directly to your TV comes from Hulu or your cable co or is made by Espial Elevate then this box will not work properly for you, instead you must get a Google ATV Certified device. There are only a few truly compliant devices on Amazon, the majority are like this box and completely useless that is unless you like your TV behaving like your touch screen tablet.

I've been using the display since April of 2020 so I've had plenty of time now to get used to it and give it a fair shake. Brightness: If you enable DyAc+ and leave it on, the brightness can be adjusted as high as 400+ nits. However, if you turn off DyAc+, then it drops to roughly 320 nits. I personally leave DyAc+ on all the time. 2D Picture Quality at 27": So a lot of people think they'll see pixelation at 1080p/27" and in my case I don't really notice it since I sit about 2 feet away from the monitor and i have it mounted on my wall. I previously had the 25" KD25F and found it too small for my liking so right now, this 27" hits the sweet spot. Remember, there is an 8 pixel per inch difference between 25" at 1080p vs 27" so all you have to do is move the 27" back a bit and you get the same view. 3D Gaming at 27": I got an FPS jump of >30% going from 1440p back to 1080p with this display which was nice. As soon as I started playing CoD: Warzone I noticed the input lag and motion was far better than my old Asus PG278Q which is a 1 ms TN panel but from 2014. With DyAc+ enabled and the ultra low input lag of this display, my K/D shifted upwards and I've been averaging 5-15 kills per match in Warzone since I bought this monitor. With my old Asus PG279Q, I had peaked and could feel the input lag. S Switch: Man what a handy little tool! I setup 2 profiles so far, one for desktop with the black equalizer set to 5 and vibrance set to 12 and DyAC turned off. When I want to game, I choose the other profile which turns DyAC to Premium while boosting vibrance and black equalizer. Very handy little tool that a lot of other manufacturers should think about copying. Colors/Sharpness: Out of the box they're a bit dull so I just set it to user define + standard and gamma at 3 and now it looks pretty good. I also had to increase the Sharpness to 8/10. You should download the color profile for this display and then calibrate it. Since it is a true 8 bit display with near 100% sRGB, you will get very nice colors from it that matches a lot of IPS displays. DyAc+: So this is the entire reason I bought this display, to have BFI that doesn't lose brightness when turned on. I can confirm that this monitor does not lose any brightness with DyAC enabled and infact gets MUCH BRIGHTER (up to ~480 nits peak) unlike every other competing display which tend to cut their brightness in half with BFI enabled. I briefly read about changing the vertical totals on these forums and since I likely won't hit 240 FPS even with a 9900k@5 Ghz and 2080 Ti in the games I play (Warzone/Apex Legends), I settled on 182 Hz with VT of 1350. I tested many different vertical total values out and 1350 just seemed to work best as the top/bottom of the screen had minimal blurring and the middle was great. It also works perfectly at 240 Hz with no VT adjustments needed. Additionally, you can enter the service menu of this display and calibrate the area/intensity using the UFO Ghost page found on blurbusters or their utility. I did this for my display by setting a custom area/intensity in the service menu and have virtually NO ghosting (see attached image of UFOs). Negatives: ------------ Yes there are unfortunately negatives with this display as there would be any display on the market. TN: Because this is a TN display, it will have limited viewing angles and you should be prepared to sit in front of the monitor with at least 1.5-2 feet distance between you and it. I have my monitor mounted and sit back about 2 feet from it which is ideal. Color: While the color is fantastic with it being a true 8 bit display, a lot of high end IPS have gone 10 bit and have better sRGB coverage than this one does so it doesn't match top tier IPS panels. If you want to do professional work, I would recommend having a separate IPS monitor for that or if you absolutely cannot afford two monitors, then buy an IPS monitor instead of this one. Overdrive: This monitor does not have dynamic overdrive which is unfortunate. What this means is if you lower your refresh rate, AMA (what Zowie calls their overdrive) only has 3 settings and so you end up with more double images at refresh rates below 240 Hz because the overdrive doesn't compensate. Some new displays (namely an AOC one) has dynamic overdrive which accounts for this and so you end up with no double images/ghosting while gaming at lower refresh rates. While not a deal breaker by any stretch, I would have loved to see Zowie include this. Price: Let's face it, this is an expensive panel for 1080p and being TN. $650 is asking a lot but if you are a serious gamer that wants the best technology, you gotta pay. Other panels offer similar performance but they lack DyAc+ which is the ultimate differentiator. I'd say if you don't care about DyAc+, then you could get a panel from say Asus that costs $200 less and will give similar performance--just be aware that Asus displays BFI is <200 nits which is pretty dark. That's it, hope you found this review helpful. If I had to, I'd buy this monitor all over again and am highly satisfied with my purchase and you will be too.

I was pretty enthusiastic about the recently introduced Arlo Ultra 2 Spotlight kit (2-cameras and a base). I thought this was finally going to be a security camera kit that I could comfortably use with my Apple TV 4K, iPhone, Mac and Windows computers. However, I returned the kit today after a disappointing 2-day experience with these security cameras, at least for the Apple HomeKit environment (which is why I bought them in the 1st place). Pros * 180-degree field-of-view is really marvelous (great color); fish eye correction is well done. * Night vision is really good (but resolution is a problem, see Cons) * Automated Spotlight for night vision motion triggers really helps - it triggers color to also be captured on recordings * Can be powered by battery for a while or with full-time wall power. My one camera went from 100% to 85% after two days of testing (my only data point there). * Can record locally to a SD-card * Relatively easy to mount / install * Web access to home cameras via Arlo login account is great (nearly real-time views, just a few seconds delay) * Camera and base setup can in theory be done from the Arlo website (once registered) * Snap on magnetic power connector is great (very secure and easy to attach to the bottom of the camera) Cons * Advertises as 4K pixel resolution, but I am nearly certain Arlo must be compressing the video so much that it looks *no better* than 1080P resolution (cannot clearly see faces or license plates that are 20' away from the camera) * Uncertain about how well the wireless works to the cameras; before I mounted my 1st camera, I found the video got unacceptably jerky on the recordings / Arlo website when I was only 25-30 feet away from the base unit (not anywhere close to the suggested 300 feet in their marketing materials). It seems to me in my limited experience, one might need a separate base unit for each camera (my application was one for front yard, and a second for the back yard) * Relatively weak documentation on how to setup the system (surprisingly). Some pictures were not as clear as they should have been (like where the "Sync" buttons are on the base and camera units) * Could not get one camera to pair *at all* with the Arlo base unit (after 5-visits to tech support, no luck). Tech support was not very helpful (perhaps 4+ hours spent on the phone with them). I suggested they send me a replacement camera, but they didn't want to do that (so their "boss" said) * After setting up zones to not trigger cars passing by the front of my house, or people walking by on the near-by sidewalk, I still got numerous warnings on my Apple Watch and iPhone (via Homekit). When I went to review the recorded videos, there were none! I suspect (?) Homekit alerts aren't being filtered by Arlo in their software as it was seemingly doing the right thing for not capturing video for people on the sidewalk or cars passing by, but my guess is that the zone marked motion alerts were still being passed on to Homekit (and thus to me). This happened many times during the 2-days I used the one camera that was working. Too many false-positives means no trust basically... * I seriously doubt the cameras running on battery would last the advertised "six months". I would guess no more than 10-20 days max based upon my limited experience. Make sure you get the 25' charging cable to charge your cameras; the included short power cable wouldn't have worked for me (and I suspect most people). * The kit I got included a magnetic base attachment unit for mounting the camera and a different unit for screwing the camera firmly into the mounting bracket (very stable). For mounting cameras outside, Arlo recommends the cameras be used with the mounting hardware that allows the camera to be firmly attached (screwed in) to the mounting base. The magnetic base is only usable IMO if the camera is over soft materials like a couch or carpeted areas as I almost dropped the camera off of the base (not very secure when holding on via magnets). I would have had to purchase another mounting bracket for outside *if* I had got the 2nd camera working (I never did). * I could not get any alerts on my Apple TV from the one camera that did work (I assumed alerts should have been displayed there). Never got far enough to get this resolved either. Maybe this is an Apple problem (not sure to be fair). * Unclear how secure the video streams at Arlo are (never got that far in my analysis). Arlo does not advertise if the video is encrypted or not (I assume it is not and would therefore not be considered private IMO) * Pay for recordings I recall was $9.99 per camera (not a very good price IMO after spending nearly $650 for the kit) * A post online reviewing the Arlo Ultra cameras suggested that if you disabled the pay for storage subscription on the Arlo website and opted to use local video storage to SD-card in the base, you wouldn't get any Apple Homekit alerts. If true, that would also be a deal breaker for me (what kind of security would that be without any motion alerts)? So, maybe for those that don't care about HomeKit, this might be a pretty good solution for home security, but for me, the negatives far outweighed the positives!

The idea of a solar panel powered camera with no extra wiring is wonderful. However, it does have its limitation compared to wired units. I have installed various brands of surveillance cameras over the past two decades in multiple households and decided to finally also give Reolink a chance. The pros: Setup of the camera is very easy and quick. Download the Reolink app, create account, turn on camera, follow voice prompts, scan QR code, setup WiFi credentials, setup new camera password and you are done. Mounting the camera was straight forward and allows to be either screwed into the wall or ceiling, or strapped around a tree, pole, etc. The Reolink video quality is very good for a low cost camera. Night vision image is very crisp. Battery seems to stay in the upper 90% the whole time during the day and night. However, can't speak on its lifetime over the years being exposed to warm and cold seasons just yet. Camera can record directly to microSD card (max 128GB) as well as cloud simultaneously. The microSD card recording is a big plus as it does not have to rely on currently working WiFi signal and works during power outages of course. The cons: The camera mount has no security to prevent thieves from stealing it within less than a minute as it is only screwed in by hand with no tools. Make sure it is mounted high enough where a person can't get to easily. At least other brands require to use tools with some having to remove the housing first to expose mounting screws. Detection & Recording - Because it is a battery driven camera, all motion detection is via the PIR sensor. There is no pre-recording time as seen with wire cameras and therefore any recording is a little delayed and only lasts up to a set time, with 30 seconds being the max after an event trigger. Cloud recording is limited even further, including for paid subscriptions. The detection area is questionable due to the PIR sensor use only. Even with 100% sensitivity setting, a lot of motion events (approx. 80% of them) are being missed. Luckily I have another camera mounted in that vicinity that is capturing all of the events. Overall, I might consider Reolink cameras for future purchased due to the picture quality and ease of use, but most likely will stay away from the battery powered versions due to detection and recording issues.

I'm pleased with this purchase. This seems to be a high-quality cable at a cheapy-cable price. It's thicker than any other USB cable I've ever used (and I've been using them since USB became a thing), and it has a ferrite core (that little barrel thing near the mini-USB end), the purpose of which is to reduce or eliminate EMI (electromagnetic interference) and RFI (radio frequency interference). I've only used this cable to say "check check, testing" into my Blue Yeti a few times so far, but the sound is beautifully clear with no hint of buzz or any other undesirable noise, and for a ten-foot-long USB cable that's snaking amongst a whole lot of other cables including AC cords, that's impressive. I think I'm going to buy a couple more before these cables get "discovered" and possibly go up in price and/or down in quality, as seems the fate of so very many products in our shamelessly (and often unethically) capitalist society. I highly recommend this cable for use with USB microphones (and for any other mini-USB applications).

Seller is falsely claiming 480MB/s data speeds. I tested these cables on a brand new Samsung T7 SSD with the Blackmagic disk speed test and found they don't even reach 1/10th of the claimed speed. For benchmarking I used the USB cable packaged with the T7 drive and got around 400MB/s. "Okay," you might argue, "but these are really just for charging. Stop complaining." Well then how about this: DON'T CLAIM DATA/SYNC SPEEDS THAT THE CABLES AREN'T CAPABLE OF. These are trash.

AAWireless Review I was excited when I received the AAWireless device. It is a lot smaller than I expected it to be. It's got a 6-in USB cable and the devices about the size of a box of blue tip matches. The setup was pretty straight forward and quick. I took the update and did a factory reset on the unit to make sure everything was fresh. My car is 2018 Honda Accord Hybrid and my phone is a Samsung 21 Ultra. This works perfectly when wired to the USB of the car, it responds as fast as I can talk to it and understands me about 99.999% of the time. I wanted the wireless feature so I could just jump in the car and drive and have these features. Once I married the phone to the AAwireless, it automatically starts up Android Auto on the phone and on the head unit. Pandora starts playing and Google Maps is displayed and I'm ready to go. On my first test run, someone called me. I press the answer button on the head unit and asked how I sounded. They said I sounded normal. I asked if I sounded tinny or did they hear any background noise. They said you sound normal. So the unit was performing well using the telephone option. Now I try to give it instructions. I say "Ok Google", to which I hear the chimes immediately. Then the problems start to become apparent. #1) it could not understand what I was saying. If I asked "what time is it?", it would show on the screen "where to sit". if I ask it "what's the temperature in Juneau Alaska", it would show me "i'll ask her". I was literally screaming commands. I noticed that if I turn the radio off and spoke very loudly and very clear, it would understand me correctly about 60% of the time. I found out it was not using the microphones inside the cabin of my car, but the microphone on the phone itself. So if I picked up the phone hold upside down (where you talk if you hold your phone to your head) and close to my mouth it would understand me clearly all the time. But what's the point of having wireless if you have to hold the phone in your hand? #2) something else I noticed was my heads up display was always dark. Sometimes it goes dark if I'm in a tunnel and there's little light on the outside or after sunset. But this was dark all the time for some reason. #3) driving around for 45 minutes or so, I noticed my battery on my phone dropped about 20%. I can understand why this is happening. The phone is communicating with a device wirelessly, communicating with the head unit Bluetooth,using internet data,and running applications. The phone is working tremendously hard. I don't think i could go on ride for 2 hours without the need of charging up my phone once I get to my destination. Although I do have the recharging pad / surface built into my console. I could rest the phone on there and have it charge up. I don't think it would charge faster than the battery was depleting energy. I tried every option and the application setup for the device, I tried different communication methods for the USB on the phone, i try a beta version of Android Auto,and I could not correct the microphone issue nor did it help the battery usage issues I'm not going to return this to Amazon. I think as the product matures I will give it another shot in the future. Right now its got too many flaws that are resolved by me just plugging in the phone with the usb cable I hope this information helps somebody

I had a new Avermedia Live Gamer 4K GC573 card but was having some minor problems with it. Comparisons of the Elgato 4K60 Pro to the Avermedia Live Gamer 4K GC573 seem to show both cards as pretty equal competitors. However I found that not to be true in the case of 3840x2160 60 frames per second capture (2160p60). I was upgrading from an Avermedia Live HD PCIe capture card. I am running a 4K monitor and was outputting the desktop HDMI through a gofanco Prophecy Intelligent 4K 60Hz downscaling splitter to feed the capture card 1080p video. I upgraded the capture card because I wanted the ability to both pass-through 4K video, eliminate the splitter, and improve the quality and resolution of the capture. I tried the Avermedia Live Gamer 4K card first but had some glitches with the resolutions and pass-through. Wanting to avoid any problems I decided to try the Elgato 4K60 Pro. THe Elgato claims supported capture resolutions up to 2160p60 (3840x2160 at 60hz) but when I tried to capture at that resolution I had an "encoding limit" error - the Elgato could simply not capture 2160p60 video on my machine. I tried both the Elgato 4K Capture Utilty and OBS with the same results - all the CPU cores would hit 100% and I would experience frame dropouts. The minimum requirements for the Elgato are listed as a Intel i7 CPU (i7-6XXX) or AMD Ryzen 7 or better. My capture PC has an i7-4790K CPU so technically I don't meet the minimum requirements. But CPU benchmarks show the i7-4790K having similar or better performance than for example an i7-6500U in most areas outside of power consumption (source: CPUBoss website). Given that I believe the i7-4790K should meet the minimum requirements for CPU for the Elgato (unless there is some other CPU enhancement in the i7-6xxx series that the i7-4790k lacks that is necessary). By comparison using the Avermedia capture utilty RECentral 4 the Avermedia Live Gamer 4K (GC573) was capable of capturing 2160p60 (albeit only using the YUY2 and NV12 decode formats). In addition I was able to capture 2160p60 on the Avermedia using OBS with the default video format capture of "Any". (OBS gives video format options as: Any, XRGB, NV12 or YUY2 and I was able to capture 2160p60 using all of them.) The Avermedia 4K minimum CPU is an i5-6XXX, so its requirements aren't as steep as the Elgato 4K card but I'd venture that 2160p60 capture on the Avermedia on an i5-6XXX is probably as unrealistic as the Elgato claim using an Intel i7 CPU (i7-6XXX). I found that the alleged 4K capture ability of either card appears only possible at higher than the minimum CPU requirements. Capture at lower resolutions with the Elgato worked fine and I didn't have any other problems with it in my testing. Overall I found that although the Elgato 4K60 Pro is comparable to the Avermedia Live Gamer 4K in most ways, its higher system requirements for capturing 2160p60 video mean it's inferior to the Avermedia 4K, especially at the same price.

I bought the DragonFly Black about a year ago for my mobile music production setup, as I wanted a high quality portable DAC for my mobile music-making setup. It outputs a very strong signal, and it gives a lot of power to my mixing headphones and portable monitors. HOWEVER, I've started noticing that the onboard DSP on this DAC will sometimes do what appears to be very aggressive peak limiting on the signal. I started noticing this when I was doing some drum sound design. Transients would sound muffled or they wouldn't even appear at all sometimes (pure impulses don't seem to want to come through). I A/B'd this with other usb DACs I had lying around, and confirmed that the issue was indeed confined to the device. I recorded the output of the DAC back into the system, and sure enough, the output waveform confirmed what I was hearing: the transient of my test signal was smashed by some process and then replaced with a fade-in attack, an instantly recognizable signature of some kind of compressor. I've attached the before and after photos. Furthermore, what is interesting is that the peak limiter will only kick on with peaks that are spaced far enough apart by relative silence. It seems to be that a peak from silence will "wake up" the limiter, and then take a few seconds of silence to go back to sleep. This peak limiting behavior is persistent on mid-2015 macbook pro, an m1 apple air, as well as a computer running Alpine Linux, so it safe to say that this is a firmware related problem. I also bought and tested the DragonFly Red, and it also applied the same peak limiting on my test signal. So far, I've only encountered this issue in music production related tasks, such as previewing drum samples and other short audio files. For more long-term music listening, this doesn't seem to happen. I've been trying to communicate with Tech support about this over the last few weeks, but so far it has been a slow and unhelpful process.

review_text: We have a little cabin we occasionally visit that is far from any internet/WiFi or any cell phone signal on a large piece of wooded property that is approx 20 acres. But family lives full-time on the property next door and they were more than happy to share their WiFi with us. Since we only visited the cabin a couple times a year we didn’t want to spend a fortune on a high end system and gave this one a shot. After about 1hr or studying the instructions, fidgeting with the settings and loosely placing the Bridges on window sills we couldn’t be more pleased. While I’m writing this review we’re streaming a movie & surfing the web while we wait out the bad weather outside. The instructions could be a bit better but I have a lot of experience with other bridges and setting up home networks and was able to figure it out. Couple pleasant surprises; 1) You DONT have to have your own access point plugged into the receiver unit, it actually has one built-in! I do wish it was easier to change its name and pw though as they are both ridiculously long. 2) The two bridges are very forgiving in their placement and automatically paired within 60 seconds of roughly pointing them at each other. I’ve had other wireless bridges that were better at being paper weights. But these are incredible, no drop outs and we only lost about 1/2 the speed of what the family gets in their house! …And that’s with me just leaning them in our windows, while going through several walls, a metal roof shop building full of tools and equipment and even a few trees!!! In other words - NOT a direct line of sight and still works great! Can’t wait to get them properly mounted, I’m sure the performance will only get better. Knowing that we didn’t have direct line of sight between transmitter bridge and receiver bridge I really didn’t expect this to work, but it does and without any fuss. Highly recommend! ***UPDATE*** Finally mounted the bridge properly on a pole. It works even better as I had suspected it would. Now we get only about 1mb/s less than what the host is getting straight from the internet provider. Extremely pleased!

I just picked this up to replace a Klipsch BT speaker I’ve used for over 10 years. Why do I own a BT speaker and how do I use it? I’m a photographer and knowing the model’s music preferences, and having a service like Apple Music or Spotify, allows me to play music during the shoot to help put them at ease and bring out a bit of rhythm to help with posing, especially flow posing. Carefully adjusting the playlist can help bring about desired body language and facial expressions. The sound isn’t great but it’s very, very good, with a prominent midrange and inoffensive treble with sufficient baritone and bass notes. It’s been tuned well for its size and should work well with most any genre of music. Despite being designed and advertised as “360 degree sound,” the tweeter is clearly front-biased while either a port or passive radiator is rear-biased. Listening to Duffy “Rockferry” and Caro Emerald “Deleted Scenes From the Cutting Room Floor” both sound great. I’m not ashamed to break this out for a studio portrait or conceptual art shoot. The buttons could be better labeled with the industry standard rather than proprietary choices, but once you figure it out, it’s fine. I don’t need the water resistance but it’s nice knowing it’s durable. The exterior of my Triple Black unit is delightfully understated. Battery life is serviceable… I’d expect a unit of this size to have at least double the advertised runtime, so a charging base is already in the shopping cart. The lack of USB-C quick charging, especially in this latest, version II release is a huge letdown. The inclusion of a 1/4”-20 thread in the base, the standard thread for photography, is a huge boon, especially for photographers and using while outdoors as it can easily be mounted on a tripod or light stand for better sound performance. Ultimately, it all comes back to sound. It’s far better balanced than the Beats Pill and is able to be played at full volume, unlike the Beats, of which the bass heavy tuning causes the full range drivers to rattle and flutter at full blast. While the Revolve II is clearly directionally biased, it’s not as bad as unidirectional speakers like the Beats Pill. I’m able to set this up on a tripod in the studio, connect Apple Music, set volume to half and never have to touch it again as the sound is delivered in all directions. For the price, it’s one of the better portable BT speakers available. If you need more volume and higher fidelity, I’d recommend the Plus version, as it is large enough to accept Bose’s signature tuning and does sound better overall. However, for my purposes, the non-Plus version fits perfectly in my camera bag, alongside my lenses, making it perfect for studio and on-location use. It’s the best collection of compromises for the price point and sounds almost as good as it looks. The sound is actually so mid-focused and clean, I’m considering buying a second one to use in stereo with my iMac, just plucking one off it’s charging base whenever I head out to the studio or location. If you want a $200 portable BT speaker, you’d be crazy to buy anything besides this, unless you’re an uncompromising bass head. If that’s the case, buy a Sony and avoid the Beats Pill.

I received my Zenbook UX534FTC-XH77 on 09/18/2020. Today is 09/25/2020, a week later. Overall, it is a pretty decent laptop. Royal blue color is very nice. So far, everything works. Although I am not impressed by the screen pad 2.0 and use it only in the traditional touch pad mode, I am quite happy with this laptop. However, by comparing to the Microsoft Surface Pro 4 that I own for almost 5 years, I found the following deficiencies of the Zenbook UX534FTC-XH77: 1) The main screen is not a touch screen. I used to be able to scroll up and down with my finger directly on the screen with my old Surface Pro 4, and now I cannot. 2) There is no num lock indicator. You can't tell whether the num lock is on or off. I went to Settings -> Ease of Access -> Keyboard and turned on the Use Toggle Keys to work around this deficiency. However, it is no replacement for a real fix. Also, scroll lock key and indicator are both missing. 3) There is only a back facing camera, but no front facing camera. I used to use my Surface Pro 4 to take pictures of objects or record events happening in front of me that is interesting. This is now not possible. 4) Touch pad is not centered to the main keyboard section. My Zenbook is 15.6" and therefore it has number pad at the right hand side of the main keyboard section. Touch pad is centered to the PC, not centered to the main keyboard section. It is so much to the right from the center of the main keyboard section that I accidentally touched the touch pad by my right palm several times and changed the cursor location while I was typing. In my opinion, totally centered to the main keyboard section may not be good either. Because it will make it hard to balance the laptop on your lap while you are typing. However, it should not be this much to the right from the center of the main keyboard section as it is now. 5) Screen resolution is only 1920x1080. My 5-year old Surface Pro 4 has 2736x1824. Consequently, all objects are big and the display can only show so many of the objects. Not only that, I can actualy tell that the objects are much less refined both in color and shape by the Zenbook than my 5-year old Surface Pro 4. I don't game. Without gaming, my old Surface Pro 4 with 2736x 1824 resolution did not give me any speed issue. This new Zenbook, with less resolution, did not show me any performance gain either. For my use, I would prefer to have a higher resolution. I can get 4K quality through the HDMI external display. But this is only practical when you are right in front of the home or office display, not when you are away working with the PC on your lap. I could use its passive features like basic drawing and interacting with the screen (just like you can with your finger because it's a touchscreen) but the pen wouldn't pair at all with the laptop or any of my other devices. I went through all the troubleshooting steps in the manual online and through every other troubleshooting info I could find after spending hours on Google searching for help. I made sure it wasn't a dead battery and that the laptop paired just fine with other bluetooth devices so, unfortunately, the pen was dead on arrival and the pen being included with the laptop was part of the value proposition of the device so where I would have given it four stars had the pen worked, I had to drop it down to three since that's $50 worth of defective product there. The laptop itself would work well for anyone who would never have to use it outdoors or in direct sunlight indoors as long as you keep the brightness at maximum all the time. Because of the low brightness and the defective pen, I have to give it three stars overall instead of the four it would have earned otherwise.

Update 11/14: I ended up buying a third one not long after posting this review and still stand by everything so far. Original: It looks like most all of the reviews up are from Vine reviews of a free product, or they're in French. So I figured I'd chime in a little, since I ended up buying a second one of these, and I'm contemplating a third. As a disclaimer: I don't use these for the actual portability aspect, but rather as small monitors on my desktop setup. I do not use them for any sort of professional work, and I cannot speak to their quality in that regard. I mostly use them for media, chrome, Spotify, etc. So truly accurate color reproduction isn't a massive point for me. I also haven't tried the speakers on them at all. The color quality has been fine for me in the few movies I've watched, and for my general browsing. With that said, I really like these a lot. The built in kickstand is great and I haven't had a single issue with it. The only real qualm I have is that the display inputs are on the side, and not a hub on the back. That seems to be common with this type of monitor, which makes sense portability wise, so it's not doing anything different. I'm using them differently than intended, technically. To hide the cable a bit I'm using 90 degree angled USBC connectors, with no issue. One of these is connected to my GPU via a single USBC cable, and the other through my onboard video via a single usb4 cable. A usb4 cable was required for video when connected to the motherboard usb4 port, USBC would not work. I have zero issues moving between them with my mouse, and notice no real ghosting/delay when doing so. I am not using these for gaming, and probably wouldn't recommend it unless it's something super casual, like an rpg. It's extremely light and easy to move around, if needed, which is great for the (intended) portability aspect. All in all I very much recommend these if you get it at the (regular) price of about $110. I've seen the price change a lot, but there's usually a coupon to clip. I probably wouldn't go over $120 though, but that's just me. If you're in need of a portable, lightweight monitor, or just small extra ones like I'm using them for, I don't think you can really go wrong with this one. I haven't had any issues yet, so I can't speak to customer service, but I'll update this review if it happens, and whether or not it's a positive, or negative experience. I did have one fall a couple of feet onto tile, and nothing broke. So, that's a last thought positive to throw in for the portability use of it.

But there is a software bug that when in this mode the calculator function doesn't work properly. I bought these to store large file for video editing when it's not practical to transfer them over the network. The first thing I found out is that they are pre-formatted with FAT32 which has a maximum file size of 4GB. I reformatted them as exFAT and the problem is solved. Performance is decent for the price. Sustained read speed is about 135MB/s. Sustained write speed is much slower at about 35MB/s. Burst write speed is around 65MB/s and I saw it maintain that speed for nearly 1GB before it dropped down to 35MB/s. These were measured using USB 3.2 Gen 1. I also had the opportunity to try this flash drive on a USB 2.0 port. Sustained read speed is about 38MB/s which is close to the limit of USB2.0. Burst write speed is about 22MB/s for about the first 1GB, then the sustained speed drops to about 17MB/s. I expected this to be around 35MB/s since the device can transfer data on USB2.0 at speeds of at least 38MB/s and it can write to it's Flash at speeds of at least 35MB/s. Something else I noticed is that while plugged into a USB2 port, the drive temperature doesn't increase, even when reading or writing for several minutes. However, when plugged into USB3 port for a few seconds, even when the drive is not being accessed at all, the drive gets fairly warm. It's not hot enough to burn your skin but it makes me think that leaving the drive plugged into to a USB3 port for extended periods of time (something I normally do) will shorten the life of the drive.

I'm going to start with the good news...this thing really performs. I upgraded from a Linksys AC1750 that was going on 5 or 6 years old. It had always been rock solid (not a single outage in all those years) but I had a feeling I wasn't get the speeds I should have been, boy was I correct. I recently upgraded my FIOS internet from a 100 to a 500 Gbps plan because I have two sons and both are now using tablets, etc. Plus I have a high end gaming PC and we have three TVs in the house streaming 4k, in addition to other devices. After the FIOS plan upgrade I ran a speed test from my PC and was getting about 340 gbps download and upload speeds. However, after I upgraded to this router...520 gbps download and upload! On top of that the range of the 5G network is way bigger than it was, probably triple the area. One of the other main reasons I wanted to upgrade to this router is so I have better coverage in my back yard in the summer. This thing covers my entire house and most of my yard - front and back. I am extremely happy with the performance. Now lets discuss the initial setup... First off, I got it done and it only took me a total of about 15 minutes. But there were some annoyances that I want to share with others. When you first start the setup and open the app it tells you to scan the QR code on the router. Mine didn't have any QR code on it. That was number 1. I checked the box too, no QR codes anywhere. So I had to do it manually. Not a big deal for me, however...when you select to do it manually in the app it takes you out of the app into your phone's settings to connect to the router network (NETGEAR** and the password is written on the bottom of the router). It also says that after you connect to go back into the Nighthawk app to continue setup. OK, so I connected to the router manually (which worked fine) but then wasn't able to go back into the app because the app was still directed to my phone's settings to connect to WIFI. Nothing was happening, so had to close everything and re-launch the app, which then started the process over again. Finally after 3 tries, the app recognized that I had connected to the router and continued with the setup process. Then, the router needed a firmware update. During that update I got an error message saying that it couldn't find the router, but the firmware update finished successfully anyway. Then I had to re-connect my phone to the router (again) manually to move to the final step in the setup. All in all the setup completed correctly but as you can see there were some hiccups. As stated it only took me 15 minutes or so but probably should have taken less than 5. I am being nick picky here but I remember setting up the Linksys router and it went very smoothly and quickly. Not really a big deal though and now that its done it never has to be done again. Given the performance I am getting from it, I don't really care. Hence the five star review. The only thing remaining is to find out how well this stays connected over the years. After how extremely well my Linksys performed I have very high expectations. We'll see...this review may change.

review_text: I've had this bag for 11 months of fairly heavy use as a business traveler. Pros and cons: Pros: -Great bag design as far as pockets, handles and holders -Looks good - got many compliments -Holds an amazing amount of stuff -Fits under the airplane seat in front of me perfectly for easy access to my stuff during flight -Zippers and seams have all held up well - no fraying -love the charging port for my battery pack -easy to carry, comfortale straps Cons: -Really only one. There are two metal rods around the top zipper that hold the bag's shape when it is open for loading. Those work great. But on this trip I noticed the bars are poking out of the material, creating a hazard. I was thinking plastic tips could be added to these to keep this from happening. I pulled the metal rods out to keep from poking someone's eye out when swinging the bag on my back. Turns out there are plastic tips on one end of the rods where the material is intact, but not on the other where they poked through. Still gave it four stars, although I think it should last longer, but it functions beautifully other than the metal rods and looks good.

The noise cancellation and transparency are also much better on these.However, that's where the praise ends. If these earbuds were around £100-£130 (like they should be) it would be a solid 5* review. The problem is they have a tendancy to be unstable, I've had several connection issues from brief pauses, to them deciding they want to take an hour off and just refuse to work until later. Currently, I have both in, the left one is on and can cycle through modes, but I only have music from the right. It's ridiculous. Thankfully this doesn't happen often. Also updating takes at least an hour, I'm not exaggerating.More importantly though, they're lacking loads of features which at this price point is a joke not to have. No multi-connect, no "find my buds", no modes by zone, wireless charging requires spending £50 on a case, these are all features which many cheaper earbuds have. There's no excuse for them not to be on here.If you want great audio quality and don't care about other features then I would highly recommend these, however since bose can't be bothered to acknowledge it's not 2015 anymore and actually modernize their features list, I'd really recommend looking at other products for now.

I bought this looking solely at the small form factor, manufacturer's name, and Amazon reviews. It appeared to be the best and most reliable 1TB backup solution for my PCs. I had considered a 1TB flash drive, but they were substantially more costly than this device. I've had it for several months now, and I can say it's been a good device. It's fast, holds a ton, and I can back up both my wife's PC as well as my own on it very quickly. It's a nice feeling being able to grab a tiny device like this in case of an emergency, and have everything on both PCs back up on them. It also has built-in encryption software, which updates itself periodically. Definitely a plus if you want to add a little privacy protection. But I failed to really consider the cable aspect. Sure, the device itself is super small, and fits in your pocket. But it's useless without the USB-C cable it comes with, so that pretty much has to stay with it. Together, it ends up taking up so much more space than other storage options, and it's very... awkward. This really offends my OCD, since there's really no way to make it neat and tidy (unless you buy a case, but that defeats the small form factor advantage). Although I still use it, I've decided to go with different media. If you don't mind the cable thing, or regularly leave USB-C cables on or around your PC, this is a very good device.

I bought this as a secondary monitor to get a little more pixel real estate as an upgrade from a 24" 1920x1080 monitor. For the most part, I am happy with it. I use this with a personal photo workstation and with my work computer for CAD-related activities. In both cases, this is a secondary monitor. The good: The screen is very bright, very crisp, it calibrated (via DisplayCal) very well and the gamut seemed to be near 100% sRGB. In terms of color rendition, it looks a lot better than the monitor it replaced. With comparing photos on it to my main 100% sRGB monitor, there is little-to-no perceptual difference. The screen is bright and the text crisp. No dead/stuck pixels. The indifferent: I don't use this monitor for gaming, so I can't comment here. There are no internal speakers (it uses a headphone jack). I can't talk about the stand because this is mounted to a monitor arm. The monitor was very easy to connect to the monitor arm and is very stable on it. The bad: This monitor, unlike the one it replaced, so not seem to auto-switch when one source is powered down, nor does it automatically switch to the "live" input if all sources are off and one turns on. i.e. if the monitor is set to use DisplayPort and every source input is turned off, if I turn on the HDMI source...it won't auto-switch to the HDMI source (or vice-versa). My old monitor would. Further, if I have both sources on and active but I'm using, say, the HDMI, then I power that source off--it won't automatically switch to the DisplayPort. This can be a problem because on startup it sometimes doesn't recognize the monitor. While this doesn't make me regret this monitor, it does get annoying. In conclusion I think if you're looking for a good, inexpensive 4k monitor that is 24" this is a good bet to get--especially if you're running it from a single input source. The color is good, the brightness is good, the monitor is crisp, and for the price it works well for photo editing, CAD, etc. Better for those uses is likely going to cost a lot more (as my main monitor was well over twice the price). I think if you can live with the lack of auto-switching and no internal speakers, this monitor should be on your list.
