I've had this watch for about 2 months now and I really like it. I've made a Pros and Cons list below of my opinions with this watch. Pros: -Time: It tells the time, as a watch should. -Background: You can customize the background to have it be a photo of your choice that you've taken. -Phone connect: I had no issues getting the app on my phone and connecting my watch to the app. -Water reminder: I have a reminder set to take a drink of water every 2 hours between the hours of 9am and 9pm, and I like that you can customize the reminders -Battery: AMAZING battery life. I charge my watch maybe once a week. -Water resistance: I wear my watch in the shower and have no issues with it. I had also done an event that involved me jumping into a lake and I kept my watch on with no problems following. When swimming, I will not use it as I'll be submerged in water and this watch is water RESISTANT, not water PROOF. -Incoming texts and calls: I can receive them with no issues and can dismiss calls with the button and quickly glace at the text if I'm unable to see my phone. -Steps: Gives a good read on my step count for the day. I like that it tells you when you were most active in the day and also that it gives you an average of your daily steps. -App: The app is great to use to look at your progress for the day and compare your day with other days. -Breathe: As someone with anxiety, it's nice to have this setting to help with breathing exercises. -Sport mode: There are several options of sport activities to use. -Find your phone: Great to have as I lose my phone all the time. -Brightness control: Great and easy to control. -Alarm clock: I have my alarm set to vibrate and it's subtle enough to wake me up without startling me. -Camera: Watch works great to take pictures with using your phone. -Call log: You can look at your recent calls and dial out without using your phone. -Strap: The strap is comfortable. -Raise your screen: Works great when you lift your hand to check the time or incoming text or call. It does go off when I'm not bothering with the watch at the time, but the screen is on only for a brief moment. -Comfort: 100%! Half the time I forget it's even there. Cons: -Accuracy: I don't believe this is accurate with calculating heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen, or sleep. There will be times where I'll be sleeping for the full night and my watch will tell me that I was "fully awake" at points throughout the night. It will also say that I have been "light sleep" in the mornings when I am awake and happen to be having coffee at the table. It will also tell me that my oxygen is at 90% when I have no respiratory issues to have my oxygen be so low. It will also give different readings in one sitting when checking my heart rate and blood pressure. -Time/Date layout with custom background: You cannot chose where the time and date will be placed when using a customized background, it only gives you 1 generic option. -Texts: You cannot text back to incoming messages on the watch. -GPS: All this does is tell you your location in the world using latitude and longitude coordinates. -The button: The only use I've found for this button is using as the "home" button. Why the button twists, I don't know what the point of that is when you have to scroll with your finger on the screen anyways. -Sport mode: I don't do a lot of the sports that are listed and I've found it to be inaccurate with my steps when I use the walking option. -Weather: Also not accurate. -Voice control: It says you can press the button for 3 seconds to activate your voice assistance, but what it actually does is either give you the SOS option or the option to shut the device off. -Swiping: Swiping up shows your recent text messages. Swiping down shows you a menu to access your watch layout, if the Bluetooth is connected, the brightness adjustment, and the watch information. Swiping to the left brings up your watch's application menu, but this can also be done with pressing the button. Swiping left is also like the "back button" to go back to the previous screen you were on. When you swipe to the left, it shows your recently used 4 apps that you've accessed with your watch. The SOS button is there as well. I would rather have the option to change where my watch goes when swiping left or right. -Games: Why? The screen is too tiny for this. -Strap: The strap is a bit big on me, even on the tightest loop, and I need to wear it below my wrist - this could contribute to the accuracy issues. Have not used: -Music: I don't want my music coming from my wrist, personal preference. -SOS: I haven't needed to use it, hopefully I won't need to, but I'm glad it's there. -Notification reminder with additional apps: I don't have notifications turned on for email or social media, as a personal preference. -Siri: I don't use Siri, personal preference. -Stopwatch: Haven't used yet. -Passcode: I don't use a passcode, personal preference. -Calculator: It's a calculator, basic, usually not needing my phone for math use. There's a lot more to the watch that's provided, which I think is great. I do enjoy it and I'm going to keep wearing it. There's the good, there's the downside, there's some annoyances, but no technology will be 100% perfect to your every need. This is still a great watch, especially for someone who's never had a smartwatch before.

I've only spent a little time trying to replace my current whole home wi-fi with this product, so I'm sure I will find much more delinquencies, but here are some issues I have found so far: You can not change the Wi-Fi channel They say that the router has intelligence that selects the band, but my router chose the busiest channel, and hasn’t changed it for over a week. All my neighbors are on the same channel, and I can’t do anything about it. * You can not set a port forwarding address You can only select an address from a list of CONNECTED devices. So the device has to be connected, and the software has to present the device, but the list of connected devices is not complete. * You can not reserve a range of IP addresses You can only select an IP address to reserve from a list of CONNECTED devices So the device has to be connected, and the software has to present the device, but the list of connected devices is not complete. * You can name a connected device, but then it forgets the names at random. They probably use the IP address to remember the device, but with DHCP, that IP address will change. They could have used the MAC address, but they apparently did not. And the deal breaker is this one: * You can not manage ports. You do not know what ports are open or closed, and even if you did know, you can not change it. You can fake an open port by using port forwarding, but only on ONE IP address. Even if you could forward the same port from more than one IP address, you would have to enter each port/IP address individually, and you are limited to 64 entries. If you have home automation, forget it. So if you have any software at all that requires you to open a port, and you want that software on more than one device, forget it. You simple can not do it. The port can only be forwarded from an IP address, not opened on the router itself like every other router I have ever seen. Just horrible.

I wanted to love this product and to start I did. The Garmin r-10 is beautiful looking all the way to the carrying case and the set up is extremely easy. The Garmin app that pairs with it is fantastic. I only used the Driving range feature and it's awesome how it shows you shot dispersion for all your shots, your metrics for individual shots and averages per club. It's also very cool how you can record video straight to the app through your phone and observe your swing with the data right beside it! The only problem is I found the data to be questionable. I tried it once in my backyard hitting into a net and 3 times at my local driving range. The distances in the backyard seemed to match up to my usual distances but of course I had no way of verifying those. So I took it to my local range. It seemed to worked fairly accurately with shorter clubs but began to give a lot of questionable carry distances for longer irons and longer clubs, at times 10 to 15 yards off what I could pretty plainly see with my eye. As someone who also has the tendency to pick the ball or hit up on the ball, I questioned also the accuracy of the attack angle readings (which are calculated based off the measured metrics). So I scoured the internet for reviews on its accuracy. Many golf blogs give it glowing reviews without giving it much rigorous testing. I found one "professional" reviewer with much more robust testing equipment than my naked eye, that seemed pretty critical of its spin measurements being off by the thousands. As someone who bought this to improve his swing and understand all these kinds of metrics for the first time, I feel the lack of confidence in the accuracy could derail and mislead my progress, as beautiful as the interface on the app is. Amazon accepted it as a return before 30 days which I respect and appreciate, though UPS had to pick it up at my home which made it a little trickier. For me $600 is a lot of money, and I would probably stop using it overtime if I doubted the accuracy too much. I wonder if anyone else here has questioned its accuracy. For me, I'll hope they come out with an R-20 or improvement down the road that I'll consider because as I said the app and interface and the promise of all these metrics at that price is very appealing!

Preface Let me start this review by giving you an idea of the experience I have with electronics and technology altogether. I spent five years in the Navy working on top secret electronics, which included radios, navigation equipment, multiple servers that served fourteen different pc’s, over a dozen antennas that fed through amplifier trays into receivers for pc’s to analyze. During this time I built a server at home and loaded up all my movies so that my coworkers could watch movies while on watch late at night (or whenever they wanted to slack off at work). I then went to work at an Intel fab, where I worked on giant equipment that uses chemicals to etch wafers. I built the web page that a fair amount of my fab uses to store and pass down information from shift to shift. I have built applications in multiple languages. I have a few apps on the Google play store. I built my own server at home that runs my own email server, a Plex media server, a DNS, and security camera server that takes streaming video from 6 cameras around my house. I think I’ve established that I’m not new to technology, troubleshooting, maintenance, or setting up devices. Review My wife and I bought this frame after comparing features from other brands of digital photo frames. The features that really appealed to us were cloud connectivity, no need for memory cards, no need for monthly subscription plans, the smart photo matchup, and the ability to play videos. This photo frame checked all of those boxes. My wife and I recently lost our daughter and planned to dedicate this frame to all of the memories we have with her. We received this photo frame and opened it immediately. I plugged it in and my wife started setting it up. After two or three initial attempts at connecting to wifi, we saw the connected message. I had my wife start adding photos, but as she was doing it, the frame disconnected from wifi. I assumed that maybe I had been too far from the router, the frame was going to go on a bookshelf that sits about 8 feet away from our router. I unplugged and took it around the area where we were going to end up displaying it. The connectivity issues continued. I rebooted my modem, my router, and the frame. I ended up factory resetting the frame and resetting it up, although this would later prove not to really make any difference. I somehow got it to connect again after several frame reboots. My wife added an album through the app and I was able to see a few photos, but now I saw ‘offline’ show up on the bottom of the pictures. She had spent over an hour looking through memories of our daughter, and this was a painful process for her. She hasn’t pushed herself to look through our albums until this photo frame came, because she wasn’t ready to deal with the emotions quite yet. Thanks for the extra deep pain Aura. I spent the next several hours troubleshooting this stupid frame. No combination of things would get it to completely work. It would load, at max, 5 photos that would loop. I was really annoyed by this. I have no issues with looking at FAQs and troubleshooting instructions from any company. I ran through all of Aura’s ‘fixes’ and nothing worked. Did I receive a faulty product? Most likely, but several other issues we ran into bother me about the whole product. My wife added videos and the app told her that videos weren’t supported. A video did display on our frame and did play. There is also a volume setting. The lack of attention to detail bothers me here. The level of quality control bothers me too. I know that it is possible for defective product to escape quality assurance, but if the issue is the hardware that is being used for the frame, then I don’t want to risk having a chip that works, but will go out right after the one year warranty ends. My total order price was $192.96 after tax. I have smart plugs that cost $10 and can maintain a better wifi connection than this photo frame. I wanted to setup this frame for my wife and I as we deal with grieving our ten year old daughter. Now, I get to return this frame just to do more research for another frame. I’ll order some other frame and it will take several more days to get here. I miss seeing my daughter’s face everyday and lousy quality control is making that gap longer. Do yourself a favor and look for a better product. I don’t order expensive products unless I do a lot of research, and I failed with this purchase. I would rather pay a subscription than deal with this kind of crap. If I would have bought this for a relative, especially an older one or one not so electronically inclined, they would have disowned me because of how troublesome it was. TL;DR I have a lot of experience with electronics… a lot! This frame met all the requirements my wife and I wanted for a digital photo frame. We wanted to dedicate it to our daughters memory. After hours of trying to make this thing work, I gave up. It was hopeless. Bad quality control means forever wondering how long a ‘functional’ unit will actually last. Save yourself the time and look elsewhere. There are other frames out there. I’m angry that I bought this. Don’t be like me, be happy, and look elsewhere.

A little background: I’m coming from a bug ridden 6 node Linksys Atlas Max 6E setup that I purchased last year. Review: I’ve only had my deco xe200 setup for about a week and so far the only slight negative I have is that I do not get close to the full internet speed like I did on the Linksys, but with how easy this deco xe200 is to setup and how well the signal penetrates walls compared to my previous Linksys Atlas Max 6E system, I end up not minding the slower speed as the Linksys constantly had issues and working with Linksys just ended up with me returning all my units for a refund as the issue would not even be resolved by their engineers. The Linksys had more advanced features that are not available on the deco xe200 such as manually setting the channel of each Wi-Fi band and the channel width, but most people would not need/touch these settings, but also a lot of issues came with those advanced features. The deco xe200 mesh router has been a great replacement with no issues so far. My current deco xe200 setup consist of four nodes that provide the same Wi-Fi coverage as the 6 Linksys nodes that I previously had. I will need more time with the tp-link deco xe200 before I can give a more thorough review. Negatives: This mesh system cost a pretty penny. Mesh node is pretty big. The image made me think it would be smaller but this negative is more on preference. Each node only have 3 Ethernet ports (1 10gigabit and 2 gigabit), this is only a negative if you need more gigabit ports and can be remedied by purchasing a switch. Not getting full internet speed (‘getting around 300-350mbps vs the Linksys I was getting 430-480mbps from my 500mbps internet plan) Positives: Wi-Fi coverage is great and is able to punch through walls with no issue. Status light can be set on a schedule to turn off at night in case a node is placed in a bedroom. Easy setup and configuration. Has a built in separate IOT 2.4ghz wifi SSID for smart home devices. Phone application is user friendly. Notifications when new devices connect to network. 10gigabit wan/lan port which helps to futureproof the mesh system for future upgrades to internet speeds. Would I recommend? I would recommend this mesh system If you are looking for a futureproof Wi-Fi mesh system that is consumer friendly and/or plan to build up a smart house with many IOT devices. If you are looking for a more cost effective route, to-link has a more affordable wifi 6E mesh system they sell that would do just the job.

TL;DR- This projector suffers from some of the worse LED blue color shift I've seen, and cannot be rebalanced to produce accurate colors. You will spend hours trying to find a balance for the blown-out colors without losing details in the shadows due to the lack of brightness until you give up, set it back to default, and resign it to a projector for multiplayer gaming and Netflix tv binging where you can force yourself to overlook the issues. I waited a few weeks before I reviewed this in the hopes that I would come around to it. I've always been a fan of projectors on a budget, and I've owned my share of them over the years. When my last projector suffered a part failure that cost more than this projector, it was time to shop. Based on some early youtube recommendations (trust paid promotions are your peril, clearly), I was drawn to GooDee and this projector. I'll break the rest of this into it's big three categories: Picture: I've been wary of LED projectors due to their notorious blue tint, but they have made advancements in the last few years and every review I could find, at the time, suggested this was far less of a problem on this model. When I received it, I noticed immediately that this was not the case. This projector skewed hard blue and was presenting primary colors shifted towards their blue mixes as a result. After spending an awful amount of time in the color tiny menu (which yields little to no customization after numerous experiments with completely emptying or maxing a color) and display settings menu, I found no mix and match allowed for saturated colors, accurate reproduction, and details in shadow. A requirement of mitigating the hard-blue shift it to lower the brightness to a 40 setting or less (out of 100). The side effect of this is all detail in dark colors and shadows completely disappearing due to the dim output of the bulb at that point. With my hands completely tied, I deemed this to be incompatible with watching movies, and have been annoyed by the magenta red jerseys, and blue-green fields while watching sports. Adding insult to injury, thought common in this class and hard to knock at this price point, the focus is so soft at the edges when the center is correct that this cannot be recommended as a work place projector, rendering its abundant brightness even more useless. This soft focus will also become more evident while gaming, where HUD objects are generally on the edges where the focus is the furthest out. Device: I find it hard to complain about the form factor of this projector. It’s relatively light, though not ridiculously so. It’s relatively quiet, though not silent by any stretch. The focus wheel feels fine, though a bit touchy. All in all, I have no complaints about the physical device when not discussing its function. It’s a solid enough built projector, and the included bag is nice. Sound: This projector includes speakers, and though I had no desire to use them long term, they were used for several hours during testing. If you’re looking for a relatively portable projector to play youtube videos or Netflix shows, the sound is perfectly adequate. In a small bedroom, it’d probably be fine for most uses. However, in any normal sized room the speaker housing will begin to vibrate and peak if you push the volume towards the upper 3rd. Overall: Though there are things to like about this product, and I really want to like it, at the end of the day it’s a projector and has to be judged on what it projects. The lack of color fidelity (look at any other of the photos already attached to other reviews, the blue isn’t from their cameras), the questionable color controls, and soft focus make this a pass. Even GooDee’s own 620 traditional projector seems a better option than this model. Pass on their LED offerings.

review_text: I tried out this drive with a 90 gig set of files ranging from .5 to 5 gigs in size. I was not controlling for background activity, so take this information with a grain of salt. First and foremost, please subscribe to my YouTube channel at transformational gaming. You can also hit me up on Twitter @transform_gamer if you want to discuss any of my reviews. There's good and bad about SR5014. Let's start with the bad. The app is not all that impressive. Difficult to connect to the Marantz AV receiver, the application is somewhat plain looking and is a little clunky. But that's about it when it comes to negativity about this receiver. Outside of that, this av receiver is probably the best 7.2 channel receiver out right now given the price of 999. You can say other things like not having an a way to spread vocals to the front as opposed to the center channel in surround mode. It sounds really stupid but I hear that Denon has the same problem. And Gene from audioholics has been protesting this problem, so I hope at some point they make a compromise. But, with a 4 volt output on the preouts, the SR5014 has some serious pop. My previous AV receiver was a the Onkyo RC260. So, I just wanted a receiver with preouts. When I bought this, I was amazed by the difference in quality. The preouts that went to the my powered subwoofer have noticeable clarity. The surrounds have definition and each channel just have a real punch. Maybe I had a poor receiver to begin with, with the RC260, but now I feel like I can enjoy my front stage without immediately going out and purchasing an external amplifier. I have not experienced equipment failure like the others have reviewed with this receiver. But, I must say that for those who are not Atmos guys, (this receiver can do Atmos btw) this receiver provides a great 5.2 surround solution in bi-amp mode. There are so many configurations. You will have the pleasure setting up your receiver for the coveted sweet spot. Also, another quality that was so refreshing was the EQ setting for each channel. I've been looking for an av receiver that has an EQ for years since the middle 90s. And, I can play with and EQ each channel? Man - I am just so flattered with this receiver. Great product. I may step up to 11.x in the future, but I'm just not interested in having that many channels to manage. Seem like that would be a nightmare. And how much content has 5 channels mixed in its content, let alone 11. Okay up mix is a thing... but how much accuracy is in that processing? Okay, this is a review, so I'll get back on track. If you are good with 7 channels, get this receiver. Marantz is the best. I'll be definitely looking to purchase my next av receiver from Marantz.

From the strongest point to the mildest point: PROS: - This is *ideal* for transportation with its very thin shape. This part is 5 stars. One advantage is that it is easy to slide even when the table surface is rough or sticky. - When fully charged, the battery lasts for more than a week, perhaps two, under full office use. - The silent clicks feel comfortable. I'm not sure it's the silence that is pleasant, more than the feel itself. CONS: - *Critical*: The mouse does not systematically hold when you hold down the left button. I'm surprised not to see this criticism in the other reviews. Is this because it's only my own mouse that is like that ? This makes dragging screen objects completely unreliable. When the hold fails, the object is released in the middle of the course and falls in random parts of your computer windows. When you do that to drag text, then the piece of text you are moving finds itself inserted in the middle of a random word or sentence. Every time, the only resort is Ctrl-Z when it is available. It's very annoying. This is the main reason why I'm only giving 3 stars. - There is no LED light to warn you in advance that the battery is about to be empty. There is no LED light to tell you when the mouse if fully charged. There are various LED lights but the manual does not explain their roles. - For the mouse to last for more than one week, it seems that you need to charge it for 24 hours. It could be less, but again, there is no LED light to tell you how long. - The bottom surface of the mouse is not even, which makes the mouse wobbly on a flat surface. As a result, the mouse feels "cheap", which is eventually a reflection of its price. NEUTRAL: - When the mouse is in sleep mode, and you wake it up by pressing one of the buttons, it takes about one second for the cursor to appear. So during that time, don't start moving the mouse to see where the cursor is, because in this process, you end up losing track of where the cursor could have gone. Overall, I don't regret my purchase for its price and for my intended secondary use of this mouse.

review_text: This system works well for some devices. We have certain devices that support both 2.4 and 5 Ghz (802.11n) but eero will lock them onto 5 Ghz with no internet connection. Customer service can move the devices to 2.4 Ghz where they will work again. This will last for a limited time. The only user solution is to pause 5 Ghz for 10 minutes via the app. After 10 minutes, eero will simply move the device back onto 5 Ghz and freeze the connection again. Now you have to spend and hour on the phone with customer service again... **Update to 4 stars. I had to dig deeper into the issue and learn more about network adapters. Eero tech support should've known how to fix this issue but they didn't. My network adapter is actually dual band 802.11ac & 802.11n as well as 802.11a/b/g. In the network adapter's advanced settings, I found a setting for 802.11ac vs 802.11n and a setting for every combination of 802.11a, 802.11b, and 802.11g. These 3 are the older wifi versions and 802.11a is 5GHz while the other 2 are 2.4 GHz. My default setting was 802.11a/b/g. By playing with these settings I was able to determine that it is 802.11a that locks up eero on 5 GHz. Since changing this setting to 802.11b/g I haven't had any issues. Hopefully, this helps anyone else who may be experiencing this issue as well.

I will update this after some actual field use. The inReach Mini was well packaged with the optional charging items. Set up, activation and initial testing of the unit was extremely easy and straightforward. The device is very small, but feels substantial and very good quality. It looks like it should stand up to typical use, and some abuse quite well. The Garmin Explore website makes it easy to set up your 3 preset messages. The Earthmate App (I use an Android phone) makes syncing the device and using many of the features very easy. The app is intuitive and easy to navigate and use. The Explore website also has other functionality and is also easy to understand and navigate. Please note that for the mini, firmware updates need to be done with Garmin Express. If you don't already have it, it's a free download. I connected the mini and within 2 minutes the update was installed. All other syncing functions like waypoint updates, messages, etc., are done from your mobile device when you connect to the mini via Bluetooth. Even without a mobile device, the mini is completely functional, and scrolling through and selecting the various functions is easily accomplished. You can send messages without a mobile device, though it will be a bit more cumbersome than using your phone. It's nice that you don't absolutely need a functioning phone though, in case there is a situation where your phone is damaged and you need to communicate or send an SOS. I was surprised how quickly the GPS acquired a fix when first turned on, and how quickly messages were sent and received. I realize that depending on location, topography etc., that messages may not always be quite as quick, but my initial impressions are extremely positive. My wife and I spend a lot of time, mostly fishing, in areas with no cell coverage. I will update this review after some use in the field. We camp in some areas that are steep canyons. I am anxious to see how long it takes for messages to send with a limited view of the sky. For those considering one of these it might be helpful to know how the messaging works. To me, it seems best set up to send a preset message once you are off grid. You can have 3 different messages, each with their own (and different if you choose), contact list. You can send an unlimited amount of preset messages each month as they don't count against your allotted messages. The way my wife and I plan to use the device is to send a preset message that basically says we are off grid, and to reply if something important comes up. All your recipients have to do is reply to your message and you will receive it. If you choose, each message can also contain a link to your location. If a recipient clicks on it they will see precisely where you were when you sent the message. Obviously if they reply, the reply and any messages exchanged will count against your monthly allotment. My initial impression is extremely positive and I am happy to have this device.

These were a great solution for covering about 100ft of ethernet cable from the modem to the office. A couple tips, though: i didn't use any of the connector pieces, they're bulky and ruin the streamlined look entirely. Simply cut a couple of the track covers so you can stagger them like bricks. The cover being over 2 track bases holds them together just fine without a clunky joint piece. Second, I screwed mine in, as that's one of the mounting options. But I didn't use the screws and anchors included in the kit. They're obviously cheap and the screws are not suited well to the task. I used lath screws, as the extra wide heads are perfect for screwing into flat surfaces, and the screw teeth are wide enough apart that they work well in drywall so no anchors were required. But after reading the other reviews, I can tell you that if you try to use the fasteners provided and have to futz around with a bunch of poorly designed connection joints, you're going to have a bad time and an unsightly installation.

I was looking for a simple watch and was intrigued by this product with the heart monitoring. So, I thought I'd give it a try. This watch has self-care apps and corresponding hardware such as blood oxygen sensor, and pulse... It also includes a skin temperature sensor and another sensor on the side that somehow measures heart health (The feature is called Arty). What does this watch do well? This is a simple health and exercise tracker which provides some smartwatch features without loading it down with connectivity hardware that eats battery....like wifi and GPS and cellular connectivity. As long as you have bluetooth connection with your phone, you get simple..and I repeat simple notifications from some apps... text, email, facebook. 1) The pedometer is pretty much right on. 2) The measurement of pulse ox, sleep, and exercise measuring throughout the day works well. The breathing app relaxes me. 3) The battery life appears to be as advertised. I've been using it for 9 days and there is 17% of the battery left. 4) The price of $100 puts it right in line with similar watches from other companies. I think the addition of the Tic suite of health apps makes this a better value than the others. 5) Even though the Arty feature is poorly documented, it gives you an idea of where you are with your heart health.. cheaper than going to get an EKG. (this is NOT a valid substitution for getting medical care if you feel you need it. I am NOT a medical professional. Annual physicals are encouraged!). 6) I love the weather at a glance feature. Updating is dependent on an active bluetooth connection with the phone. Here are the negatives... 1) The user interface is a bit clunky. I'm used to the smooth Wear OS experience. Finger swipes on the screen aren't as smooth as they could be in my opinion. This is especially true in the app drawer. 2) The notifications from your phone could be improved. Text notifications come in multiple copies and broken up into pieces. So, a three sentence text might show on the watch as 5 or 6 different notifications with no logical order. Also, only notifications from select apps appear on the watch 3) The distance for walks or runs is not very accurate. I tracked a 0.6 mile run wearing both the GTH watch and my Ticwatch GPS Pro. The GTH watch said I went a mile. I realize it is approximating my distance based on the number of steps... BUT there does not seem to be a way to calibrate the distance per step. Apparently it uses the GPS on your phone if it is connected via bluetooth. Otherwise it uses the steps and what it thinks your stride is based on height and weight. 4) The Arty feature (only retail watch in the world with this technology), practically speaking, is spotty at best. After some research, it would seem that the developer of the technology (ATCOR) has worked with Mobvoi to get the technology to market for the average consumer. The algorithms used in the software are said to be the same as what the medical community uses to characterize heart health. ATCOR claims to have published 1600 peer-reviewed publications on its technology. I really don't know what the outputs mean about my heart health. It is not consistent. Most of the time it's right on with my age... 40-50. I just measured it now and it says my ArtyAge is 16-20. But sometimes it says my heart age is 20-30. One time it said 70-80... Gee thanks. This may be based on variability in how hard I push against the sensor on the side of the watch. I don't know. This is the feature that differentiates the watch from the competition.. It should come with better directions. 5) The three letters "GPS" appear in the title for this watch on Amazon. This watch does NOT have GPS. Per Mobvoi customer service, it uses your phones GPS when it is connected via bluetooth.

review_text: These Sena units have some really nice features: the intercom is fantastic and this company is literally the only one that gave a moment's thought to charging ... you don't have to remove these speakers to charge them—that's worth the price of these units alone. The long-enough flexible cord makes it easy to route around the back of a helmet, sound is decent, volume is decent, and bluetooth pairing was a breeze. That being said, I don't know what they are measuring with their dimensions. According to their website: the Speaker drive unit=32 mm - thickness 4.4 mm ... Nope. The speaker measurements are approx 55mm in diameter (not including the antenna bump on the left speaker AND not including the adaptor for the microphone—which adds another 15mm to the width). The right speaker (+/-) is 17mm thick and the left speaker is 16mm thick ... that's roughly .6" and .7" thick. Which makes them among the thickest in-helmet speakers available. What I don't like: Too thick (hurt my ears after a short time), (+/-) buttons are very hard to press even without gloves on, and the prompts to let you know the intercom is connected or volume is maxxed out is insanely loud. If on-hill communication is paramount—for families and ski instructors/coaches, these units are a solid choice.

review_text: So, the device I order was refurbished, which is fine and I knew about prior to ordering. However, I didn't know that the previous owners' network information would still be on the device and I would have to do a factory reset to get the device working with my router. This information would have saved me so much time if I had known prior to trying to set up the device. I was following the instructions provided in the box, but they were not working because of the previous network being still active on the device. I had never set one of these systems up and was going in circles trying to figure out why the network it was showing me was not my own. It finally occurred to me that the device wasn't factory reset prior to sending it me, and that it was password-protected with someone else's network and password. After I Googled how to reset the device, everything else went smoothly. Seems obvious in hindsight, but even my tech-savvy husband didn't figure this out while helping me. Anyhow, during the initial confusion where I was trying to get to the Netgear website to unlock the device, I decided to call the hotline provided by the website's chat feature. This felt unsafe immediately. There was a ton of background noise of many people talking in the background, everyone was speaking with a foreign accent which I have great difficulty understanding because of my hearing issues, and then they asked me to go to a webpage that my browser flagged as "unsafe" and was showing the page as unload-able as well. After asking me to go to another page that seemed suspicious, I hung up on them as my gut was telling me not to give them any more info or go to any weird webpages that won't load and get flagged as 'unsafe'. They MAY have been legit, but it sure felt shady. I thankfully figured out the factory reset after this, since I was determined to not call them back. And like I mentioned, it was smooth sailing after this. If I hadn't figured this out myself, I would have returned the device as not working.

I bought this camera to monitor our pool water level while travelling. It is installed upside-down in a window frame with the camera lens about 1.5 inches from the window glass, and set to flip the video 180 degrees. It works well in daylight. The 6 foot+ cord is long enough to reach a power outlet below the window while having the cord following the window frame (instead of just dropped straight down over the glass), and Google included a flat wall plug for the USB cord. I'm happy enough with the camera that I won't be replacing it. There are several things that, together, made me at least consider returning it though. 1. The camera will only rotate video 0 or 180 degrees. That means you cannot mount it on the side of something and have the video rotate 90 or 270 degrees. This seems like a silly software limitation that Google should correct. At some point. Hopefully. 2. Mounted close a window, night vision is totally useless. That's because the infrared transmitter to assist with night vision reflects off the window, making the video appear completely gray at night. As my intended use is to monitor water level in my pool, this is only annoying. If my intended use was to monitor an exterior door thru a window, this camera would be a no-go. 2a. Humorously, the camera interprets reflections in the window, and if it decides it's a person it issues a person alert. So we get "people alerts" from the pool camera when people move around inside the house. 3. The video has about a 165 degree field of view, and it is clear when not zoomed. You can zoom the video but it becomes pixelated pretty quickly. Don't use this camera expecting to look at small details that are 20-30 feet away. 4. This camera DOES NOT work with the Nest app. At least they tell you this on the web site, so I knew it before buying the camera. Fortunately my Nest doorbell and my Nest thermostat also work with the Google Home app, so I've almost abandoned my Nest app. I say "almost" because I haven't had time to figure out how to get my Nest Aware subscription activated in the Google Home app yet. It wasn't obvious during setup.

I took the reviews of this product with a grain of salt because Carplay is naturally finicky. In my 2020 Civic, it behaves normally about ~90% of the time. Introducing a hacky way to get wireless Carplay is obviously going to kneecap the reliability, but how much? I decided to gamble on this thing to find out. Setup on day-1 was pretty straight forward. I did have issues initially pairing my phone because I was within range of my home wifi network. Evidently the iPhone is too stupid to let go of a known network during the pairing process. This can be remedied by simply forgetting your home network (or since you're in your car anyway, drive like 300 feet away -- out of the range of your network -- and then do the setup process). After I got it initially paired, it took the ~90% range down to what I would say is 70%. The biggest issues I had were the device not showing up at all on cold-boot and the audio had what I would describe as "buffer" issues... There would be short, quick bursts of audio dropping out/popping. It was fairly passable, but it was immediately noticable because wired Carplay did not do this. On rare occasions it would get super strange where the connectivity was slow/erratic and so was the audio. Sometimes skipping a few tracks would clear it up, but other times it'd stay a garbled mess until I got annoyed and unplugged it. I tried tampering with the various settings behind the scenes to improve the usability. You can configure parameters (and update the firmware) by connecting your iPhone to Carplay and then navigating to 192.168.50.2 in Safari/Firefox/Chrome/whatever. I found that the "check for firmware updates" button sometimes requires a few taps to actually register that there is one available. (if it says "no updates available" just tap it a few more times and it may find one). After much tweaking, I landed on the following settings: Audio delay: 1250ms (higher number will cause more touch/screen delay, lower can cause audio issues) Boot delay: 10s (anything lower and the device would sometimes not get picked up during a cold start. Even with 10s, it sometimes still didn't get picked up) I ran the device for about 2 weeks and would wager it worked as-expected about 80% of the time with these tweaked settings, which honestly, was fine... I guess. But then it just stopped working. Completely dead. QC on something like this is probably not incredible so I wasn't particularly surprised... but when it came time to send it back I just opted for my money back. Not worth it, imo.

I wanted to use a pair of wireless Bluetooth headphones (https://amzn.to/3lKFySg) with my computer, so I bought this Bluetooth adapter. This adapter supposedly uses Bluetooth 5, the version which minimizes audio latency, so that when you watch videos, the audio and video will be synchronized. Unfortunately, the adapter I received did not work properly. There was significant lag between the audio and video, and the audio would frequently cut out for a few seconds at a time. I suspect the one I got may not actually be Bluetooth 5. While in Windows Settings the device is called "Bluetooth 5," if you inspect the device driver details, it shows a Bluetooth 4 device driver file name (see the screenshot). Incidentally, you have to use a driver provided by the manufacturer, not a standard driver available from Windows Update or Realtek, the company that makes the Bluetooth chips. With the same computer and headphones, I was able to get perfectly synchronized audio and video using another adapter (https://amzn.to/3npdqod). It's more expensive, but I suppose this is a case where you get what you pay for. Bottom line - if you want to use your Bluetooth headphones to watch video, do NOT get this adapter. I can't even recommend it for audio only use, due to the intermittent connection loss. UPDATE: Seller was very aggressive, contacting me multiple times following my review, offering cash in increasing amounts to take down my review. I contacted Amazon about this shady practice, but this product and seller remains active, while my review disappeared from the product page despite being rated very helpful. Do not buy this adapter. Instead, spend just a couple bucks more and get the Asus 5.0 BT dongle (https://amzn.to/3PY2o8V) - it worked out of the box for me. No need to download uncertified drivers from suspicious websites.

review_text: I bought this router because I'm currently upgrading my home network. For background, I am working on an IT-related degree and I have some experience with this kind of equipment. I have A+ and Net+ certifications. I build computers and have been the family IT guy for over 20 years. Opening Box: When I got the router I was surprised by how small it is. It seems well-built but not necessarily sturdy. It came with a power cable. Installation: I separately purchase CAT6 and CAT6A cables to attach the router to a modem, access point, and switch. Everything connected well and I was able to mount it to a wall plate I created to hold all of my networking equipment. If you want to use POE you'll need to get a power injector. I bought one to power my access point. Configuration: Here's where things got difficult. This router has ALL the options. It was overwhelming to someone like me. I had watched multiple YouTube videos in preparation for configuring this device but the software had changed enough to throw off my plans to go crazy and try everything out. I ended up setting up a basic configuration and firewall. I just didn't have time to hunt down videos and scroll through forums to find instructions for the things I felt like doing. At some point, I plan to go back and do more. Overall, getting the basic configuration done was pretty easy. I just wish MikroTik provided more user-friendly instructions/videos to help someone like me get things rolling. It would really help with device familiarization, which would make those jumps into more advanced configurations easier. Conclusion: Overall, this is a great device and for the price, it has amazing versatility. The only reason I knocked off a star is I really believe MikroTik should provide more for people who need assistance figuring out configuration. This router is somewhat marketed to a SOHO user and not everyone is capable of this level of configuration without putting a lot of time into research.

With so many devices needing an Internet connection now a days, a loss of connectivity can turn a smart home into a dumb home really quick. Unfortunately my cable modem likes to randomly lock up every few weeks and the only way to get it working again is to reboot it by pulling the plug. Normally it’s not that big of an issue, but recently it happened on the second day of a week-long trip. Luckily I had family not far away that was able to access my house and reboot it for me, but that’s not always the case and I kept thinking there has to be a better way. I was very happy when I found this switch which does more than I even thought possible. In a nutshell, what this device does is it pings a number of sites, if none of the sites respond it will power cycle the outlets. This MSN switch has a great deal of configuration settings that allow you to customize exactly how it works. You can configure which sites it pings, how long it waits between pings, how long it waits for the ping to respond, how many failed pings in a row it requires before it will power cycling the outlets, which outlets to power cycle, and so much more. While it comes out of the box preconfigured, you can easily change the settings to your liking via its embedded web server. By default it is only remotely accessible from within your local network, but it is easy to set it up to be accessible from the Internet as well by creating an account on the cloud4uis website. This allows remote access from either the website or from an app. I had found some other devices similar to this that have a single outlet, but as I have a more complicated setup with multiple routers acting as access points I wanted to be able to control more than one device. Unfortunately those extra routers sometimes prevent my modem from starting up correctly so I have the modem plugged into the first outlet and an inexpensive network switch plugged into the second outlet. I have the MSN switch configured so that it waits 20 seconds before turning on the modem and waits 2 minutes before turning on the network switch, giving the modem time to start up before it starts receiving traffic from other devices. I also have the MSN switch plugged into a UPS, so if the power goes out everything will continue to run for a bit as long as it’s not a long outage. While the embedded web server gives you full control, the app and website are missing a few setting found in the embedded web server. Unfortunately it is lacking two things I'd like to know while I am remote: Connection Status and Event Log. These only seem to be available when connected to the switch locally and are not visible via the app or the website. Other than that I’d say this device is nearly perfect. Update: With so many configuration settings, unfortunately it's a little too easy to configure it incorrectly. My Internet went out overnight and the MSNswitch correctly detected it and power cycled my modem. Unfortunately the modem didn't come up correctly, and while the MSNswitch detected no access it did not attempt another power cycle. When I checked the settings I noticed I had "Force UIS Reset after initial power-on" set to Disable. I believe without this enabled it won't attempt another power cycle unless it has successfully connected after it powered on the modem. This setting is a little confusing as it's listed in Advanced Settings, separate from Timeout Settings which has a number of settings related to resets. Update: While this works just fine when I manually turn it off or on, it never resets when the internet is down. I've played with the settings numerous times, and I believe I have it configured correctly. My modem just crashed, rebooted itself, but didn't come up correctly. The Internet light went out and the Cloud Link light just continually flashed, but after 10 minutes it still hadn't power cycled anything. Finally I ended up pulling the plug on the modem and plugged it back in. Everything came back up and the lights returned to solid green. What happened? I don't know. No emails were sent and when I logged in to the MSNSwitch and looked at the logs it's as if nothing happened. The logs ONLY log when the switches turn off or on. It doesn't log if the connection was lost or anything other than the switches changing state.

review_text: I’ve had a Ring alarm system for almost four years and the experience has been great, but my one complaint from the very beginning is they didn’t offer a glass break sensor. As anyone with any security system experience knows, this is an integral part of a complete system. After waiting impatiently for years, I was thrilled to find out they finally released one. I received it within 48 hours of ordering it and was eager to set it up and test it out. For those of you looking for specs, here they are: Detection Range: 25 feet Suggested Mounting height: 7 feet off the ground and higher Size Across: Approximately 3.75 inches Weight: Approximately 5.7 ounces Just like all the other Ring alarm sensors, it was packaged nicely and included directions, batteries and mounting screws. The set up was also just like all of their other sensors. The app guided me though the set up and even provided a video. The most difficult part for me was removing the plastic battery tab. It was stuck and I had to remove the sensor from its mounting base to get it to come lose. The sensor can be set to work in three different modes: Home, Away and it can even be set to work when the system is disarmed. Although it will detect the sound of glass breaking while the system is unarmed, it will NOT notify the central station in this mode. It does however send a notification through the app. Having it detect glass breaking while the system is unarmed requires you to turn off battery saver mode, which can be found under “Mode Settings”. I have no idea how much faster this will deplete the batteries. Further testing will be required to determine that. For right now I decided to set mine up and just place it on top of a shelf between two windows. I set it on the very top, which was approximately 6 feet 2 inches off the floor. I then turned off battery saver mode and kept the device in view in the app. For sound detection testing purposes, I have the advantage of being a drummer. For testing I used a 15-inch Wuhan china cymbal. For those of you unfamiliar, these sound very much like breaking glass. I placed the cymbal approximately 18 feet from the glass break detector and hit it in such a way as to mimic the volume that I believe a shattering window would make (I know I know, it’s not very scientific). The detector immediately detected the sound and sent a notification through the app to my phone. SUCCESS!! Had the system been in Home or Away mode, it would have notified the central monitoring station. So clearly I’m very happy with this product and its performance, but I do have some feedback for the Ring team: The batteries that are included are basic alkaline AAs. Every other device I have ever purchased from Ring came with lithium ions, which are known to last much longer. It seems they cheeped out a little when it comes to this sensor. For the price I paid for the glass break detector, I don’t think including lithium ions are too much to ask for. After these run out, I’ll be replacing them with Energizer lithium ions. My second suggestion would be to allow this sensor to be programmed to alert the monitoring station when the system is disarmed. A great deal of home break-ins occur during the day. Having this added layer of protection 24/7 would definitely be a serious bonus for any home owner, especially to the highly vulnerable and those living in crime ridden areas. My third and final suggestion is, it would be very helpful if Ring could somehow provide an official testing method. A certified sound clip or tool would be immensely helpful and would prevent people from resorting to random and sometimes ridiculous testing methods (such as hammering broken glass to death). For now, I’ve given this product a four-star rating. If I have any issue with it, or if Ring does any improvements to it, I will consider adjusting that rating accordingly. Lastly, I want to clear up a few misnomers about this product. Another review stated this product needs a “hub” to work. I have absolutely no idea what they are referring to. If you have the Ring alarm base station, then this item will work with no additional item(s) needed. If this reviewer bought this without a Ring alarm base station and thought it would work, then they obviously didn’t read the description. That’s their fault and not the fault of this device or the Ring team. Another repeat statement I have read a lot is that these are too sensitive and false all the time. This is a glass break detector, and therefore is designed to detect sound. Yes, a very specific wavelength, but with that said, the placement of this should be well thought out. If you place this in a kitchen with a tile floor, there is a higher probability you will receive false alarms every time you clatter silverware, dishes glasses and drop anything metallic or glass on the floor. If you place this in a room with a loud stereo or surround sound system, you’re going to receive false alarms. If you place this in a music room with a drum set, you’re going to get false alarms every time someone crashes on a cymbal. This isn’t specific to the Ring glass break sensor. All glass break sensors are prone to this. Give careful consideration about the placement and the programming modes you want this to arm in. Keep in mind you can program this to only arm when the system is in Away mode. If you have more than one throughout your house, you can also program some to arm in both Home and Away mode and others to only arm when in Away mode. If your home or business in noisy 24/7, this may not be the best addition to your security system. There seems to be a lot of confusion about when this will trip the alarm and notify the central monitoring station, and when it will only send an alert to your device via the Ring app. I have already covered this, but will restate it. It can be programmed to trip the alarm and notify the central station in Home and Away modes. It can also be programmed when the system if off (not in Home or Away mode) to send a notification to your device through the Ring app. This can be done by turning off the battery saver mode, which can be found under “Mode Settings”. Turning off the battery saver mode will NOT affect how the device performs when the system is in the Home or Away mode. I hope this review and all the additional information I have put in to it helps others to make an informed decision when it comes to this glass break sensor. As I stated earlier, I’m happy with this item and plan to order several more to add to my security system.

review_text: To think these used to come free with iPhones and now they’re being chucked out at £19 is a bit annoying but having decided to revert to basics so I can enjoy Apple Music lossless it was money well spent.I actually wear them in opposite ears, right in left, left in right and they fit better, are no longer loose and sound fantastic with highs, mids and lows very discernible.As with all Apple products, they just work but there’s a way to make them sound even better via your iPhone.1: go into settings access the music tab and if on, turn off the EQ2: ensure you have the Apple health app open and then download the Mimi hearing test from the App Store.3: performance the hearing test and screenshot the result to your photos.4: go into settings, find the accessibility tab, open it and then open audio & visual within the accessibility tab.5: turn on Headphone Accommodations and then hit custom audio setup6: you'll be asked to use audiogram, select yes and then download the photo you saved from the hearing test and your phone will analyse it and customise your audio accord to the results of the test.It’s all very clever but the difference it makes is beyond belief and has turned what were already a great set of buds into a fantastic sounding set of budsOne final tip, I also turned the sound check in the music tab off and despite many expects claiming having it on makes no difference, to my unatuned ears, turning it off in conjunction with the actions above also made a difference to the sound.You can thank me later.

I have a bunch of laptops from very basic no-frills models, to heavy-duty gaming laptops with high end NVIDIA chips and lots of video memory. I bought this laptop so I could work while traveling without lugging around any more weight than necessary. "Work" for me means connecting to my office network, running basic MS Office apps (Word, Excel, Outlook and PowerPoint) and doing Internet searches. No video production or processing. I found the culprit to be these galaxy buds. The lithium battery had expanded and melted my charger and ruined the galaxy buds. The charger had gotten so hot that the insulation surround the cable melted and fused the charger and buds case together, ruining both, all this happening while my family was sleeping a few feet away. This is a fire hazard and very well could have damaged more than just the charger and buds. The troubles with this product don't stop there. review_text: I initially gave this 5 stars because the speaker by itself is amazing. I changed the review once I realized I can’t connect reliably to other UE speakers which is why I bought this speaker and several other megabooms for the backyard and patio. Once the hyperboom is connected to other UE speakers through the UE app the system deteriorated. The much promoted party-up feature creates a very unstable system in regards to connectivity. The Bluetooth connection drops incessantly, music is glitchy, and the speakers randomly disconnect and turn off completely. I am fairly tech savvy and followed all the instructions for getting party up to work, constantly disconnecting and reconnecting the speakers from Bluetooth and each other, resetting the speakers, and following all directions on line. I even did “forget device” on phone and reconnected every device several times like they were out of the box. All software is up to date as well. There was no interference. Distance of source to speakers was 10-20ft, well within their claimed 150 ft range/ One afternoon I had to reconnect the speakers to each other through party up 8x. For the price of the speaker AND other speakers this is very unreliable and UE needs to work on their software and connectivity. If you want this as a single speaker then it’s awesome, but $400 is a lot for a single portable speaker. If you want this for an integrated UE wireless Bluetooth system then I’m sorry to say this won’t work and look elsewhere. I know Bluetooth isn’t always so reliable, but I’ve had many other integrated Bluetooth speakers I use outdoors for much less money and they work better. If you want one amazing portable wireless Bluetooth speaker and don’t mind spending $400 you’ll probably be happy but don’t expect much from party up. FYI every party up video shows all the speakers right next to each other. Who puts 5 speakers right next to each other? Once spread out, anything will interfere with the connectivity between all of them.

It comes with all the cords you would need, which is a nice touch. The RGB lighting, while a nice touch, is pretty underwhelming, but to be honest, I would have paid the same for this monitor even if it didn't have the lighting. The stand is beefy and pretty stylish, but it does take a lot of space on my desk, which I understand, because this is a heavy monitor. There is no power brick, so that is nice. At first, I didn't care much for the buttons on the back of the monitor, but after about 10 minutes of playing with it, it's pretty easy to navigate the menus. I had no dead pixel issues, and the brightness was more than adequate in my somewhat light room. The pre-settings for different games is nice and saves some time making adjustments. I also hate buying a monitor that has built in speakers because I don't want some crappy monitor-speakers and it's a waste, so I was happy to see that this doesn't include speakers. So far, I have played COD: Modern Warfare, Star Wars Fallen Order ,and world of warcraft and all of them look amazing. I honestly don't have any complaints other than I wish there were more than 2 usb ports, but that is all I could come up with. Another review stated that you have to make sure to switch the monitor settings to extreme to get the refresh rate to where you want it to get the benefits of the monitor, but that was very easy to do through the monitor buttons/menus. Overall, I am very happy with this purchase and if you have the money, you should pick one up.

Design is terrible, requires opening the plastic shell and cutting out plastic dividers. The board is designed to not use them, as there is no separation space for wide RGB plugs, while the case includes dividers that literally blocks you from plugging in your cables. So to install any RGB, you must remove the case and cut out all the dividers from the case, not to mention shaving off the edges, because the RGB pins are LOWER than the fan pins, and you have to cut out enough clearance to make the plug fit. You can buy the board without a case for like $10. Cooler Master took this board, put a logo on it, and covered it with a non functional case for over double the price. If it didn't have any dividers, the case would be fine, as it is nice to have a cover and magnetic attachment. No idea if it gets hot inside the case though. This board is a questionable design with questionable quality. The RGB input uses a 3 pin to 2 pin adapter, making me question how this is legit. Even if you didn't need the full 3 pins, the board should use it anyway for cable compatibility. This product is installed in a system I am in the process of building. I have no idea of how well it works or longevity until the PC is built. It may be better to just buy the no case $10 board that uses sticky tape. There also seems to be cheaper cased versions with functional case design that even come with remotes. Those are $5 cheaper than cooler master. So I honestly can't recommend this product, even if it works, aside from the looks and magnet, because you have to cut out plastic to plug in your cables.

My review is based on photos above water, not underwater. I took all photos on a sunny day at Lake Tahoe. Best results are in DIRECT sunlight (do not face your back to the sun) and keep your face up towards the sunlight, not straight on. Otherwise the shadow cast by your features will darken your face. If you're not facing the sun, you just look like a dark silhouette. 1/50 shots turned out completely useless/black. It cost $32.90 to get 50 shots processed into prints + CDs at Walgreens. It took about a week to process them, because they had to ship them to a state with lower regulations (supposedly, processing these photos involves chemicals too dangerous for California). I loved about 75% of the photos we took, the others were just not taken in optimal lighting. The photos are no where near as crisp as what you would get on an Iphone (later generations). But it is a great alternative for preserving memories without the cost of destroying a $1000 phone or camera in water. I am planning on putting them in a photo album. We hardly ever take pictures on our phones because we're hardly on them when we're together and we are camera shy. This gave us a good excuse to take pictures and save our memories. I would recommend it for people with a similar situation. Also, this gave me serious nostalgia to when I was younger and my mom would capture everything on these disposables. We have probably some 30 packs of just developed photos from these disposable cameras. :) They are so fun to look back on. And there's something about being on limited film and each shot mattering. Nothing like current phones, where all the screenshots and multiple takes flood up the camera roll.

I've only had the computer for 3 days so this is about setting it up, not how it works. It arrived in a factory-sealed box so it obviously hadn't been opened. Its contents included the TC-895, keyboard, and mouse, as advertised. There was also a 6-inch cable labeled Serial ATA, the usual very-small-print warranty, FCC and EU Declaration of Conformity that included info on power management and a page with what appears to be drawings of what needs to be plugged in, and flyer titled, "Got a Question About Your New Acer Device? Ask Us!" Usually these days a new electronic device of any complexity has a poster-size or foldout series of illustrations and instructions on initial setup, and in the case of a PC a well as a photo or drawing showing labeling the types of ports or plugins on the front and back. If you want anything more you go to the website and download a PDF users manual. So I thought I'd see if maybe it was missing and there was one online. I was easily able to find the proper Acer support page. There I found the Users Manual but no Setup Guide. The users manual said nothing about initial setup. BUT, it referenced the Startup Guide/Poster that doesn't exist either in the box or under my computer model's online documentation list. The hour was late but I decided to chat with Amazon tech support. Abdul was helpful in that he told be what the ATA cable was for (in case I wanted to add a component) but could find nothing about set up. He did offer to set up a return, however, if I wanted to send it back. I declined. Next I called Acer support. I was quickly connected with a representative who had no more luck than Abdul at Amazon. Trying to be ever so helpful he offered to walk me through the setup process. By then it was almost 10 pm and I'm not a night owl so thanked him and said I'd call back. The next day I decided to just plug it all in and see how I did. It went well. By Day 2 I was able to identify the front and back ports (some of which had microscopically small symbols beside them). I was unaware until now that there are 3 types of USB connections. The bottom line is that Acer should have some simple documentation packed with its computers. It would save a lot of time and frustration for those of us who aren't tech wizards. Now I just hope the thing continues to work.

review_text: One of the first things I needed to do with this is to transfer my existing, full, 1TB WD MyCloud (5-6 years old) contents over to this. I routinely get full gigabit to the WD MyCloud despite its age, for reading and writing. (90MB/s or more). The model Buffalo I have is a single disk 4TB model. My WD MyCloud is a single disk 1TB, I figured they would basically be identical in performance, but with more space. Doesn't seem to be the case. Contemplating gutting the mycloud and hacking a larger drive in to it. The Buffalo is on the same network, same switch, same batch of ethernet cables - and it tops out at 30MB/s for all transfers. It has a gigabit ethernet port, is connected at gigabit link speed - but something, either the processor/RAM or disk inside severely bottlenecks transfer speed and it seems to hard limit at about 30MB/s. The transfer from NAS to NAS is up to over 24 hours at this point, and if I push anything else to the drive, I'll see both transfers halve their speed to about 15MB/s while running concurrently. I've benchmarked and tried files that are friendly for network transfers (single large zip files for example) and nothing more than 30MB/s. So, it works for storage, I now have lots of space for the random stuff that I need all over the network in my home (gigabit ethernet drops in every room). But for speed? It's severely lacking. Again, no idea what the bottleneck is, currently assuming it's a weakness of the 800 Mhz processor and 256 megs of RAM. Not the best choice if multiple users will be hitting it for anything more than basic document storage. I'm betting that streaming HD video from it (4k lossless) would probably choke it, or be limited to a single stream. User interface is nice. Setup was super easy. Adding an extra 2TB external hard disk was supported (via USB, but 2.0... blech) with no issues. Shame about the performance.

They need 3, maybe 4, watches but somehow they keep adding more and more and more to the point that there are maybe three dozen options. This is really silly and makes it difficult for the layman to understand what he should be buying. Anyway, even the smaller version of this watch is hilariously bulky. They make the claim of something like 14 days battery life--not even close. Apparently it's 12-14 days if you disable all features. Even for basic running mine drains pretty easily getting closer to one week battery life. I thought that all this extra tech would be an improvement over the 4S or whatever super cheap basic Garmin I had--nope! When traveling long distances the watch still gets confused for the first activity, just the same as cheaper Garmins, and will muddle or lose the majority of the GPS portion of an activity. The HR monitoring is more-or-less identical to cheaper models. If you are using a foot pod and want to design a custom UI... this screen is tiny. Even with power-pace-time-distance I need to really inspect it to see what's going on since the screen is relatively small and there's no way to actually fine tune font sizes or anything. I'm sure there are some cool features here but with this price tag you had better be sure that you're going to use them. As a premium running watch it's a disappointment.

**Update** 2 weeks in dropped rating to 2 stars So the timings don't work as others have said here. I just tried to give my daughter more time and it just wouldn't work at all. So in the end I just bypassed circle by using the random mac address feature in windows. My daughter is only 10 years old and she's still nice enough to ask for extra time. However I'd actually be a little disappointed if by 12 she isn't bypassing this herself. Don't buy unless you have really obedient kids. This won't enforce anything and will actually cause you more headaches than it will solve. **original review** So yes it does what it says on the tin, "Kind of" I was already using OpenDNS which is pretty much exactly what Circle is doing under the hood , DNS ARP poisoning which means acting as the name server for your devices and then forwarding the requests on after applying rules. If you already have a way of doing this either via , OpenDNS/Cisco Umbrella , a Fing Box or an Ad sinkhole like PiHole then don't bother with Circle as it's no better than any of those and way more expensive. I have all of the above devices and services so this is a fairly informed review. I gave it 3 stars as there are major issues which are easy fixes however I believe the devs have been lazy. Firstly the biggest issue is the HSTS issues. So Circle will just display a cert error instead of a customer error page like Circle does on Netflix routers with Circle built in. They see a request for a https cert so they can at this point redirect to a custom page when a block is about to happen however they just the request fail to an ugly someone is trying to hack you page provided by chrome. Then the whole issue around timing , if you set up times for blocks then the are all screwed. Their FAQ states that it comes from the phones settings however my device is set to PST and the blocks are happening at GMT/UTC. And you can't just change the times in the app no you have to totally delete your account and set it up again and hope that their bug doesn't take effect again. For a simple DNS sinkhole it's not worth it and I would recommend people buy either a PiHole for about $30 which will also block all ads on your network which is something that Circle doesn't do. Or a Fing Box. giving us the options to import block lists would be useful as then we could also block advertising networks etc. So for what it is a really basic DNS blocker which is overpriced I'll rate it at only 3 stars and that's being generous. BY the way the app only has 2 settings Add people and add devices that's it , For people you can add times for when apps can be used. however again super basic. This device is made for mom and pops who are not technical at all and need a really basic way to prevent their kids from getting online. Note it won't prevent any tech savvy kids as they will easily bypass it.

I have a very mixed review. I bought this as a player to listen to audiobooks, I have more than 650, and my iPod does not have enough space to store all of them. Yes I know this exceeds the "music" function's ability to access files, but my homework indicated that I would still be able to us it. The Good - feel of the player in my hand, is nice. The buttons are all solid and easy to use, function of each is very simple. Sound is good, I have not compared the sound of the same files over different devices, so take it for what it's worth. I did use a high quality set of head phones. A 256 mini SD card is supported and all the files can be read by the player. From the perspective of listening to MP3 files there is nothing wrong with this player, it works and works pretty well. The Bad - these are all software (firmware) issues. I did my homework before I purchased this, so I knew before I bought it that the "music" function would not show all my "songs" (book chapters) or "artists" (authors), but there were plenty of reviews that said you would be able to access all your files in the "file management" function (true). So I figured it might call for a little "extra" work to access everything but i accepted that. There are a number of problems that make this player unusable, at least for me. 1st the directory in the file function only recognizes 25(ish) characters, the file structure I use for my books include the series name, book number, and the title, there is a good chance that all the books in a series will show up as individual files with the exact same name. This makes it impossible to figure out which file is for the 1st book in a series vs. the last book. 2nd within the file directory function, when you navigate to a specific book so that you can play it the chapters are not sorted in order. My files are all numbered correctly and they have the correct order number, but they don't sort so you can't start play on file #1 and expect is to then go to #2 when it is done (No I do not have it on shuffle). I had to go through a lot of effort to rename my files so that they were labeled such that they should sort correctly, a complete waste of time. 3rd You are supposed to be able to use a 256 GB Mini SD Card, which does actually work I can see all the different files that are on the card, but I can't navigate to a book and hit play. I was counting on being able to do this to get around all my files not showing up in the "music" function. I have to open the book and hit play in the chapter view which is a problem due to my second issue above. 4th In the "Music" function when you sort by "artist" (author), the complete name is cut off after 10 characters, not a big deal because I can recognize who the author is, but because I included the series name in the file name all the books in the series are lumped together. 5th In the "music" function sorting by "album", again because it only recognizes 20 something characters it lumps all the different files together. What this means, from a practical point, is that I have a book series where the series name and book number is to long for the software to recognize so I have one entry for a series of books (all the books in the series) and all the chapters for all the different books are lumped together into one entry, for example a series with 5 books will show up as 1 book but it will have 5 introductions, 5 chapter 1s, etc. Which means if I hit "play" all 5 introductions will play then all 5 chapter 1s will play, etc. Which again defeats the whole reason for my buying this player. At this point I don't know what, if anything I can do in order to use this player. My bottom line, I can't use this for the reason I purchased it. VERY DISAPPOINTING. I DO NOT recommend buying this is you are planning on using it for audiobooks, unless you only have a few books (less than 10) or only use a memory card that is less that 64 GB (the smallest card I have). I think all my "issues" could be fixed, but in all reality I don't expect that will ever happen and I will never be able to use this. If playing your files in order is important to you, choose something else.
