I usually keep my headphone purchases in the $25 - $30, because I am guilty of losing things. Case in point, I lost a pair on Friday night and hopped on Amazon the next day to buy a new pair. These were recommended as a slightly nicer, slightly pricier version of what I usually get so I figured what the heck! The cord on these is unbelievably long and clunky. I prefer the neckband design for wireless earbuds (again I lose things) but there is so much excess wiring. I would have fared better with wired headphones. This model also touts an Apple W1 chip with magnetic auto play and pause. The magnet does trigger an auto pause, but if the buds are magnetically connected any longer than 15 seconds they don’t auto play when disconnected. Having to push play manually would not be an issue if it didn't take so long to find the button on the obscenely long neck band. I also took a few calls and music did not resume after I hung up. I have never had a Bluetooth device where this was a problem. These headphones are markedly worse than your premium beats or airpods (naturally), but I am disappointed to say the experience is worse than a pair of Anker's or something you can get for 30 bucks cheaper. Will probably hold onto them as a back up pair (I lose things), but I've had them for just over 24 hours and I am seeking out a new pair. Update: I bought a pair of AirPods. Auto play/pause is still only a 15 second feature, but tapping the pod makes things much more streamlined and the sound is better. The cord is the primary issue with these phones. I would still go high end model or low end. This middle ground price doesn’t give bang for buck.

I'm very happy with the performance of this router. I had the Slate model for years. This is very similar but bigger and better. I was starting to have trouble with the Slate not being able to connect to every wifi network and decided to upgrade. I'm glad I did. The AX has no problem with the newest wifi6 networks when acting as a repeater. It also provides a much stronger and faster connection for clients. The software is very similar to the Slate. I use the built in WireGuard VPN software to connect to my home network. The Slate would top out at about 10 Mbps, but this one maxes out my home connections speed at about 25 Mbps. According to the specs, it should be capable of much faster, but I just haven't had it connected to a fast enough source to test this yet. It does everything I need, and I'm very happy with it, but I do have a few criticisms. It is substantially bigger than the Slate. It still fits the bill of a travel router, but definitely takes a lot more room in the luggage. It also has substantially higher power requirements and I'm not thrilled with how it's delivered. This unit takes 20 watts and delivers that with a 5 volt 4 amp adapter. The Slate could run off just about any USB adapter. Try to find an adapter that delivers 4 amps though, or a cable that can handle it. The adapter is big with a thick wire. So, on top of the AX being bigger than the Slate, the power adapter is huge compared to the Slate. I'd say the power adapter alone takes up as much room at the old Slate router. I feel like they should have increased the voltage rather than letting this thing draw 4 amps. That's what the fast cell phone chargers do. They jump up to 9 volts to reduce the current requirement. That approach doesn't require a heavy power brick and thick wire. I attached some images with the old Slate and new Slate AX side by side.
It may support 2&5g WiFi but it does NOT support 5G WiFi alone.

review_text: Klipsch discontinued their Promedia 2.1 set years ago and seems like now in 2020 that 6.5" woofer replacement is not available -not even on eBay at the time I was looking. Common speaker problem -especially in Florida, the foam excursions dry up and crumble away after years of use leaving 2 options; replace the foam excursions OR replace the whole speaker. I bought the "DIY" foam replacement kit for $25 first (on Amazon). Lots of great reviews on this - personally I thought my work was perfect until I powered it up and played some music -and it farted to no end (no good). So that was a $25 waste. Some people have a real knack for this - I guess I'm not one of those people. Instructions were not clear (generic instructions - not specific to this speaker) and as perfectly as I tried to glue in this excursion the speaker didn't come out right. So I bought this little $10 replacement. For $10 it is really great! But it's not as good as the original Klipsch when it worked. That Klipsch ProMedia 2.0 6.5" sub is a 6ohm speaker. This is an 8 ohm speaker. It has some punch with the right music, equilization and volume - but not nearly as good as the original Klipsch (not correctly matched to the internal amp built into this subwoofer assembly. But for $10 it's good enough. If you are a hard core audiophile you're going to have your computer running through a higher end speaker system anyway. But for a quick dedicated media set (2 speakers and a sub) this was pretty great -sad Klipsch doesn't sell it any more. When your sub's excursion foam breaks up -this is worth $10. I might send my original to a speaker repair shop for them to re-foam - expect that might be $35-$50. I can use this one in the mean time and it's not bad.

This replaces a non-Nikon 28-300mm general purpose lens, and surpasses it in every way. I miss the 300mm range but appreciate the wider 24mm end as well which is more useful in close quarters. Yes it goes to f6.3 pretty quickly in the zoom range, but with today's cameras you can up your ISO a lot without getting too noisy. It has minimal to insignificant distortion and CA is also kept well under control. When used on the 45.7MP sensor of the Z7/ Z72 you also have plenty of room for cropping, thus utilizing the best part of the lens, and makes it very useful for birds, insects and general close up work. I have yet to try it for portraits but have any confidence it will shine there too. I shoot professionally, and have several prime and top grade lenses to compare it to. I have been really impressed with the 24-200mm's performance. While it might not be as absolutely as sharp as some of them it is not too far off, and for an all purpose lens it makes far less compromises that you would expect. The enclosed shot is a moderate crop from about 150mm and has a nice bokeh as well.

review_text: I love bluetooth earbuds. My Bose QC's are probably the best sound from a compact earbud - I've never experienced better, but these EarFuns, for a fraction of the price, are amazing. Sound is clear and crisp. Most of the time we wear earbuds we are on the move and there is extraneous sounds, movement , etc, and the EarFuns handled this well.Now, for the Noise Cancellation. it is difficult to beat the Bose's for that too, sorry Sony. Now, for 20% of the price , the EarFuns provide perfectly acceptable ANC, most annoying sounds are masked to an acceptable level. I've tested them on planes and trains and they worked well. They do not rival high end products - but I don't expect that at this price point.All in all I think the Ear Fun Air Pro 3 is a bargain, a great all round product.

I used this case to complete the first build I've ever made. Obviously, my opinion is from the point of view of a novice builder. I suggest checking the Corsair website for greater details and to ask questions before you determine if this is the right case for you. This is a full size case. If you want to build compact, this is not for you. As a first-time builder, the features that attracted me to this case are: 1. The large size makes installation easy and provides open space for airflow. 2. It has a lot of fan mounts (I am overly paranoid about temperature control) 3. It is strong, fits tightly together for no rattling sounds, and is customizable. The size of the case and the abundance of fan mounts provide excellent airflow. Additionally, all of the fan mounts have easily removable mesh filters that allow for quick cleaning. Don't overlook the PSU intake filter on the bottom. Since this is my first build, I thought I would struggle mounting all the parts because of needing to work in confined spaces; however, the mobo was probably the most difficult part, but even mounting it was simple. I think the standoffs may have been a bit short compared to what I saw in videos. You may want to buy some taller ones if it makes you nervous. I mounted a large CPU cooling tower, and it still has a few inches of space in the case. Cable management was also easy due to the amount of open space behind the mobo. I didn't notice this in the specs, but I was pleasantly surprised to find 2 additional mounts out of the way on the backside for SSD drives and mounts for 2 HDDs at the bottom. Although, I removed the HDD mounts because I don't need them, and they are near the PSU. They may restrict room for power cables. The side panel window provides a normal amount of visibility for RGB enthusiasts. It is important to note that the window is glass, not clear plastic. This means it is heavier and obviously breakable. Be careful with it. The case is solid, silent, and easy to configure. I don't know what else a person would want in a case. I highly recommend it to anyone who wants a large tower. If you are designing a compact build, this is not your case.

I’ve been a Fitbit user since 2012 and having used at least 7 different devices over those years (Zip, One, Force, Charge HR, Charge 2-4) - long enough to know where they’ve hit the mark and where they’ve missed it. The Sense was an upgrade from my Charge 4. Where it excels: - Watch face: allows you to choose the face with many free and paid options ($0.50 - $1.50) - Built in GPS (same as Charge 4, handy feature) - Sleep tracking: includes optional SPO2 monitoring with an additional free app installed to the watch - Apps: you have a number of different apps that you can download to the watch - Exercise tracking: Charge let you add your top 5 exercises to your watch for quick add. Sense has the complete list already on it - Water logging: can be done right from the watch (awesome!) - Weather: you can add an app to see the weather on your phone. Supports multiple locations - Music control: right from your watch (Pandora, Spotify, Deezer) - Voice assistant (Google or Alexa), EDA scan, find my phone, answer calls from your watch, full text message viewing, and ECG are new additions from the Charge 4 - notifications to drink water during the day (optional setting) is helpful - Alarm will monitor your sleep to wake you at the most opportune time (not in the middle of REM sleep for example but before/at the time you set) Now for the bad… - Claims to hold a 6 day charge but with basic use and some daily exercising, I find myself charging it every few days - watch faces are nice but you can only keep 5 on hand in your app. If you accidentally write over a paid face, its a pain to get it back without paying for it again - watch disconnects from your phone very frequently requiring one to open the app constantly and sync to restore the connection - find my phone (one of the features I was really looking forward to) rarely works because the watch disconnects from the phone so frequently - ECG regularly says the results are inconclusive despite remaining perfectly still - Missed notifications (calls. texts, calendar, drink water) - a constant issue because the watch doesn't stay connected to the phone - Doesn't seem to sync in the background despite all the settings on the app, watch, phone indicating it should Aside from the frustration around stuff constantly not working because watch disconnects from the phone, the vibrations on the watch are sad - even with vibration turned to “strong”. Additionally, the Charge 4 had different vibrations depending on the notification (reminders vs calls vs texts, etc). The Sense notification vibrate are all the same, and can barely be felt. I don't rely on the watch to wake me up whereas my Charge 4 was an awesome alarm as the vibration was so strong. Am I happy with this watch? Eh. It has a lot of potential if these main issues are addressed by way of software updates or hardware upgrades in v2 Side note: all my complaints are echoed on the Fitbit Community pages which tells me its not a problem with the device I received, its issues with Fitbit Sense in general

If you just want to have a headphone stand that gives you a place to put your headphones, this stand will work just as good as any out there. I initially bought two of these 6TB drives. One was fine -- no complaints. (UPDATE 8/12/2021: The first drive I bought ended up dying after a week of actual usage. The SMART tests and other diagnostics were 100% fine initially, then as soon as I started to actually use the drive it completely died and I lost data. HORRIBLE, GARBAGE DRIVES! DON'T BUY THESE!) This only earns one star, I would give zero stars if I could. After plugging the second drive in for the first time and powering up, my drive monitoring software (Acronis Drive Monitor) popped up with a disk health warning on the 2nd drive -- bad/reallocated sectors. Drive health 80%. Warnings to immediately back up my data because the drive is showing signs of early failure. Yet I could clearly see this appeared to be a brand new drive, power on hours was zero, everything seemed okay other than the bad/reallocated sectors. Since this hard drive was going into my NAS and I didn't want to risk the drive dying at an inopportune moment, I heeded the warnings and decided to get it replaced through Amazon's returns. After all, the listing says "Product *works* [emphasis mine] and looks like new. Backed by the 90-day Amazon Renewed Guarantee. This pre-owned product has been *professionally inspected, tested* [emphasis mine] and cleaned by Amazon-qualified suppliers." Well, this drive certainly looks like new appearance-wise, but doesn't work like new! It already has signs of imminent failure out of the box -- either it's defective, or it's an old and busted drive that was poorly or improperly refurbished. Next, Amazon initially put me through the wringer asking me to get a warranty claim number from Seagate (the drive's OEM). So I had to get on the line with Seagate technical support who asked me to use their SeaTool software to run a bunch of tests on the drive which confirmed that indeed it had bad/reallocated sectors. With a case number in hand, I was able to get Amazon to replace the drive. The replacement arrived in a few days. So I plugged the replacement in... and found the exact same problem. I was sent a different drive with the same specs and a different serial number, seemingly in good visual condition and in a fresh anti-static bag, but just like the previous drive it had bad/reallocated sectors indicating imminent premature failure. This time, frustrated with having to go through Amazon, I decided to start a warranty RMA claim with the seller using the contact information provided on the 3-year warranty card in the package containing the drive. They happily acknowledged my claim within around 5 hours, shipped out a drive the next day, and I received it today (three days later) via USPS Priority Mail. When I made the RMA claim I specifically mentioned my hardships with the previous drive, and mentioned I was really hoping that this drive would be better and not have any bad/reallocated sectors since I really needed to be able to rely on this drive not showing clear signs that it would die on me prematurely (within reason, obviously, given that these are "refurbished" and sold at a discount). Lo and behold, I plugged in this drive and immediately Acronis Drive Monitor starts flashing even more serious alarms at me. This replacement drive was at imminent risk of failure and was in far worse condition than even the two previous drives -- 30% disk health overall. Tons of bad/reallocated sectors. Not even usable for unimportant data, just total junk. Completely ridiculous and unacceptable. Did they even test these drives before sending them out? I emailed the warranty department again and told them about my experience, showing them the results of my SMART diagnostics, and while they offered a profuse apology and a refund, speculating that maybe the drive got damaged in transit, this whole ordeal was a colossal waste of time and energy. The fact is, the likelihood that this drive or any of the previous ones got damaged in transit is pretty low. I've literally never had this problem before, being a purchaser of dozens of drives. Rather, it's much more likely that these drives are simply low quality garbage and/or failed drives which are being pawned off as "professionally refurbished" by resetting their SMART data (like turning back the odometer on a car). I might have just got lucky with the first drive that turned out okay, the rest immediately showing signs of being old busted junk by throwing errors when they're first powered up. Don't buy these drives. The price is attractive but it's not worth your time or the risk that they will fail on you unexpectedly. Spend the extra $70 or so and get a new drive from a better seller.

Most, if not all, televisions will be subject to updates, it's not unique to this TV. So this was not a deal breaker for me. After my update I did not notice a difference with the picture quality. I'm only a novice when it comes to calibration though. Watching some 4k content on you tube is amazing, especially scenery. Honestly, I don't know if I'd be able to tell the difference with 4k content and 1080 content. I sit 12 feet away from my H9g set. Up close the pixels are very small and the edges of objects I'm viewing are VERY crisp and clean. The color is quite good and the black levels in contrast with bright color is pretty amazing. The TV needs to be set on smooth level to reduce the stutter and judder of anything that Pans across the screen. The "Soap Opera" effect is very noticeable if this setting is Not used as many before me have commented on. (Maybe check it out at a local dealer to see if that might be a deal breaker for you.) I use this TV for movie watching. No sports or gaming. The available 4k content that I've seen on You Tube, Net Flix and Amazon Prime has been a mixed bag of quality. I can say that when good quality content is displayed it comes across as quite beautiful and stunning. Too many variables to consider with 4k to compare apples to apples. I can not comment on a 4k blu ray platform as I do not have one hooked up. I've had this H9g for a little over one month and there recently has been an issue with the screen going black for one to two seconds. If other reviewers start to mention this problem with their H9g's then it might be an issue. Overall, I'm quite happy and pleased with this purchase. Excellent picture quality that holds up well with You Tube testing videos, black level testing, blooming, banding, brightness and color, among others. I'm looking forward to purchasing a 4k blu ray and expect not to be disappointed. If your willing to wait for it to become available, like I did, I believe that you will be pleased with the purchase. Hope this might help you !

Amcrest reimbursed me the full purchase price for this as a product testing program in exchange for giving them honest feedback. The following is the complete e-mail (with very minor edits for clarity,) that I sent Amcrest. --------- I am a systems administrator for a relatively small private, non-profit University as well as an occasional Twitch Streamer. I also own two other Amcrest devices (WiFi security cameras, though one doesn’t function.) I have tested the webcam on my work PC a few times since receiving it, including conducting a candidate interview with it today. I’ve also tested it with OBS Studio on my computer at work (which I’ve used to test a few other A/V devices) although I have yet to attempt to actually Twitch stream with it at home. My goal is to provide nitpick-levels of detail in order to help you develop the best products possible. My feedback is as follows: **Image Quality** The lens focus is not optimal for desktop use and, as a fixed lens, it cannot be changed. It’d be nice if you could do so manually by manipulating the lens, as you can with some cheaper webcams. My webcam is almost exactly 2ft away from me on my monitor at work, but my face and hair seems relatively blurred/fuzzy. I’ve attached two captures taken on different days. My face looks a little out of focus, while objects in the background are far more clear. The parts of the image that are more clear look fantastic, far better than your average run of the mill webcamera, but the Achilles’s Heel of the device is that a person sitting 2 feet away from the camera (which has an effective distance listed as >1ft) is blurry compared to the background, and that, especially given there is no way to control the focus like I can by turning the lens on the (insert random-named Chinese brand from amazon) camera I was using before, makes it only a slight upgrade over that camera. The overall image quality is superior to the cheap no-name camera, but it’s very, very distracting and disappointing that everything behind the subject is far better focused than the actual subject themselves. Additionally, lack of 60fps at any resolution is disappointing. I believe some more mainstream-brand devices can do 1080p@30 or 720@60. This does 30FPS on every setting except 4K. For content creators, where many streamers are trying to stream in 60fps no matter what resolution they opt to transmit in, this is not really a good webcam for those users for that reason. Another issue I ran into is powerline frequency. I am not overly familiar with specifics of where 50Hz is needed vs 60Hz, but the camera defaulted to 50Hz for me and had very strange image quality issues, I suppose you’d call it a flicker. I had to use the Windows Camera app to change that to 60Hz to eliminate it. If this is a regionally-varied thing (kind of like NTSC vs PAL,) then this will be extremely frustrating for American buyers, many of which wouldn’t know that the powerline frequency setting is even a thing, and especially not how to change it, given that there is no configuration software for the camera at all. The biggest point here for me though is the focus. This would be SUCH a killer webcam if the focus was better! Manually adjustable, autofocus, or simply tweaking the fixed focus at the factory. Unfortunately the focus issues described earlier absolutely kill my mood on this camera at this price point. **Build quality** Decent. Doesn’t feel overly cheap, but doesn’t feel premium by any means at all. What I mistook for a second microphone was actually just an LED light. Speaking of that light, I understand that it’s reassuring for some to know their webcam isn’t on, but most other manufacturers do that by simply not having a light active when the device isn’t in use. Having a constantly-on LED is annoying, and there’s no way to remove the “disabled” light without covering it up, which disables the indicator that the camera is enabled. This is something that could easily be toggled with configuration software, if any existed. Also, the stand seems stable but feels like it should be a bit harder to adjust, as simply closing the included privacy shutter tries to topple the camera forward for me unless I kind of pinch it close or move my hand in a very particular way. I feel like it being tighter/harder to move would keep it very firmly in place when angling the camera itself up and down, and when using the privacy shutter. **Audio Quality** Webcam audio quality is never all that good, short of paying an exorbitant amount of money. This is no exception. As a result, I almost always use a dedicated headset mic. The HVAC in my office is fairly loud, with the ambient sound level hovering around 48 or 49db as measured by my watch, vs around 30-32db background noise as measured in a quiet room at home. The camera microphone picked me up without too much background noise, and while my MS Teams test call has me sounding like I’m in the bottom of a bucket (admittedly some of that could be the service) it’s still way better than the no-name camera I mentioned having earlier. I have never used the microphone on the no-name camera, but we have a few of those on site and our users who don’t pair them with headsets have to have us install equalizer software to actually make those cameras work with MS Teams or they are inaudible. The fact that the Amcrest camera picked me up with no issues is a plus. **Overall Thoughts** This is an otherwise very good webcam impacted by the focusing issue I keep going on about. If the focus issue wasn’t a thing, I would say the price point (I paid around $70) is pretty fair. However, taking the focus issues into consideration, combined with my other gripes (particularly having to find and configure powerline frequency, etc.) I would say that this camera as it stands now, is overpriced (at $70) compared to alternatives that can auto and manually focus, and which have the capability to operate at 60fps for lower resolutions, which is important for digital content creators, an industry that is becoming increasingly popular. Most web conferencing applications generally don’t have fantastic video quality anyway, so I feel it would be a better to focus on feature set and the optic glass / lens vs trying to cram in more megapixels. It doesn’t matter if my face is blurry at 1080p, 1440p, or 2160p, it’s still blurry. Thank you for the opportunity to receive and test your product. I hope that my feedback is helpful.

I'm a computer geek from way back. I had systems that dated all the way back to the late early 2000's. The actual systems are long gone sent to the rubbish bin. I kept the hard drives because they contained things I might still want. I kept the SATA hard drives on a shelf in my walk in closet. Just recently after a deep clean I found like 10 of these old SATA drives. All but one still worked. The one SATA drive that croaked had only a backup of the Windows 7 operating system on it. I had no bloody use for that muck. So I set to installing 5 of the old drives at a time in this bulk hard drive enclosure. It was like going back in time. Tons of old files and pictures greeted me. Things I forgot all about but still desperately wanted. By today's standards the drives were tiny most being between 10 GB's, 100 GB's and a few at a whooping 500 GB to 1 terabyte. I downloaded the whole lot to an 8 Terabyte storage brick and again to a back up 8 TB storage brick. I can now safely erase and break up these old drives thanks to this very easy solution. The nice thing is that pulling data off five drives at a time was very much a time saver. I got things sorted in about two days. The fast USB bandwidth moved my files quickly the only limit being the slow old drives. There is nothing difficult about configuring this enclosure to see and access the 5 drives. There is NO special software or geeky knowledge. On Windows 10 it was just plug and play. There are 6 bright blue LED's on the side of the enclosure. One to show the unit is powered. 5 to show the drives in residence are operational and recognized. Windows 10 discovers the drives readily. At first their might be a few minutes before Windows see's the drives for the first time. When in doubt just restart. Be aware that you should remove the USB connecting this 5 Drive enclosure to your computer because often times these old drives have boot sector start ups and operating systems on them. These other OS's on these drives could confuse your start up processes and cause your system to hang. Let your system start first then once the Operating system is fully up and running only then do you plug in the 5 drive enclosure. Wait a few minutes and Windows should recognize the drives. It's your call but at times Windows will ask to scan and correct flaws it finds on the older drives. I'd say unless you know very well what you are doing always refuse to let Windows "Fix" the drives because if the Window's fix breaks the drive it might not be recoverable. I'm advising caution when asked to let Windows repair a drive but of course its your call. Hope this helps. The 5 drive enclosure was worth its weight in gold for me as it brought back pictures and documents of old I'd forgotten about.

review_text: I really wanted to love this dac/amp, I really did. I wanted a full tube amp (not a hybrid like most on the market) with an integrated dac, and this is one of the only models available. However, there is a constant electrical buzz (mostly in the right channel, but present in both) that changes with the volume. It's always there, and very distracting. I tried to fix it in every possible way: new tubes (Russian military grade imports), a power conditioner, better shielded cables, and isolation from emi sources. None of these changes has effected this noise, so I'm guessing its the wiring/interference from inside the device itself. Monoprice always has great ideas, but their QC is hit or miss from product to product. This one is a definite miss, that's why it goes on sale for $280 from the $400 msrp often. It does sound great, and the external housing and controls feel nice, but the constant noise is too much for me.

As per their advertised features, they are an excellent bluetooth headphone. The company's customer service is great. The problem is sensitivity to interference, from microwave ovens (to be expected), and other spurious noise sources (intermittent and undetermined). The sound will cut out, and in worst cases, the connection is dropped. When the noise cancellation circuit is energized, the interference generates a loud CLICK or POP, that is very annoying. Not sure if that can be engineered away (without too much expense). In comparison to other bluetooth headphones (Turtle Beach, Corsair) that utilize bluetooth USB A dongles, the Q20+ range was inferior. Not sure if the integral bluetooth in the laptop, phone or notepad was to blame. Due to the use of the same IC chips by different labels, it's hard to say if the technology is to blame, or a specific implementation. Could it be antenna issues? Noise rejection failure? Who knows. Perhaps, when the "next generation" beyond bluetooth, moves to the 5 GHz band, the interference problem will be resolved. If you have a low-noise (RF) environment, these headphones should work well.

Of course headphones are bulkier and put more pressure on the ears, so it’s a preference thing as to which you use for what situation. Perhaps the ANC would be more evident if I was somewhere nosier like on a plane or outdoors on a busy street. When switching from transparent to ANC mode and vice versa, a voice tells you which mode you’ve switched to which I appreciate rather than just a beep. Quality of the sound is very good with a nice bass and the fit is comfortable. I was pleasantly surprised to find out the case can act as a power bank for other devices as it has a USB port (guess I didn’t read the description too closely when I first ordered it). The one thing I think could’ve been designed better is the opening to the charging portal. You have to hold the plastic down to access the wire charging portal. I have a wireless charger but I recently read that wireless charging may degrade your battery faster, but not sure if that is because people may have tendency to keep charging their device when full or near full due to ease of wireless charging (which is not good for device) or other reasons. Overall, I like these new earbuds and look forward to using them outdoors.

I was excited to try this new pass-through design connector. Got myself a nice pair of Ideal FT-45 crimps and these plugs. I made two CAT6 cables using these plugs. My excitement quickly faded after plugging in my newly made cables and checking my Windows 10 network settings and my routers network settings. Found both devices reporting 100baseT instead of 1000baseT. Previous CAT5e cables I was using always allowed for 1000baseT Link speed. Removed the cables and re-verified my pin out was correct for T568B on all 4 plugs. Found all 4 plug ends that I just made appearing to be correct so I swapped back over to my old CAT5e cables and rechecked link speed. With old cables the link speed went back up to 1000baseT. Cut all the plugs off that I had just terminated and replaced them again. Reinstalled them and found link speed again at 100baseT. After reading some of the bad reviews for this product I decided to cut all of the newly terminated plugs off again and replace them with some old style cheap monoprice plugs that I had bought several years ago. After replacing the plugs I retested the link rate speed and found I know have the 1000baseT data rate I was expecting. I am not sure what it is about these plugs but they simply do no work no matter how perfect the termination looks. As another reviewer pointed out, the plugs do not look as pictured in the ad. Mine looked to be gold plated only on the top of the plug pins with the rest looking like a silver color. The item page for these plugs shows a couple of pictures clearly showing the entire pin as being gold plated. For me this has turned into a waste of time and money. I really do not understand all of the good reviews unless I was one of the unlucky ones to receive a bad batch of these plugs.

Now I know surge protectors and different breakers can cause speed drops so I ran a best case test to see the speed. I ran a test in the basement, next to the router, on the same circuit breaker, with no surge protectors, hardwired and got best speed of 120 mbps. Don’t waste your money on this. It’s too good to be true. My regular WiFi is 4x as fast. Wire up some Ubiquiti access points and you’ll be in a much better spot.

The laptop is good and it build quality too. However, 8GB of RAM (with only 5,75GB available), keeps running out of memory all the time. I'm totally frustrated by it and I regret having bought this laptop. It's not possible to expand the RAM, and that a killer for me.

So before I bought the eero, I was using a nighthawk router. Amazing router, nighthawk is great, but it was old, I bought it before wifi 6 and everything. I just upgraded my internet to 1g of fiber, and figured I should probably upgrade my wifi as well. First of all, just switching to a mesh system in general is amazing. Wifi extenders are a headache. This eero was cheaper than the nighthawk mesh system by a LOT. I don't know if it's as good, or better than the other mesh systems, but I know this. 1: it's sleak, and small, so it fits NICELY into my interior. 2: it's cheaper than other options! 3: the app is SUPER intuitive, and easy to use with plenty of amazing features! 4: I was having issues with my routers not connecting to my fiber (issue on my internet providers part) and the customer service was friendly, quick, and helped me figure out the problem, gave me some numbers to give to my internet providers, and they were able to fix the issue. 5: it does what it says! I'm getting 1g of wifi through out my house, very very fast speeds, and it's mesh! I have one in my living room, one in my office, and one in my gaming room. The one in my gaming room is the one set up directly to the fiber (the gateway? Not sure, not very tech savvy). What's nice is I can do a direct ethernet connection to the mesh systems which i do with my ps5 and switch in the living room and my wifes work computer in the office, and it works just fine somehow not sacrificing my wifi bandwidth? Magic. I then hook my gaming PC up to the one thats directly connected to fiber, i don't see a difference in speed, they are all utilizing very fast speeds. My smart home responds fast (mostly samsung and govee). My security system doesn't ever lag (I use eufy). It's literally mind blowing compared to my old house set up 🤣 (fiber) and this mesh wifi changed my life y'all, so I can't even imagine the need for the more expensive 6e, unless your ultra rich and have a GIANT house (mine is 2300 square feet and I do not lose coverage). I ALSO have a few of the cheap echo dot 5th gens, which extend the mesh system even further! That is my review, 10/10 eero. Love the app, love the speeds, perfect!

This is an ok product, but it doesn't do anything particularly well. The interface is lousy. You have to got way too many buttons to get to commonly used settings. The clearvu offers no advantage over the traditional sonar. It's literally the same image in a different color. It's so grainy that it's worthless. The tradition sonar actually gives more information because of the multiple colors. The accuracy/detail of this unit is low compared to slightly higher end models. Everything is just blobs. There's not enough information graphed to be really helpful. This unit is very low on features. The mapping feature is useless. Plotting points requires way too many buttons presses to use. If you just need a basic sonar, save some money and get the lowest end striker model. The regular traditional sonar will give just add much real information as is available on the more expensive model. Or, get something like the deeper sonar that uses your phone for a head unit, has real mapping, a better interface, real maps and constant updates/support. Battery life being the drawback.
Good looking, fast charger which charges my Apple phone and watch as well as my Sony buds.

review_text: I bought 3 headset. The Steelseries Arctis 7+, the Turtle beach stealth 700, and this JBL quantum 800. I've had the first two for about 2 weeks and i wanted a good headset with the same features as the Turtle beach 700. Specifically simultaneously Bluetooth and wireless USB connection use. If the Turtle Beaches weren't so notoriously flimsy with deceptive solidity i would have kept those. So ultimately it is between this 800 and arctis 7+ and i am basically set on keeping these after a few days. Build/comfort: 7/10 i feel more comfortable tossing these around (like into a bag, onto a bed, falling off a table or small daily accidents) I wish the pads weren't leather and/or at least had a fabric ear cup like my comparison headsets. Sound isolation is not bad nor is sound leak, not the greatest but average muffles sound to where there's plenty i don't make out sounds well but still hear them to know there is a sound. But when in use i don't even use the Active Noise Canceling because the isolation and volume is enough. They have good weight distribution for my head. I prefer some clamping force to relieve me from feelinge the head band too much. The 800 has a nice balance between the 3 sides. I wear glasses half the time and I've worn worse. I honestly can't complain about glasses with these. I've worn these for more than 10 hours multiple times. Sound: 8/10 the sound is good. I was surprised how flat the audio was out the box BUT it wasn't totally flat despite the EQ saying so. At least not compared to the arctis and my srudio monitors. The main issue is if you are going to be using ANC sometimes on and sometimes off. The Low and bass end is stronger ON and weaker OFF. And after adjusting it im still worling on finding a good bass balance because it either stands out too nuch or is too hidden. I couldn't use my EQ sliders from other devices. But the potential is their for great balance if you stick to one mode. The sound stage/surround sound is a bit weird in my opinion. Not bad just different, tighter. I play on PS5 not PC so i am not sure if the JBL surround options affect this, but i do use DTX on the playstation end. I did notice the surround sound got better and less narrow after messing witn the setting on the PC hub when i reconnected it to my playstation (turned it off and on). But after i couldn't tell a difference between on and off. Of my 3 comparisons i think the TB700 weirdly enough had the best sound stage/surround sound for gaming. I would put these 3rd but they do job and it is probably better on PC than playstation. The 3.5mm jack audio is solid. My phone has a built in DAC and LG sound engine. I actually just tested it right now while typing this. Almost want to move the rating to a 9 but i stick to 8. ANC does not work while jacked in, it will turn off anc. When the headset is on your PC settings affect the jack audio BUT it will not stay on if you are not using USB 2.4ghz or Bluetooth. Of the 3 headsets this is the only one without high end distortion. Battery: 5/10 Tied for the worst part of the 800. With Lights, USB wireless, Bluetooth, and ANC you are looking at 9-10 hours. With no lights, no ANC, just Bluetooth and USB wireless you are looking at about 24 hours or so. My next test will be with ANC, Bluetooth, USB, and no lights to see how much ANC affects battery and i will update this section. Full charge is between an hour and 2. Very fast. As i am sure you have read the headset will immediately cut power when plugged in and i hate that. But also if there is no sound from USB 2.4ghz or Bluetooth playing for about 20 minutes the headset powers down. And once the battery is at about 25% it will play a warning aound. Then again at aboit 15% and 5%. For my comparison the TB700 does a stagnant voice prompt that is annoying and the arctis does a tone every few minutes which is just as annoying. I do not find the JBL 800 warning annoying. It highlights how the battery isn't THAT bad since the warnings are about an hour or more apart. Plenty of time to give it a 15 minite charge for a solid 20% boost. UPDATE: having the ANC turned on does inconsistently deplete much more of the battery. I lost about 30% in 2 hours. Without ANC and with Bluetooth and 2.4ghz dongle and lights i was losing about 10% an hour. Without ANC or lights i was losing about 10% every 1-3 hours. I lowered the acore from a 6 to a generous 5. Connectivity: begrudgingly 5/10 I would love to give these a 10, very few headsets have the 3 options of Bluetooth, 3.5mm jack, and usb 2.4ghz and can use them all simultaneously! Unfortunately the range is non existent. Per my comparison the TB700 cuts in and out at the back door of the house (about 10-15 steps away), the Arctis cuts in and out a bit earlier at the kitchen ( 8-12 steps) and this JBL has the most annoying disconnect reconnect at the just walking out of my room (5-9 steps) the distance is honestly REALLY bad, the worst i can remember of any wireless device. But i can get to the bathroom with both doors, bedroom and bathroom closed ( 3-5 steps) no i am not taking large steps i am size 11 us men and my feet are about a tonail apart each step. If you have a JBL device it plays that sound every time it connects and it plays it even if the connection is interrupted a second. Awful. The connectivity is ironically the worst despite also being the thing i got them for. I suppose turning off while charging falls undee this as well. Oh and the mic does not work with Bluetooth. I read people using it on Bluetooth and tbat being their main use, but apparently mine doesn't. Could be a dud. Mic: 3/10 While in PS5 chats no one can tell the difference between this and the other 2 headsets although i can during the mic tests. It is pretty average. The actual mic isn't as ugly as it looked in photos and actually blends in well when swung up. It feels weird how it stiffly can be beny where i want it but hey it works. Weird there is a mute button on the left earcup when swinging up mutes it but great to have a backup if anything happens. UPDATE: after streaming and listening to playback, this is one of the worst sounding mics i have ever used. Plugging earbuds into the ps5 remote sounds better or the same as this. So much background noise, so much digital noise. Horrible low volume voice pickup but drop a pen and you will hear it. Changing my overall score. Other 7/10 Esthetically these are very nice with and without the lights. The PC hub software is better than the arctis software in my opinion. Has all the same options plus a little more like saving more than 1 custom EQ. The JBL quantum does not work with any JBL mobile apps unfortunately. And unlike the other 2 i had no issue updating the JBL quantum 800. Overall 5/10 I am ultimately keeping the JBL over the other 2 because unlike the TB700 i don't think it will break on its own after a few months and it doesn't have distortion. And unlike the arctis it has simultaneous Bluetooth and 2.4ghz which is my must have feature. If you don't need that feature i absolutely recommend the Steelseries arctis for gaming. But if you are like me and need Bluetooth and USB wireless simultaneously i would recommend the JBL 800. The battery isn't that big an issue, i just think when you compare it to something like the arctis 7+ that can last 30+ hours, makes it seem worse than it actually is. In reality the 10-20 hour battery life (depending if you use lights) is kind of average for audio devices. I think most people will be find getting home from work or school and playing for 2-6 hours with these. I am a typical 10+ hour power player and they have been fine. UPDATE: I. Looking to replace and return these. The mic is just horrible. I was willing to accept the average battery life and extremely short wireless range but adding on how bad the mic is. I would not recommend these for more than $80 or less after tax. I would have been furiously upset if i paid full price for these. These would have been perfect if they didn't waste their time putting lights on it and instead actually made the mic, ANC, and range better.

If you need a high volume pack for transporting your laptop plus materials like binders and books, beware. This pack is divided into three narrow compartments. The first zippered section is well organized for your phone and small stuff. The second and third sections are both well-padded but way too narrow. I can barely fit in a binder and two books. Because it's so well padded, this would be a good pack for commuting with two laptops and a few other items. It's not great for the college prof. or grad student on the go. Also: The water bottle holder on the side's too narrow for most bottles.

This backdrop looks great and will serve its purpose for on camera work. A couple things were not clear at time of purchase. 1. There are 3 streams of light coming down from the top of the backdrop. These are NOT on the drop as pictured on the sample. It is misleading. Bricks only, NO streams of light! 2. There is NO sleeve to slide the pole through at the top. Had to roll the backdrop and poke holes in it to attach it to the stands.

Amazon blocked my account after I questioned 2 charges that I could not figure out. These charges totalled less than $30. I could not view my account, none of my 2 dozen Alexa devices would work, the clock on my echo dot wouldn't even work. My Prime acct, which I pay for annually did not work. I could not watch a single video. This brand new 65" TV I just purchased was a useless hunk of garbage. This review is more about how Amazon treats it's Prime members, more than 10 years, than about the TV. I was appalled at the fact that they would prevent me from using what I already paid for because I questioned something worth less than $29, after spending tens of thousands of $$$ over the years. And BTW, noone would tell me what I was being charged for after inquiring for 2 days and numerous phone calls. I guess my message is this: Amazon doesn't give a damn about it's customers. They have waay too much power over how we live our lives via that spy named Alexa. They have increased the price of Prime membership by $20. I will not be renewing. I'm going to give away my 8 Fire sticks and replace them with Roku sticks and purchase only Roku tv's in the future. As for all my blink cameras, echo shows, and echo dots, they'll be included in my next yard sale!

I was a little bit sceptical because it was so cheap, not just that but I had never heard of the company before! It's very light weight and small, the usb cord that it comes with has a different end than other portable hard drives I've used so don't lose the cord! Other than that I have no complaints, I bought it just to install Ark on (that game is a hog when it comes to space needed) and it's done it's job well. I will definitely buy from this company again, as it gave me great value for my money.

The image quality is pretty low, but not much worst than what my 2019 Jetta has. The bezel feel good and strong, but doesn't fit anywhere near as good as factory. It has gaps and you will need to put hot glue or something under the bottom tabs to lift up the bezel so the top tabs will lock in place. Hot glue seems to hold to this plastic really well. Make sure to still leave enough of the tabs poking out to still sit in the wholes. It comes with more than enough wire to do the job on my 03 GMC 2500hd 4 door. I also had to twist the camera to get a straighter image. It's still not 100% straight. But not off by much now and I can get it straightened out. Also the cover I got was smooth, no texture. So it doesn't match factory.

The dongle for this wireless mouse was packed deep inside the mechanism. I searched fruitlessly for it for 5 hours. Finally one of the maintenance staff for my locked-down senior residence facility came to my apartment, located it, and got it operating. IT SHOULD NOT BE A TWO PERSON JOB TO INSTALL A MOUSE! Nowhere in the brief installation directions did it show the dongle hidden in the mechanism.

I've used FitBit Alta HR for years. Decided to start running more, wanted something to track my actual distance, not just number of steps. The look of the Garmin is more masculine than my FitBit. I had many different colored bands and the smaller face gives it a more delicate look. That said, I didn't buy the Garmin for the look. I think the GPS tracking on the Garmin is great. I love that it buzzes me at each mile. But the Garmin is stupid. Unlike the Alta, it does not recognize activity on it's own - if I start running, but I don't hit the tracking button, Garmin doesn't believe running is happening. The Alta was smart enough to figure out what was happening, and I'm still adjusting to having to tell the tracker what I'm up to. In fact, I started a run the other day and missed the last of like four clicks you have to do to tell the Garmin I was running and after half a mile realized it hadn't started tracking me yet. Very frustrating. I also miss the entirely silent buzz of the Alta alarm waking me in the morning. Before purchase, I swore I read the Garmin had a silent alarm also, but mine buzzes me awake. Not ideal when I'm trying to get up and let my husband and dogs keep sleeping. All in all, the tracker is good. My issues are largely due to the adjustment from another type of tracker to this one. I'm still on the fence about if I want to use both for unique purposes or another option.

After getting tired of the cost of disposable batteries for my keyless front door lock I spent a fair bit of time researching rechargeables. The EBL's were very highly rated, were higher capacity at a reasonable price - not the most expensive but far from the cheapest. Before using I did a full charge overnight. From the first real use I noticed problems. They batteries have just a hair bigger diameter then standard AA's and were very hard to install into the holder. Once installed they were so tight the spring would not push the battery into the right spot to make contact with both the negative and positive terminals - I pushed them into place. I accepted this thinking I would get good life - not true. Not only was the life less then half of the disposables they went from working to dead with no warning. The lock has a low voltage warning light that never came on - they were just dead. I would expect this from lithium batteries (I have several lithium power tools that are full speed one trigger pull to dead the next) but not from NIMH. After the first set died (luckily I could get in via the garage door) I tried the 2nd set (also fully charged at purchase and stored in supplied plastic storage box) - again hard to install and they were totally dead. I went back disposables and will look at other brands - I DO NOT RECOMMAND THESE.

We tried plugging it into my husbands laptop and it still wouldn't work. There is a website listed on the packaging, but the entire site is in Chinese, not English. We tried to troubleshoot it on Amazon and that wouldn't work. Do not purchase this item. Now I have to go through the trouble of returning it in order to get a refund. I also had to order a new external hard drive. BUYER BEWARE! THIS IS ABSOLUTE JUNK!

I purchased this for my new macbook retina. Big mistake. The adhesive wasn't good so in the process of me trying to apply pressure to have the cover stick to the screen, it cracked the retina display. I will now need to take it to apple and pay hundreds of dollars to have them replace the retina. I will not be purchasing this again.

I always wanted a stylus phone. Put the status phones was so pricey that I never thought of buying one. When I saw this on sale on Amazon I grabbed it. The best smartphone I'm using so far. I have used Samsung Google and Apple phones earlier which are good but they are too pricey. I am been using this for more than 3 months now. Moving forward I will stick on to the Motorola brand. I think they are priced very well for what they are.

Not gonna lie, installing this thing SUUUUUUUCCCCCCKKKKKKKSSSSSS. Every negative review on here harping about the “3rd time’s the charm!” is spot on. You’re not buying 3 of these...you’re buying 1 well-installed one. If that. Here’s the thing. It’s just like every other screen protector you’ve ever installed...but bigger (unless you put one on an iMac I guess). Bigger in two ways. Bigger than the last one you installed and bigger than it really should be. It’s almost exactly the same size as the screen itself...but not exactly the same shape. The result is that even if you get it installed correctly, the edges will touch the rubber gasket on the top case of the MacBook ever so slightly, making it fail to properly adhere to the screen. I suppose you can install it exactly perfect and this won’t happen, but I don’t think you’re going to install it that well. So while I was able to get all of the bubbles out of the field of the screen protector, the edges had raised areas with small bubbles that annoyed the ever-loving you-know-what out of me. That said, my computer was stolen from my truck last week and I’m buying 3 more for it’s replacement. So I can’t give it a 5 since it’s such a finnicky PITA, but I also can’t give it a 1 since I’m buying 3 (really one) more. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
The cords are diable yet very flexible. They are easy to use and work well with my iPhone. Good quality for a good price.
one of the earbuds stopped working after two months. This is so shameful and I seem to not be able to get any refund for it cos they were expensive.

review_text: I have been using TP link routers for several generations and I guess I'm just used to fundamental features working. I went for speed here and I failed. Just like the team at Asus did when they released thig garbage router, something people have had over a decade to figure out, and it can't even keep the SSID broadcasting on the network. It takes hours or frustrating troubleshooting to get it back online. Devices disconnect, Google home devices flip out and just forget that network existed and it takes hours to get everything back online. Yet some devices just keep on trucking. It's bonkers. I hate this router. I want to kick this router through a window. Don't buy it.

What am I supposed to do with these?! There were no instructions, no adhesive… just pads? I ordered for the S7’s I own. review_text: Took me 15 minutes from start to finish. Had google WiFi I bought back in 2016 that started to just get slow. Used the same WiFi name and password from last mesh I had and everything synced up within seconds. I pay for 200/200 mbps from my isp and in my worst spot of the house I am getting about 140/150 download speed. Very happy with that speed! I do have a few WiFi 6 devices and they seem to be getting me about 190 within 20 feet of node. I really wanted to get the Amazon WiFi 6 nodes that just came out because of Black Friday discount but these to be honest I can’t wait over a month for them to be back in stock. The price was almost the same anyway and these do a great job. Would highly recommend to anyone that wants access to fast internet speeds with WiFi 6. Oh and the other thing I love is the settings that they let you access through the app and the web portal. Much better than google WiFi in my opinion. EDIT: So after about a month I had to return this and get a different product. Mainly because I started having issues pulling up certain websites. In order to confirm that it was the router I would turn off my WIFI and try to access the sites via my cellphone data and it would get me to the websites. So rather than try to go about troubleshooting it for hours on the phone with someone in another country I decided to return it and get TAOTRONICS mesh system which was more than half the price of this unit. The great news is that the taotronics router has worked out great and have had no issues. Glad it messed up on me in the end because it saved me like $300.

I had hoped that these band’s were slimmer than the black band that came with my Fitbit, but although they taper (and not very much) they are still very chunky for a women. The dressier band I purchased was more delicate but too delicate for daily wear.

We bought this because we were tired of paying Comcast every month to rent their router. You save so much money having your own! My wife was able to install and have this up and running within 15 minutes. Easy set up, quick installation and easy to follow instructions. Highly recommend!!

Having read good reviews about these earbuds across social media I purchased a pair to replace my old Anker earbuds, which had literally fallen apart. I received the Bose earbuds on the Monday and all seemed good - excellent acoustics and a powerful but crystal clear sound. However the following day I noticed the sound cutting out, leading to an uneven listening experience. After re-charging the earbuds I noticed there was no sound coming out of the right earbud. After consulting the troubleshooting page on the Bose web page I thought I’d resolved the issue but again the sound kept momentarily cutting out. The problem is not with my hardware - I primarily use my I-pad to listen to music and sound issues have never been a problem before with any earbuds that I have used. For the price paid (£219). I’ve decided not to risk it and to return the earbuds to Amazon. Very disappointed with this purchase and will look at alternative brands such as Technics, Cambridge Audio etc.

review_text: I was one of the unlucky ones who couldn't get the DVD player to work. I tried it using several different DVD's, old and new. I thoroughly tested it on 2 different TV's and kept getting an onscreen message, "ERROR DISC". I'm returning the item. To clarify, it's the Panasonic DVD-S700.

This was purchased to write a novel on the go, paired with my iPhone. It was in place of getting a laptop or tablet to write on. For $20, I didn't expect much, so was completely happy when the Bluetooth worked right away, and has never failed. Also, as a writer, keyboard feel is important. While it's no mechanical keyboard, it again exceeded what I expected. It's very comfortable, and the keys are easy to hit even with my meat sausage fingers. It's heavier than expected, probably from the battery. This means it's rock solid when typing, even when really cruising at 60+wpm. My iPhone Max fits well into the slot even with a case. It does not have an ergonomic stand (most keyboards have something that flips out on the bottom to raise the keyboard). However, again for $20, I can forgive this missing feature. Bottom line, you're getting more than you pay for with this. It far exceeds what a cheap keyboard should be.

We have 8 of these cameras on our construction sites. We use the EIOT sim cards with 24GB of data. No one can tell us what the issue is because these never work consistently. I thought maybe we were burning through the data ($60 twice a month for each camera $960/mo to run these....crazy!) so I shut off all of the auto recording that was triggered by motion during the working hours of the day. We have theft outside of those hours so it is supposed to pick that up. EIOT resets their SIM cards (but they are overseas so you only get one interaction/day which is infuriating) and they work for a day or two. So, I email Reolink support....again... They also seem to use overseas people so you can't ever get anything solved in a reasonable amount of time. (Also one interaction/day) I get all companies are trying to save money but 1. It's terrible customer service. 2. It would be a really good idea to offer those jobs to Americans (or whatever country that camera is sold in....the job stays in the same country as the camera). They don't give any good reasons or things to try either. We're so busy and I don't have time to deal with this daily, sooooo.....all that to say.....Would def not buy these again. Huge pain in the butt on all fronts, not to mention way too expensive to keep running.

I bought this hard drive to replace an older one, not an ADATA, that had out-lived it's usefulness in storage size. The 4 Terabyte storage capacity and extreme ruggedness sounds awesome a first blush, but come to find out 4 Terabytes are useless if the only thing rugged is the case. I received this drive in November of 2020 and it's now a brick as of January of 2021. I've spent the last 3 months backing up music, videos, pictures, data, cell phones, and practically anything important to any household. The drive itself has been lightly used, and mostly only written to. It's been safely tucked away in my office and in no way physically abused. After using it one evening at my sisters house to move family photos, on the next occasion I plugged it in and it gave me the error code "fatal device hardware error" which in turn means something is physically wrong with the drive. Upon calling ADATA, they implied that they "may" exchange the damaged drive for a new one under warranty, but in no way will be helpful in covering the cost of data recovery. The guy at ADATA asked me if I had my data backed up somewhere, and I was like yeah, on your POS drive. I know all products are hit & miss, but this is my experience with ADATA, buyer beware... Followup: So after contacting ADATA's preferred data recovery service, I was informed that any data recovered would start at $700 and only escalate from there into the thousands. So I reached back out to ADATA customer service which ended up being a complete waste of time and was basically told to go pound sand because they're only responsible for the hardware. ADATA may as well fire their whole customer service department and go automated because I was repeatedly told the same thing and promptly hung up on, like an automated service! The actual drivers for the unit I received are dated for the year 2006, so they may just be shoving old drives in shiny cases and selling them at profit. I will hire my own tech crew to crack this drive, and if this is the case, they will hear from my lawyers. My advice at this point is to steer clear of ADATA products, and don't expect any real help from this company should something go wrong. In Conclusion: instead of sending the drive back to ADATA, so they can do their investigation to decide whether the damage to the drive is covered under warranty in order to replace or refuse to replace the drive, I decided to have my own computer shop F1 Systems investigate the drive. When Alex removed the drive from the case, the drive was not an ADATA drive, but a Seagate drive! Classic bait and switch scam! If I had wanted a Seagate hard drive, I would have purchased a Seagate drive. Although the drive was damaged beyond practical data recovery without spending thousands at a data recovery agency at least I now know I’ll never purchase another ADATA product again. Fortunately, after speaking with an Amazon customer service representative and presenting these facts, they were nice enough to give me a refund on this albatross, but I’ve still lost 3 Terabytes of data permanently.

Here are concerns after using those for tow months: (-) When there is a light wind while walking outside, there is a strong humming noise. This seems to be caused by wind making noise in the microphone on polished surface of touch pods. Please note that without EarPods, you can't hear the wind - it is a nice Northern California breeze, not a heavy wind. (-) The price is high for the sound quality and noise issues Possible solutions: (1) If you would wear a small piece of fabric over your ear, something like a small sock, it would reduce the noise. That is how noise is reduced on high-end microphones. Of course, I do not recommend waring ear-socks. (2) If the earbuds are made with unpolished or textured surface for the touch pad, that may reduce the noise. Finally, would I recommend these EarPods? If you are using them mostly in closed spaces, it may work for you. If you run, or use them while walking or biking, forget it.

I decided to purchase the Magnetic Wireless Charger as I was looking for a reliable and compact charging solution for my frequent travels. The idea of having a 3-in-1 charger that could handle my iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods all at once was incredibly appealing, especially with the convenience of a foldable design.From the moment I unboxed it, I was impressed with the build quality. The aluminum finish gives it a sleek and sturdy feel, much better than the plastic alternatives I’ve used before. The magnetic alignment for my iPhone is spot on, ensuring that my phone snaps into place effortlessly and starts charging immediately. It's compatible with MagSafe, which means my iPhone 15 stays secure even if I accidentally bump the table.The foldable design is truly a blessing for someone who travels as much as I do. It folds down to a compact size, making it easy to slip into the included carrying case along with the 18W adapter. The case keeps everything organized and protected, so I never have to worry about tangled cables or damaged ports.Charging performance has been solid across all my devices. My iPhone charges quickly and consistently, and my Apple Watch and AirPods are always ready to go in the morning. The fact that it can handle all three devices simultaneously without a hitch is fantastic. It simplifies my nighttime routine, as I no longer need multiple chargers cluttering my bedside table.However, there are a few areas where it could be improved. Firstly, the charging pad for the Apple Watch feels a bit flimsy compared to the rest of the unit. It works fine, but I feel like it could be sturdier. Secondly, while the foldable design is great for travel, it sometimes feels a bit awkward to set up and position all the devices perfectly. It takes a bit of fiddling to get everything aligned just right, especially if you’re in a hurry.Lastly, the charger tends to get a bit warm when all three devices are charging at the same time. It's not alarmingly hot, but it's something to be mindful of, especially if you’re leaving it on a surface that doesn’t dissipate heat well.Overall, the Magnetic Wireless Charger has been a great addition to my travel gear. It has made charging my Apple devices much more convenient, and its compact, foldable design is perfect for packing light. Despite a few minor quirks, it delivers solid performance and is a reliable companion for anyone with multiple Apple gadgets.

This router only have 128 megabyte storage for the entire operating system. As soon as you install AdGuard you basically run out of space and the unit starts becoming unstable. This is got to be one of the stupidest design I have ever seen in my life. How can you make a device that gives you open source freedom to do whatever you want and then put a max 128 MB capacity into it? You have to be extremely dumb to do something like this. I inserted a USB 3.0 flash drive (ext4) and mounted it using fstab, then installed ADGuard to it which seems to work however it doesn't survive reboot. Up on reboot the USB flash storage will mount again however, there is a race condition which makes AdGuard crash and fails to start up. Google search will tell you how to do this with a USB flash drive in another way however those instructions are no longer valid due to the firmware update. With AdGuard if you have over 15 computers this router will overheat and freeze. The CPU just doesn't have proper cooling to handle 15 computers while blocking ads. In the router you have list of other apps that you can install but it's all useless due to the limited 40 mb space free. Don't bother buying this and instead buy the travel router of this version which has a microSD slot, that seems to work much better and be much more stable. For your home main router I wouldn't recommend this brand at all. They over price for a device that is not even 1/4 of $25 raspberry pi.

review_text: I've been using the (much more expensive) Nikon D4 for my food photography since 2013, but as soon as this camera was announced, I realized it would be much better suited for what I do - high frame rates and high ISO performance just aren't that important to me. Now I've finally bought it! Generally, I hate straight-out-of-the-box reviews where folks have barely used the product, but I've learned enough in five days of shooting that I feel confident sharing some well-informed first impressions. I'll update later if anything changes. Here's what I love about this camera: - Between the massive image size and the (about damned time) removal of the low-pass filter, image quality and detail is dazzling. Boggles my mind that other cameras have a filter that blurs detail to avoid moire. You can fix moire in Photoshop, but Photoshop can't reclaim the detail lost because of that filter. - The focus shift function. I do a ton of focus stacking, and this camera automates (and perfects) the process of acquiring a series of shots that, when combined in Photoshop, capture everything in focus. I shoot stacks in about 1/10th the time now, which is really important for food - the longer you shoot, the more greens wilt and the more sauces congeal. - Wifi. About time, Nikon! And amazingly, I have actually gotten the SnapBridge app to work, though it's clear from reviews that most people have had a lot of trouble with it. The CamRanger I used for my D4 had more functionality than SnapBridge (I especially miss the histogram), but the live view quality is a LOT better in SnapBridge, and viewing photos is a little easier. For what I need, it's adequate. - Roll and pitch indicators in the viewfinder, not just in liveview. - Touchscreen makes menus easier to navigate (and it's a LOT easier to "type" in it now, though a QWERTY keyboard would've made that a little easier) Here's what I don't love: -EN-EL15 battery. Really, Nikon - you give a serious camera that takes 50MB photos the same battery that my old D40X and Nikon1 use? That is NUTS. An impressive beast like this needs an impressive battery, like the EN-EL18. Yes, I know you can accessorize to use that battery, which I will probably end up doing, but the D850 should be built to use that battery right out of the gate. -No built-in bottom grip for vertical shooting. Again, this is an impressive camera for serious photographers; it's silly that I should have to pay extra to add a grip. I shoot a lot of verts, so I'm sure I'll end up adding the grip (Vello for $100, not Nikon for ***$400*** - wtf?), but I shouldn't have to. Obviously both of these items would have added to the cost, but I gladly would have paid another $500 for this camera to have those features built in. - Settings banks, and I'm going to just quote Ken Rockwell on this because he says it well: "No camera-state presets, just the same clumsy 'settings banks' Nikon has used since 2003. The lesser cameras (D750 and down) are better here as they have two mode-dial settings, U1 and U2, that let us recall complete sets of camera settings with just one click." The settings banks just recall the camera the last way you used it, so you have to be extra careful to check whether you changed an important setting on your last shoot in that settings bank. - For men only. Not really, but I'm still irritated as hell at Nikon for their 2017 publicity stunt for this model: sending 32 pro photogs across Japan to test the camera, but not including a single female photog among them. I've been a journalist since 1988 and I did not have one single newspaper job where there weren't a TON of female photographers. Nikon's oversight was stupid and insulting; I hope they never do that again.

review_text: Upon opening the box I have to admit that the charger unit looks very nice. You are presented with a nice softshell zippered carry case. Inside tha case is the charger unit, a mains plug, a USB charging lead and a small instruction booklet. Taking the charger unit out of it plastic wrap and the unit looks and feels top quality.It all goes downhill after that.To open up the unit for use you need to pull on a small (ugly looking) plastic tag marked "Pull Up" . It needs a really firm pull on this tag to make the base of the unit reveal itself. Once youve done that you can then just use your fingers to move the upper part of the charger into position (magsafe phone charger).I have to admit that once the unit has been 'assembled' like this it does look good - until you then want to use the Watch charger part of this item.The Watch charging pad is secreted within the base of the unit. You have to pull on another tab - this time a tiny orange cloured fibery tab. Its a devils own job to get you finger nails around this tiny tab to get enough grip on it to pull out the Watch charging pad. To be honest its a right P.I.T.A. I suspect people will get frustrated by this and simply lever the pad out with something like the end of a knife!Once yo've finally managed to extract this pad from the bottom of the unit you then insert it into a the USB C port marked 'Watch' which is located on the bottom hinge of the unit. And once inserted it does detract from the looks of the unit.OK so now with everything 'erected' I tried out the charger.The phone is gripped well by the magnetism of the magsafe pad and it is able to be held in both portrait and landscape positions. Charging took place as expected. The Airpods charged too although I had to be very precise with placing the Airpods on the charging pad as the sweet spot position for charging to engage is tiny.The Watch charger pad is Naff. The magnetism holding the watch to the pad is poorBased on my experience would I recommend this charger? No I would not.The plastic "Pull Up" tab is ugly and will surely split/break before too long. The absolute Faff when getting the watch pad out of the base of the unit will annoy many people.

review_text: For the techie in your life who has to have the biggest and the baddest. You’ve got it. There are more expensive options that get close but do not rival the wattage, ports, and form factor of this charger and for the money — I feel it’s a justifiable purchase. Prior to receiving this charger I was using a 65W Targus USB-C Laptop Charger that I got for too good a deal back in the day. Upgrading to this charging has allowed myself greater flexibility in not needing to worry about stress incurred from the ever changing plans of which cannot be predicted in everyday life. Thus, having a charger that is on the bleeding edge of performance in term’s of the capability of USB-C cables(maxes at 100W), the USB-C technology(maxes at 100W)and products on the market right now of which support USB-C is great. The form factor is nifty on this charger if you knowingly understand that due to its mass — this charger may occasionally fall out of a wall socket, to remedy this just use a short extension cord and your golden. The ports perform to the spec stated and I have for those readers of whom this may interest done my own standalone testing with this product with my own iPad Pro 11 inch and here are my results: Time to 80%: 65 minutes Time to 100%: 105 minutes Percentage at 30 minutes: 45% A few things to note would be that: The threshold to my understand in which fast charging occurs is from 0-80% battery life for compatible devices. My iPad Pro can support up to 96W according to Apple’s documentation. The threshold beyond 80% should back the charging wattage down to 12W max bringing it in line with many other non fast charging chargers and thus the discrepancy between the time in which the battery attains 80% and the time spent getting it to 100% lies in the fact that it is no longer fast charging. In conclusion, I would buy this charger again should it perform well in the long run and would have no problem or doubts about recommending this charger to others of which are in the market for currently in my humble opinion; one of the best deals you can get for the highest wattage chargers out on the market at this very moment.

I would give this 1 star, however AsRock had prompt support. his was intended to be an upgrade for an aging system. The issues: 1. My main issue with the motherboard is that it would not consistently see or boot from multiple flash drives for Unraid. The first flash drive was my existing Unraid install, the other was a fresh install. The only way to get it to boot to Unraid was to do a hard reboot (power cycle at power supply). Faulty or bad bios firmware, I returned this board.. 2. This mother board does not obey the AMD socket exclusion zone and oriented 90* from normal. Therefore any decent heatsink, like the Noctua's 3u NH-D9L (a) is not oriented to push air front to back (b) overhangs the first DDR4 slot. 3. Only has a USB3 internal header. This is very odd as the x470 chipset has multiple USB 2.0 connection provisions. I use a USB 2.0 internal header adapter to install my Unraid flash drive onto. 4. Why micro ATX? At 250 usd its not for cost savings. Had full ATX been chosen the first PCIE slot could have been moved down 1 slot giving plenty of room to have the RAM at the top of the board and give the AM4 socket the clearance it needs for even compact 3u coolers from Noctua. The factory AMD heat sink would not work on the board with either of the channel A slots with ram. AsRock, if your reading. Please address the above and continue produce motherboards with IPMI for non server cpus. There are many of us looking to do pro-sumer tech at home and small office.
