I got this because my outdoor channel master, and televes antenna were getting multipath. So I got this panel antenna to use indoors, on my window. It helps. I combined this antenna with a reverse splitter and my outdoor antenna. I left it UN-AMPLIFIED. That, for me just added noise to the signal. I'm trying to get a station about 42 miles away, with a 57kW ERP (Power output). It's not the best indoor antenna. I would say get a good set of rabbit ears, and UHF loop if you are seeking the BEST signal. Don't amplify if indoors. The antenna will just pick up every stray RF signal inside, plus the less than RG-6 cable (permanently attached), isn't shielded enough I'm sure. It's probably stranded copper wire inside the cable. These antennas have use. As long as you keep physics, and expectations in mind. This says it works for FM, I can say that I've heard most of these panel antennas only have UHF elements. But it did ok with my Pioneer car radio (modified for indoor use).

review_text: Empecemos por decir que lo que ofrece el producto es lo que vas a obtener ni mas ni menos. Ahora indaguemos mas en lo tecnico y por lo cual me ha decepcionado un poco el sistema. Este no es un sistema de vigilancia de video es mas en mi opinión un sistema de alarma de movimiento con capacidad de grabar el evento que activo la señal de alarma, aunque muchas veces ese video termina por frustrarte mas y a continuación explico el porque El sistema solo puede grabar entre 5 seg y 60 seg de grabación y aunque a veces 60seg es mucho tiempo, tiene una opción que permite parar el video antes si el movimiento se detiene, pero aca es donde comienza el problema en realidad, si activas esta opción, el sistema tiene una contra que la camara al desactivarse tarda 10 seg en volver a estar lista para registrar otra alerta lo cual hace que a veces pierdas información valiosa en cuanto a seguridad, si el movimiento para y luego se reactiva mientras la camara esta en el reposo de los 10seg, la camara no registrara nada en video y si el intruso sale fuera del rango de detección ya no podrás saber que paso luego, incluso si el movimiento llegar a seguir después de los 60seg max de grabación por alerta, la camara entraría en ese mismo tiempo de descanso de 10seg. Aunque las alertas en la app son muy rápidas este Tiempo se puede ver afectado si la opción de alertas rápidas no esta activada, ya que esta viene desactivada por defecto y si no se activa en cada camara puedes tener unas que te avisen y otras que las notificaciones llegue siempre tarde o después que ya se detecto el movimiento. En resumen si lo que quieres es un sistema de alerta de movimiento o cercanía este es el sistema que debería comprar pero si quieres un sistema de vigilancia de video busca otras opciones. Dentro de amazon hay varias opciones de camara ptz wifi con grabación continua, detección de movimiento, alarma sonora y audio doble vía que trabaja muy similar a este sistema y con una memoria de 32gb tienes hasta 4 dias de grabación continua y son mas económicos, aunque no son tan excelentes como este en visión de video en vivo o revisando archivos de alarma te serán mas útiles si lo que buscas es un sistema cctv, por lo menos en mi opinión. Postdata aun no se como funciona el sistema sin la membresía a Blink plus aun estoy dentro de la prueba gratis y aunque ya tengo todo el sistema para grabación local pronto volveré con mi opinión de como se porta el sistema una ves no tengas el soporte de Blink Plus. -------------------------------------------------------- Let's start by saying that what the product offers is what you are going to get, no more, no less. The product is completely wireless, giving you the advantage of a quick clean installation without wires at a glance. The remote connection from the cell phone through the app is great and very fluid, when you want to watch the videos, although the connection with my echo show 5 device has been almost impossible for voice control and for live viewing it has a delay quite unpleasant. The duration of the batteries is excellent, I have 5 cameras installed and one of them is at the entrance of the residential complex, which means that every day there are 70 average movement notifications with their respective videos and even after a month it says that it is over 70% life batteries. Notifications are almost in real time, max about 10 to 15 seconds after motion detection, the notification arrives on the mobile app, but the connection with alexa in my case has been terrible and quite depressing because I decided on the right product for that function and I have not been able to solve the constant errors between alexa and the blink skill. Now let's dig deeper into the technical and for which the system has disappointed me a bit. This is not a video surveillance system, it is more in my opinion a motion alarm system with the ability to record the event that activated the alarm signal, although many times that video ends up frustrating you more and I will explain why below. The system can only record between 5sec and 60sec of recording and although sometimes 60sec is a long time, it has an option that allows you to stop the video earlier if the movement stops, but this is where the problem really starts, if you activate this option, the system has a counter that when the camera is deactivated, it takes 10 seconds to be ready again to record another alert, which sometimes means that you lose valuable information regarding security, if the movement stops and then reactivates while the camera is At rest for 10 seconds, the camera will not record anything on video and if the intruder goes out of the detection range, you will no longer be able to know what happened next, even if the movement continues after the maximum 60 seconds of recording by alert, the camera would enter that same rest time of 10sec. Although the alerts in the app are very fast, this Time can be affected if the quick alerts option is not activated, since it is deactivated by default and if it is not activated in each camera you can have some that notify you and others that Notifications always arrive late or after motion has already been detected. No me In short, if what you want is a movement or proximity alert system, this is the system you should buy, but if you want a video surveillance system, look for other options. Within amazon there are several wifi ptz camera options with continuous recording, motion detection, sound alarm and two-way audio and lights that works very similar to this system and with a 32gb memory you have up to 4 days of continuous recording and they are cheaper, although They are not as excellent as this one in viewing live video or reviewing alarm files. They will be more useful if you are looking for a cctv system, at least in my opinion. Postscript I still don't know how the system works without Blink plus membership I'm still in the free trial and although I already have the entire system for local recording I'll soon come back with my opinion on how the system behaves once you don't have Blink support Plus.

Picked a set of these up to replace my initially-amazing-but-ultimately-hot-mess Netgear XR500 router (which itself replaced my brilliant workhorse but too-slow-for-my-needs Netgear R7000) after eyeballing them for nearly a year. Setting the XT8 units up was surprisingly simple, even though the instructions lacked a bit of detail. Plugged them both in, chose one of them to plug into my modem, downloaded the Netgear app, chose the appropriate model in said app, and away I went. Only potentially confusing point was where it insisted on asking me about IP assignment method...I selected DHCP, which should have been the default anyway. It also asked me if I wanted a unified network name across the 2.4 and 5Ghz bands...I kept them separate with their own unique names to stay consistent with my original setup. This is a nice option that some modern routers inexplicably do not offer, the lack of which can cause some older 2.4-only devices to have trouble connecting. Within a few minutes the units were linked and the two networks were visible. I initially couldn't browse the internet, but a quick modem reboot solved that...not an unexpected step at all. After that, everything was a breeze. I had kept my network names and passwords the same as before, and every device in my house had no trouble whatsoever immediately communicating with the XT8s, and I hadn't even yet moved the satellite XT8 out of the same room as the main router XT8. I then moved the satellite XT8 to my basement, a place where my wifi speeds were only around 50Mbps of an available 400Mbps on either wifi band with my previous router. I was worried that due to the distance/walls/floors between the satellite and the main router, I'd see a similar drop-off if I let the units communicate wireless using the wireless backhaul (vs. running ethernet cable between them). I'd also had terrible luck with range extenders in this room. But with the XT8s? Nope. I ran Speedtest and got speeds of over 100Mbps on the 2.4Ghz channel, and over 350Mbps on the 5Ghz channel. Impressive. I thought about plugging my PS5 into one of the XT8's ethernet ports, but the performance on wifi is so good, with such low latency, that I've had no reason to do so (the PS5 is a Wi-Fi 6 capable device, as is the XT8, so no surprise there really). As for devices that are upstairs and close to the main router XT8, unsurprisingly they're seeing almost every bit of my ISP total bandwidth. I am pretty flabbergasted at the performance thus far. When I received them, I was on the verge of returning them on the spot after further research made me doubt their capabilities, especially with regards to firmware update issues. I updated the firmware and had no problems. I'm glad I gave these a shot. I haven't even had reason to need to try their QoS functionality. I know that routers can take time to reveal their warts. My XR500 was a case study in such frustration. I'll certainly be leery of major firmware updates to these and will likely wait for inevitable followup patches to major releases before applying. But so far these XT8s have been a revelation. I've had them up for a week now without a single drop or incident since initial setup. I'll update this review as time goes by. Pros: -Fast fast faaaaaaaaaaast, even when the satellite XT8 is placed in a seemingly poor location -Unobtrusive, subdued physical design -FAST -Easy setup -Seriously...SO FAST... Cons: -App could be a little more intuitive -Packed-in documentation could be better -Satellite takes a few minutes to sync-up when plugged in -Supposed issues with firmware updates, but I've had none thus far and will be cautious UPDATE 2/3/2023: No issues thus far. I have heard issues regarding certain firmware updates, so I never update the firmware until I've read up on user experiences with them, and even then there's not much reason to unless they address something truly necessary. These have been absolutely awesome.

I've tried a few of the low cost security cameras around including ones by blink, ring and wyze and they all fell short in some way in terms of annoying detection issues or app problems. So I wasn't looking forward to the Eufy camera experience especially after reading some of the complaints here in the reviews. Well, I've only had it a day, but so far I think this Eufy camera is excellent, even taking the low price out of consideration. The camera is made by Anker, a company that is known for making power banks and chargers. First off, it does offer 2fa security by email and phone to secure the account. It also lets you choose the server you want it to interact with. The video image quality and sound quality is very good. The night vision on it is black and white but it has good clarity. So far detection is flawless. It can detect sounds as well as motions. It is easy to disable detection or turn off the camera completely. Updating the firmware was also simple The Eufy securiy app from the Apple app store is nice and works well. I especially like that you don't need to buy some plan to see or download your videos. They do offer a cloud plan for $2.99 a month, which I guess could be useful, but you don't need it. I just put a 32gb memory card in it and it works fine. I can even download the videos to the photos app on my iPhone. The head of the camera swivels so you can easily position it. You can turn off the indicator light in the settings. I unplugged it once from power and thought it might be a hassle to reconnect it. Nope. Plugged it back in and it reconnected all by itself. To top it off, it's also a nice looking camea. In my view, so far at least, this is a far superior product compared to other similar security cameras offered here.

review_text: I tried to connect to an ultrawide monitor (3440x1440). I was only able to get a lower resolution via HDMI port. Use of the Digital Display Port resulted in the correct resolution but a flickering display. Final feedback was that the computer is not able drive this resolution, without any suggestion to solve this other than to buy a new & better computer. Also contacted Asus via e-mail and received a reply stating it is possible to run requested resolution, with suggestion to update bios and run recovery Windows 10. Given the conflicting messaging I didn't bother trying that and bought a graphics card (GPU). This computer doesn't take standard size, you need to order a "low profile" version. Also, power is very limited and I couldn't find an additional power-cable from the PSU that most video cards require. I ended up buying a GT1030 (buy one with DDR5 memory, same price and twice as fast as DDR4 version) for ~$80 as they are very low power (don't need power cable) and available in slim format. Its a very low-end card, so don't expect to use it for the latest games, but it does display 3440x1440 without problem. My understanding is that the integrated chip should be able to drive this resolution, so not sure what my problem was. Good price for te system, but -1 star for low performance in the graphics domain and another -1 for poor customer support.

We have the RBR50 that we used for 3 years. We had no issues with it. When we upgraded our internet service from 300Mbps cable to 1Gbps fiber we felt upgrading to the RBR850 would be beneficial. The first box arrived and it wasn’t in a protective box. Amazon just slapped a sticker on the Orbi box as if it was just pulled off the shelf. Looking back we should of refused it then. The average speeds on the RBR850 are around 560-600 Mbps down at 6’ from the router. That’s a 40% drop at 6’! This is also the same speeds as the RBR50! I spoke Netgear Support for weeks and their troubleshooting, changes, etc were fruitless. During this time of troubleshooting the Amazon return window closed. However, Amazon agreed to exchange it. The replacement Orbi RBR850 arrived and it was in a protective box this time. Once hooked up the speeds were unchanged. Frustrated I hooked up our old RBR50 and we are observing speeds the same as the RBR850. Hooking up a $1000 RBR850 to a 1Gbps connection and get the same speed as a $250 RBR50 hooked up to the same connection?! Unacceptable. The only advantage is the RBR850 will hold higher speeds at longer distances compared to the RBR50. But out of the box at 6’-12’ clear line of sight there’s no difference. At 6’ with a high end router you should see no more than a 20% drop.

This is another quality raspberry Pi case from Retroflag. It is similar to the previous GPi case but with some welcomed additions and changes. First, I love that they’ve added a rechargeable battery pack to this version. No longer do I have to go through batteries like an old Game Gear. Secondly, the much improved power of the CM4 lets me emulate more systems than before. The additional buttons on the face are helpful as well. The new screen was a much needed upgrade, especially when paired with the new power to run psp games. Unfortunately there are some catches. The L and R buttons are still just as difficult to use naturally as on the old case design. The lack of L2, R2 and a thumb stick also limits the playable systems. There are some QA issues that I hope get ironed out in the future, such as dead pixels on the screen. There isn’t too much support for this case out there yet, making troubleshooting issues more difficult. While the case supports a CM4 without WiFi or with eMMC storage, you don’t want to get these versions. Having no WiFi makes it incredibly hard to get set up, and having eMMC locks you out of using a micro SD, even if you’re not using the eMMC storage. And lastly, though not the fault of Retroflag, the CM4 is almost impossible to get right now. Even if you do happen to find one at a marked up price, it’s probably not the one you want. So this is a great upgrade to an already fantastic case, but I would recommend waiting for awhile before buying it. At the very least wait until you have the CM4 that you want to use in your hands (I recommend the CM4102000) before buying this case or you will have a bad experience. In the meantime, if you happen to have the original case, then consider getting an upgrade with the Pi Zero 2, which is about as powerful as a Pi 3.

I've tried a handful of switchers now and most of be pretty mediocre. They lack features, quality, or value. Thus far the PAC "intelligent" switcher has been the one I stuck with despite it's lack of actual intelligence. First let me say I am using the triggering wires, not the PAC interface, this all might be different if you are using as a whole system. My biggest complaint is the lack of configuration, not trigger speed like others have mentioned. The 1-2s to trigger my head unit is almost negligible because your mind and car are switching gears (sometimes literally) so you can learn to live with the slight initial delay. Instead I find the delayed de-trigger to be far more annoying. It seems to display the video just a touch longer than it actually needs to. Somewhere ~3s after I switch into drive before the reverse camera goes away. This makes me think I am still in reverse and I need to do a double take to make sure I am actually in drive. For my side view cameras, they have their own pulsed trigger handling, so left/right signaling makes the display stay on for ~5s after the turn signal is off. Again this is slightly distracting to have a video feed up when you might actually want your map so you can see any immediate action/direction after a turn. BrandMotion has an instant 2 input switcher which would work in my case (since sides count as 1 RCA for me), but it's even more basic for nearly the same price with no room for expansion. Their 6 input switcher has it all, but I cannot justify nearly double the cost. Once you get over $100 for this kind of device I start to expect more features and sadly that isn't going to happen unless you roll the dice on sketchy overseas electronics. At least PAC is a domestically recognized company.

I bought this 945 on Prime Day (nice sale!), as an upgrade to the 935 that I’ve been using for a little over 4 years. I probably don’t use even 20% of capabilities of these watches, but as a triathlete, I sure enjoy the data that they provide… and the 945 provides even more than the 935. Nice. The biggest things that I’ve noticed over my 935 are (again) the increased amount of data that this watch provides. I particularly like the significantly more detailed sleep tracking, as well as the ‘body battery’, which I find to be QUITE accurate for how I’m feeling at any given moment. Further, I’m especially loving that the heart rate sensor works in the water – not having to wear a heart rate strap when I’m swimming to get my heart data is wonderful! The bad stuff… the buttons. The buttons just suck. Where my 935 buttons are smooth with a nice, single tactile click, the buttons on the 945 feel coarse and grainy – and the top left button got mushy and actually stopped clicking at all within the first 30 days. Further, the bottom right button would kind of catch on the way in, then click – rather like a double click. I contacted Garmin support, and they were wonderful – though they did initially try to just tell me that this was just they way they felt on this new model now, and as long as they worked, everything was fine (but it wasn’t fine, because the buttons suck). Even so, at my request, they did offer to replace it, which was awesome. I received the replacement… and it’s better than the first one. All of the buttons click, though they are still rather grainy, and the top right has that double clicky feel to it – but it’s better. Not better than my 935, but still better. It will get a lot of use with me before the warranty runs out, so I’m just going to keep an eye on it. (Regarding those buttons, after a lot of reading, I found that the buttons were improved thru different revisions of the watch – currently on Rev. D, as stamped on the box. Both my first and replacement watch were Rev. D, so apparently, there are still issues within the revision.) My only other observation with this watch has been battery life. I’m an Ironman athlete, so I need a watch that will make it all the way thru a full IM race. I did a couple of fulls with my 935 with no issue – but when I began to watch battery life on this unit, I was doubtful whether it would make it thru a race – battery was dropping quickly, even with no GPS based activity. Then I remembered… I get a TON of notifications thru my phone, so that had my watch active a lot. I went into Garmin Connect and turned off ALL phone notifications, then just turned on the notifications for calls and texts (because that’s all I want to see on my watch)… and the battery life improved dramatically. Still too soon to make the final call, but I think it’s good now. Just something to be aware of. The long and short of it?... excellent watch with crummy buttons. If I hadn’t caught it on sale, I think I would’ve regretted the purchase, as I would’ve just gone straight for the 955 (which is current right now). However, if you find this watch for a nice price (like I did), it’s worth it… crummy buttons and all.

review_text: I had 3 old phones go bad on me in the last 6 months, and needed a new, affordable one. I've liked my Moto phones, and this had decent specs, so I went for it. I've had it for a week now. I'm loving the size and quality of the display. It's a little hard to use one handed, but the extra screen real estate is awesome. It's great when the keyboard is on the screen....much more room above it. I haven't used the camera a lot yet, but I took some really lovely sunset pictures and some macro shots (that was another selling point for me....I wanted to take pictures of small details in things I collect). The camera seems a LOT better than my past Motos. And the software has some fun options. And I've always loved the Moto twist to open the camera/chop to open flashlight gestures. I'm really happy that it came with 128GB of storage, and REALLY love that there's a microSD slot so I could just pop in my old card with tons of pictures/music/videos on it already. And it's great having the USB-C connection instead of the micro USB on my old dead phones. The stylus is just okay....nothing like the Wacom tech on my Samsung tablet. But it's kinda fun to color, etc. And better than a finger for photo editing, etc. The fingerprint reader has been working great. Seems much better than the one on my beloved dead Galaxy S7 Edge. I may edit this later to add things, but wanted to mention to another reviewer how to get the 3-button navigation he's used to. I did it myself when I got the phone, because I wanted the buttons, not the gestures. Go to Settings - System - Gestures - System Navigation and then choose 3 Button Navigation. Voila!

The only good first. E Zee Electronics who I bought the board from, offered to give me a refund even though I've had the board for a few months now. I told them brief details about the MSI support issues and they asked if I'd like a refund. They sent me a packing slip a day later. Very impressed with their customer service. Now for the bad. Built a brand new computer with this mobo with all new components. When adding another ssd (for data) after the initial build, I realized that I put my OS drive in second m2 slot which is PCI-e gen3. I swapped the OS drive to the primary which supports the Gen 4 PCI-e and turned the computer back on. It would not post or display anything on the screen. Opened a case with MSI support and besides telling me to update my bios (which it was), they had not much other help besides contact reseller or create an rma. I swapped the new data drive to the primary M2 slot and the OS back to the second M2 slot and the computer fired back up. Both OS and Data drives were recognized. I decided that I just wanted to use my new build and I would just leave it as is and not worry about the issue if it worked this way. Fast forward to at least once or twice a week for the next few months the Data drive would either not be present on startup or it would just start failing to read/write to the drive mid use. I would reboot the computer, it would hang up and I'd have to kill the power to it and turn it back on. And half the time it would not recognize the data drive for a few more reboot attempts. I got fed up and reinstalled windows finally even though it was a fresh install when I built the computer. That did not fix it. At this time I opened another case with MSI and they suggested to update the bios again...to a beta version. I said no I would not be doing that unless they could point to the release notes where it said it would fix this. They again told me to contact my reseller or rma the board. Oh and when you want to open an RMA case you can't do it through your existing case, they send you elsewhere to do it. Based on support alone I will not buy another MSI product. I replaced this board with an Asus and everything has been working since. Kicking myself for dealing with it for months.

I had used a Garmin Vivo fit II for years as my fitness tracker. It was a basic step counter that interfaced with my employers health monitoring. As a Registered Respiratory Therapist I wanted a fitness monitor that would do more. I was reluctant to spend big bucks for some of the fancier ones. So, I started looking at the Amazfit models. The one negative I can say is for step tracking it is slightly on the light side. I feel my Garmin device was more accurate. With the Amazfit you have to be swinging your arm to get a accurate count. The Amazfit does a good job on sleep tracking with slot of info in the app. The cardiac monitoring is very good and accurate. If you are looking for an actual cardiac tracing you will have to spend more. It does show if you are in warm up, fat buring, aerobic or anaerobic zone based on heart rate. The pulse odometer feature is surprisingly accurate. I have compared it with multiple hospital grade units and have been very satisfied. It took awhile to get the Alexa feature to even turn on and it still does not do much and I am not sure why? The app has a great deal of additional info. review_text: Purchased this USB extender on 4th-Sep-2021 and died 12th-Dec-2021. In life, it worked great, but in death it would only work for a while and then required that I reboot my computer. Now on 14th-Dec-2021 it refuses to work with my flash drive with or without rebooting. A 3 month lifespan is too short to justify the money I spent. I will explain will how the determination was made: Possible problems are bad computer USB port, or bad USB flash drive or this USB extender is bad). I used this approach: I took the questionable flash drive out of this USB port extender and plug it directly into an unused USB port of my computer--flash drive worked fine -- so now I know the flash drive and the previously used computer USB port are both good. Unplugged this USB extender from my computer and inserted the flash drive into that USB computer port that had previously been used for this USB extender -- the flash drive works in both USB computer ports. Plugged this USB extender into the other USB port (not the one that had been previously used with this USB extender) -- flash drive still working where this USB extender had been used. Move the flash drive back to this USB extender -- flash drive not working in this extender, again. (Also had same results with my 5T USB external hard drive.) My conclusion is that the problem moves with this USB extender. (No data was lost. Both of the storage devices I used for troubleshooting were simply not recognized when plug into this USB extender.) A three month lifespan is not good enough!!! It would have been better if it never worked, because Amazon would have refunded the purchase. I will make it a point to never buy this unreliable brand again, but I will buy from Amazon again.

I purchased one of these for my girlfriend for an early Christmas present. I was pretty happy she had spoken about purchasing a bit larger TV for her home and I was just the guy to make that happen. It’s always nice when you’re buying a present for yourself as well as your person. It’s pretty hard watching your team on a 40 inch Insignia when you have a beautiful 65 inch Samsung and an awesome sound system at home. I couldn’t let her do this on her own…Lol! She had some specific criteria about what she wanted even though she didn’t know I was going to do this for HER. 55 inch was as large as she would go and she doesn’t like “clutter”. We obviously need better sound than an old, crappy, no name soundbar as well so we’ll go for the whole show with the Echo Studio speakers and I had an Echo Sub still in the box I didn’t really use. She already had an Echo Show that she loves, so this should be a no brainer, right? The speakers had already been here for a week when the TV arrived Thursday I put them all under her tree before she got home from work. I wasn’t waiting until Christmas, the next game was on Sunday. The speakers were first that evening and they worked mostly as expected. My initial impressions were good, much better than my old Echo’s although speakers that size aren’t really in the same class as my four old Kef 104/2’s that I have loved since new back in ‘87. Much less “clutter” though and they really do sound pretty good. On Friday it was time for the initial setup of the TV and of course you have to un-pair the speakers in order to set up a “Home Theater”. That seems a bit over the top, these things are supposed to work together, right? Ok, step by step I guess. I get it set up and the sound is coming out of the speakers. We sit down with a beer and listen to some music and all is good. On Saturday morning, it’s time to get serious and down comes the old Insignia and the rest of the “clutter” and up goes the new TV. When I turn it on, there is no sound coming from the speakers. Hmm! I tried lots of commands to Alexa and nothing worked. Couldn’t find anything in the app or online to help. Between Friday night and Saturday morning I did one factory reset on the TV and many multiple un-pairing and re-pairing of the TV and the speakers. The only thing I found that would work for me was to go into settings and do a restart. The factory reset requires you to start over from the beginning but the restart at least keeps your settings. Cycling power alone doesn’t help. The biggest problem with the restart is it has to re-calibrate the Home Theater settings which takes about five minutes and part of that time will be without sound as well. This can’t be that hard. This should be one of the easiest TV’s ever made to set up and use. I have to be missing something but every time I ask Alexa to play music, the speakers won’t switch back to playing sound from the TV no matter what I tried. After I killed the whole morning messing with it, I had to leave so I got it back to the point it was usable with her Apple TV and I told her not to use the A word or it might quit working. Just leave the remote alone also. Saturday evening, I had the same results, couldn’t find any way to fix it. Watched A Star is Born on HBO Max on her Apple TV through this system. Very enjoyable…great movie. Sunday morning, I decided to search the internet for people who might have been having a similar problem but couldn’t find anything. It’s getting close to game time and I need it working. I probably should have just left it alone but I’m determined. I managed to break it one last time just before the game started so I un-paired everything and turned on the TV speaker because I didn’t have time to set it back up again. The TV speaker option isn’t available if you have it paired with the Home Theater, thanks Amazon. The TV speaker isn’t bad for a TV speaker but it’s not exactly what I paid for. Sunday evening, I decided I am probably going to have to send the TV back. I hate returning things but on top of the other problems, the menu is glitchy. At times it will slow down and get to the point of freezing completely. Cycling power at least fixes that temporarily. The TV updated to the latest software as soon as it connected to the internet so you wouldn’t think that would be a problem. It’s not like this tv hasn’t been out long enough to fix most of the bugs. Maybe I just got a bad one. Overall, I would say the picture is fine and when working the sound was great but I’ve never had this many problems with a TV out of the box. When you plug them in, they work. They might need some adjustments but they generally work as advertised. I’ve given it enough of my time this weekend to even think about more hours spent with tech support or waiting on software updates. Monday I purchased a Fire TV Cube and a different TV. Guess what…it worked correctly out of the box. The Apple TV will turn the whole system on when you hit the menu button on the apple remote and the sound plays on the Echo Studios. The Fire TV remote will control the Apple TV. If you hook your HDMI cable to ARC input on the TV, the sound from the TV will play from the Echo Studios also. The concept actually works really well when you pair a Fire TV with Echo Studio’s in a Home Theater setup. Too bad I ended up adding to the clutter. At least it’s pretty small. The Fire TV experience is good and I could probably eliminate the Apple TV but we have already downloaded all the apps she wants and have all the sign in information on it. Besides, we’re both used to and like the interface. I probably just got a bad TV. There are plenty of good reviews here. This one would have been fine hooked up to my system at home. I liked the menus and they were pretty fast when I wasn’t switching apps and inputs every 5 seconds trying to get the speakers to respond correctly. The cube makes me believe I probably just got a bad TV for some reason. I’ll give it a 3.

review_text: The description for this laptop is incorrect. I thought it may have been the adapter/hub I was using at first so I bought 5 others with varying capabilities and the results were the same. The USB port will work but the display ports do not. I ended up finding the online user manual for this exact model (on Acer's site) and sure enough, it says that this model has a standard USB-C 3.2 Gen 2 port rather than the thunderbolt 4 port on some of their other models. This was very disappointing to me since this laptop meets my needs in every other aspect. This is a major issue for me since I am using this laptop to replace one that is connected to multiple monitors and peripherals through a dock.

Second stupid thing with this power supply is there's no auxiliary overclocking motherboard connector either, once again, I went back to the well of my older extra cables, and I had what was needed. The keyboard is very well built, the optical switches (brown) are perfect to type on, nice tactile feedback without requiring too much force, although this is mostly subjective. I've been using this for a week or so, mostly for coding, typing, and some gaming, and I customized the layout to something I can work with. I'm typing this review with this keyboard as well. The firmware (Windows only, so get your Windows VM ready if you're on Mac or Linux) works decently well if you can read past some funky translations from Chinese, but doesn't allow full customization: for example, the FN key and all the factory FN+? keys that do something other than send keypresses (e.g. all the ones related to light effects, or bluetooth, or changing layout, ...) cannot be changed. I would've loved to move the FN to the left hand and reassign all the keys to change light effects to some other layer, cause I almost never need to use them. Anyways, for the price it allows decent customization. If this was it, I'd give it 5 stars (maybe 4.5), but: - Battery life on bluetooth with all lights off and "sleep" setting on default, it reports low battery after a day of moderate use. Changing the sleep setting to be more aggressive doesn't seem to change this significantly. Because of this, I basically have to keep it plugged in, which defeats the purpose of a wireless keyboard. Given how heavy this keyboard is, I was really expecting it to have a sizable battery. - Randomly, keys would get stuck and repeat forever, and the only way to stop it is to turn it off or switch the bluetooth to one of the other two devices. There's no physical on-off switch so while you do this it will fill pages of whatever letter you typed last. This *seems* to happen when the battery is low, but see the above point, the battery is bound to be low very often. So, the two points above (and lack of full customization) take 2 stars away, and here you have it, 3 stars. If the firmware was fixed to be more power efficient (or a bigger battery was provided), and wasn't prone to stuck keys, and maybe it allowed to customize "preset" key combos and FN key, this would be 5 stars, as the keyboard is very pleasant to type on. Again, I'm typing this on the keyboard, so ... :)

I reached out to Asus customer support 6 months after purchasing this with complaints about the faulty ethernet chipset and frequent POST failures, and I was not only told they don't give out refunds, but they don't do product replacements for this motherboard. So, $200 down the drain. I will be switching to Gigabyte who has stopped using the same I225-V chipset for this exact reason.

It's all about your purpose for buying an adapter like this. My purpose was very specific. I sit on the couch with my Asus Zenbook. It has very tight USB-C ports. If I set the laptop on the coffee table, get up, and then trip over the cord, I'm either going to yank the laptop to the floor (been there done that with prior laptops), or damage the port (done that, too). So, my sole reason for buying this adapter was to have an adapter that could charge at full power and also provide a release in case I, my wife, or my dog, got caught up in the charging cable. For my primary "quick release" reason, it works great. In fact, it works a little too well in the release deparment. It takes very little pulling/pressure to release from the connection. I'd rather have it this way than where it was too strong, but still wish it was a stronger connection. If I was Goldilocks, then this would be a "Mama Bear" connection. As far as charging speed, appearance, and material quality, the adapter is very good. My comments about the magnet are not really intended to be negative but rather to note it in case you are clumsy like me and need something to keep your laptop from going flying when you inevitably trip over the cord that it's going to disconnect when you don't want it to at times. This would not be an issue for a laptop sitting on a desk or table. One concern I had was whether the part of the adapter that plugs into the device would cover/block the adjacent USB-C port. On the 2020 Asus Zenbook, this is not a problem at all. The distance between the laptop USB-C ports is 18.5mm on the Zenbook. With the closer (14mm) distance betweeen USB-C ports on newer Macbooks, the plug in part of the adapter may be tight with a second cable, especially if you have a wide plug housing on your other cable. NOTE that the pics included are with the Zenbook, not an Apple. The ports on the Mac are 4.5mm closer together! I've deducted 1 star only because I don't think, at $20+, the value is all that great. Update 8 December 2020: Yesterday my 3 month old factory notebook charger stopped working. I cannot say whether the magnetic connector was the cause of the problem, but I've never had a charger fail like this before.

This review is for the 96W USB-C "Replace MacBook Pro Charger" by YeHeng and DRTOPA. To be honest, I'm not sure if I received the correct product since the one I got doesn't really resemble the product renders. Instead, it looks like another YeHeng [[ASIN:B096VSVSXS 96W USB-C charger]] that strongly resembles the Apple 96W USB-C charger. Despite looking through every word of both product descriptions, I couldn't find meaningful differences between the two products that would justify the significant price difference. Looking at the label on the charger itself, the listed model number is AE96, and a quick internet search revealed that this product is being sold all over the internet under various brands. Going deeper down the rabbit hole, I found a huge red flag which makes me question whether or not this product has actually undergone safety testing by UL and the FCC as the listing claims. There's a SafetyMark registration number (160912-11) printed on the bottom of this charger, but if we plug this number into Singapore's Consumer Product Safety and Accuracy system, we see that 160912-11 actually belongs to Apple's 87W USB-C Power Adapter (model A1719). In terms of behavior, the AE96 charger is not actually a perfect replacement for Apple's 96W USB-C charger. I own a genuine Apple 96W charger so I have a solid point of reference. I have a Lenovo 15.6" mobile workstation that's technically rated for 125W, but it can charge from PD power supplies rated 87W and above. The genuine Apple 96W USB-C charger is able to charge this machine when it's running. The AE96 is only able to charge my laptop at up to 60W when it's in sleep mode. During operation, it refuses to charge at all. Perhaps it has something to do with the inclusion of Qualcomm's Quick Charge 3.0/2.0 which is absent from Apple's charger. The inclusion of Qualcomm QC does allow for faster charging of various Android-based devices and power banks, but I'm not entirely convinced that it's even necessary for something billed as a replacement for Apple's 96W USB-C power adapter. Overall, this charger makes me leery and I wouldn't recommend it. It's unclear who actually made the product and the customer service contact is a gmail address.

Here are my pros and cons: Pros - So far so good with GPS accuracy - Good/believable HR data for running (need to crank down wrist strap though) - I find the HR sensor not too protruding or noticeable - Like seeing the projected impact on battery life when changing settings (so far it seems accurate) - Find user interface intuitive - Good size screen (for sub $300 watch) - Like the ability to configure sports mode in Suunto App. - Nice simple way to create routes with waypoints and send to watch. - Native stryd power fields integration - Build quality is good - Training metrics not forced on you or in your way when you don't want them. - Does not artificially limit the activity list for a less expensive model (i.e. hiking activity included). Cons (Bigger cons towards top) - A little large/heavy but okay (not sure I will be wearing this daily once long sleeves returns) - No offline music for road runs (I have a non-phone workaround but would prefer it to be on watch). - Smartphone notifications can't be muted without muting all alerts (prefer a more passive/on demand approach to checking messages and have no desired to be buzzed every message) - Footpod pace changes data seems slightly delayed - No real Map - Wish some settings would persist for an activity (like backlight and wrist HR). - Elevation data just okay for a non-baro. Unfortunately Strava is using this data by default (it's not supposed to for non-baro device) - Elevation profiles for longer activities (10+ miles) are too condensed (need ability to zoom on current climb) - Inconsistent Backlight activation (no dedicated button) Ultimately the cons will probably keep this from being my main watch, especially once I return to the office (no music, no notification only silencing, and too big). I will use it on the weekends and for rougher on watch activities (i.e. I'm okay scratching a sub-$300 watch but not a $600 one) . I give it 4 stars relative to my secondary use case (would be 3 stars if trying to use as main watch). Also I recommend getting the ventilated silicone strap accessory from Suunto (24MM Athletic 1) to go with it.

[[VIDEOID:80bad7d107d2eac47f2018d823a84935]] These are light and compact headphones that meet all of my listening needs. They are a bit tight-fitting and don’t completely cover my ears. The sound quality is louder and high-pitched. I previously used the discontinued Sony Noise Canceling MDR-NC7 headphones which worked very well for many years. Then last week I had worn them while resting on my couch, and I inadvertently put pressure on the side of the headphones with the weight of my head twisted against the pillow. Although not a lot of pressure, it was enough to cause a small piece of plastic less than half a centimeter at the joint of the left ear to break off. I tried was unable to repair the joint with glue and resorted to wrapping tape around it as a stopgap. The MDR-ZX110AP version is designed in a much simpler manner than my older model from Sony, mainly having one piece stretching from ear to ear. The previous design was head two rotating joints on each side attached by a curved bridge-piece. I find that the one-piece curved design applies too much pressure to the point of being uncomfortable, but this model seems to have some give to it, and I expect I’ll get used to the difference. I wasn’t sure if I needed the mic for $10 extra but decided audio quality is critical to video calls and other recordings I might want to do more of in the future. The ear cushioning is also more of a professional-grade quality compared to the foam material in the previous version, but I found the foam more comfortable although it may have resulted in some of the audio leaking out to the surrounding environment. The inward fold-up when not using them is convenient mainly because it’s quick to unfold and apply back on my ears. The old version would take longer to reorient when unfolding because the each earcup was free to rotate on an axel, and you had to make sure it was oriented so that the bottom of the cup with the wired connection wasn’t spun to the top. This isn’t a big deal but added a couple of seconds every time you wanted to put them on before. The sound quality suits my needs although I do feel it’s a bit screechy in the limited time I’ve tested it. I also don’t detect any noise cancellation. I believe the previous version automatically reduced the audio as part of the noise cancellation, so it makes sense that this is louder. This isn’t a major issue for me because I only use these on my computer, so the surroundings aren’t overly bothersome. These are also much lighter than previous generations of the product. It’s actually something I’ll have to get used to, but I suppose it will be something I take for granted and hard to go back to a heavier one once I do.

(also fyi, a lot of static) If you’re needing a product to monitor/ hear elderly (or ill) person, this is NOT for that use. PROS: set up very simple & easy Units worked/connected on 3 floor levels of home CONS: Person on the other end HAS to answer the call, to hear you. This device successfully plays music over bluetooth. Now for the negatives: This is not worth $120 ($140 with a protection plan) but it doesn’t matter. There is only one device that plays Spotify in the futuristic year 2022 besides a smartphone, and it’s this music player. For such a cost, and for a device specifically designed for modern music streaming services, I didn’t expect such early-2000s interface limitations and such a thin battery life. (1) You cannot rearrange playlists once you select the playlists you want synced; you must delete all of your music and re-add it all again in the order you desire, which will take a long time. (2) Syncing all of the music can take well over an hour, though sometimes it only takes 10-20 minutes. This is true of adding new playlists AND when syncing normally without adding new playlists to sync. Syncing fails frequently, and the Stop Sync button will fail as well. Sometimes it will tell you at the end of the sync that “some of your songs” were unable to sync from Spotify; it will not tell you which songs failed, or in which playlists, or even what to do besides erase all the music and try again with another hour-long sync attempt. (3) The battery life is just as miserable as other reviews have stated, something like 3-5 hours over bluetooth. When using a headphone/auxiliary cord, the battery lasted about 4-5 hours. (4) The charging cable is extremely short AND unique to this device. My recommendation is to get a USB extension cable or create a way for it to safely stay plugged into an outlet with usb without dangling it by its tiny cord. And used to the charging method you create because you will be doing it daily or twice daily. If I plan to be away from home for longer than three hours and plan to use this device, I carry a backup usb battery bank with me, which effectively nullifies the portability aspect of this device for that day. (5) There is no repeat function; you cannot put a song or playlist on repeat. (6) The device has no audio normalization or equalizer. Expect occasional audio peaks in some songs if your headphones or speaker are at a moderate or loud volume. I was unable to test High or Highest quality music because the sync continually failed. The instructions also discourage High or Highest quality if using Bluetooth, possibly because it would skip due to too much data? (Unsure; unable to test because the sync was even longer when loading, likely due to the larger file size. The sync continually failed after 20-30 minutes of trying, sometimes longer.) OVERALL CONCLUSION: This feels like a phoned-in iPod Shuffle, but at least those synced much faster two decades ago. These devices also cost around the same price as iPod Shuffles were 20 years ago, which seems impossible. There doesn’t appear to be another option on the market for a dedicated Spotify playing device.

Not everyone has a USB-C cable. Especially, if someone only has iPhone, (up to 13 pro), they still wont be able to use their cable for charging . Why isn’t there a browser? If I screencast my phone to apple tv, and try to share something on web, the screen size does not do justice - Improve the TV - Remote interaction. Mine couldn’t work when I try to turn off the TV. Amazon Fire Cube figured it out… why cant you - Add color to the units similar to what you have done with iPhones - Apple TV+… why should I spend $6 on this service? Add more channels to it. This is $6 extra that only would get me one more tv channel which is no match for showtime, HBO or ESPN. Review after about 300 hours of use. This projector replaced a JVC DLP (rebranded BenQ). The projector is ceiling mounted. Screen is a 110" 16:9 ALR. Room is sorta light controlled - windows flank the screen. Lighting in the room is via multiple track heads on both sides of the room. Walls are white, so light from the track heads bounce everywhere. Adjustability: The ceiling in my viewing room is low - the centerline of the lens is below the top of the screen. On the JVC, the only way to get this to work was with some extreme keystone adjustment. The Epson has some easily accessible knobs that made lens shift adjustment extremely easy - especially when working on something hanging over your head. The lens on the JVC was in the middle of the projector whereas the lens on the 3800 was offset to one side. The lens shift meant the I didn't have to mess around with moving the projector mount a few inches to the side. There's a little play in the knobs that is a bit annoying at first but you get use to it quickly. The amount of lens shift is incredible making projector placement much less of a consideration. Brightness: The old projector was rated at 5000 lumens at full power - even in eco mode, that projector should haven been substantially brighter than the 3800, but I can't tell the difference. I would chalk that up to the improved contrast. No problem with viewing on an ALR screen with the lights dimmed to about 50%. Noise: yeah, it's noisy. About on par with the JVC but the projector is mounted directly over my sofa. The noise only really stands out when you are listening for it or there is no dialogue/music. The exhaust louver is right by the lens - if the projector is behind your seating position, it might be more objectionable. The louver isn't pointed directly back at the screen but angled slightly to the side. Size: I was originally considering the 4000/4010, but again, I got a low ceiling and having a massive projector hanging over your head seemed like a bad idea. The 3800 was a bit bigger than I expected, but compared to the 4000/4010, it's nothing. Mounting it was also pretty easy but the wider spacing between the mounting holes on the project did necessitate a bit of McGyver'ing on the projector mount. The bad: convergence on my 3800 is a mess. The picture seemed a bit softer on one side, but being lazy, I didn't bother trying to figure out what the issue was. The remote control has a nice "pattern" button which will display an alignment grid. That confirmed that something was wrong on one side of the screen, but again - lazy. The grid fuzzy grid lines on the left side of the screen were easily twice as wide as the nice and sharp grid lines on the right side. The fuzziness was mostly noticeable when playing video games. At first, I thought that it was an alignment issue and the projector wasn't perpendicular to the screen. Finally, when trying to avoid some household chores, I made the mistake of trying to get to the bottom of the issue. Several hours later after messing around with the projector mount alignment, then diving into the convergence menu, I came to the conclusion that there was nothing that I could do about it. If your a type A person, trying to do a point by point convergence adjustment is like being a hamster on a hamster wheel - you just can't stop. YMMV - my tip would be to check the projector's convergence when you get it. Maybe it's just the luck of the draw. Since I'm lazy, I'm now outside of the Amazon replacement window and I don't feel like going thru the hassle of getting a warranty refurb from Epson. The projector is still usable but it bugs me now that I've confirmed what the issue is and I can do nothing about it short of getting a replacement.

Received the product in a timely fashion. Had Windows on it. First boot up, Cortona talked me through set up. I had a Microsoft account already. Installed personal software on it. Luckily, kept my personal files from my prior laptop on a flash drive. Used product for three days and while in the middle of being on a website, it crashed. Got a Blue Screen error. Then got Black screen when I tried to reboot. Took it to local Geek shop. Below is their message of what was wrong with it: "The laptop's SSD was formatted using the MBR partition format instead of GPT, completely opening it up for failure as MBR can easily cause data corruption and as a result, boot issues. GPT stores the data and way the partitions are organized in a more secure way in order to prevent corruption. We were able to run chkdsk and sfc, two commands within the Windows command prompt on an external system in order to fix the corruption in the boot files of the drive. We then ran a program built into windows to convert your drive from MBR to GPT to ensure this does not happen again. Your total service charge will be $249 (minus the $59 diagnosis fee, you will owe $190 upon pickup of your device). " I spent more to get it fixed than I paid for it. The total out of pocket for me, I could have bought a brand new laptop. I will have to fight with seller and Amazon on making this right to me. I am keeping it because I have no other computer.

Did not spend enough time with the other one to see this issue. -Slow wake up times from sleep on BOTH UNITS. If you can deal with the above cons, playing panel lottery and only a one year warranty with to back it: This is the panel for you! Keep in mind you need something like 12 or more pixels with issues for a warranty claim. UPDATE #2: I was persistent and got a 3rd replacement. No dead pixels this time. Panel uniformity is trash. This one suffers from a blatant green hue on the right 1/4th of the screen and it's a little darker there. There's a 2"-3" dark blob on the far left center that is very distracting. The left side has a very mild warmer hue than the center. These monitors are horrible. Good ones do exist though. I took a trip to microcenter and saw a perfect one. I lost the lottery. FINAL THOUGHT: I don't think it's the right time to buy a 34" 3440x1440 panel for gaming (As of 11/29/20). All the reasonable options on the market have feature sets that are all over the place or that are incomplete. That is unless you are willing to spend $2500+ on top of the line HDR1000 models and wait a long time for stock. LG is the only brand that has the specs nailed on the head for gaming panels, but they can't seem to manufacture them properly. This monitor shouldn't even exist. It makes me sad to think how many people own this panel and just decided to deal with the issues or aren't informed enough to notice them.

First of all, there is no manual. Go to their website and it's very difficult to find anything on this monitor. I was about to give it one star when I found information on a different LG monitor that worked here. Monitor is 3440x1440, yet when I hooked it up, my Windows 10 machine with a Radeon R9 270 suggested something 3840x2160, so I set it to that. How does a monitor exceed it maximum resolution? anyway, nothing I tried as far as different resolutions worked right. I got stretched photos and text or the entire screen would not be filled. I then found that there is a tiny swivel stick on the bottom of the monitor to go into settings (I kept getting popups to use arrow keys or press button to accept, but I searched the entire monitor and couldn't find any buttons). Well, I found a setting for INPUT and then ASPECT RATIO. I assumed Full Wide was correct, but it wasn't. Standard was proper ratio, but didn't fill full screen. Finally, I picked Cinema1, then switched to resolution 3440x1440 and it worked. I hope this helped someone because without a manual, how would anyone know any of this? [update 7/13/2020] my previous information was for an HDMI connection. I ordered a DisplayPort cable and using the full wide setting works and the color and clarity is much better by the way. refresh rate also went from about 30 to 60 now. I bought a used 5th wheel RV last summer. I plan to live in it full time. Only one problem...the wifi in the main house (my roomie lets me use his for free) would never reach the RV. I spent about 6 months researching solutions and although this Wavlink product is pretty expensive it turns out I could not have done better. BE ADVISED...if you watch videos about how to set it up you'll see people attaching routers to their cable modems and running LAN cable through the walls and crawl spaces and buying expensive mounting arms and so on and so on. YOU DON'T NEED ANY OF THAT IF YOU WANT TO BRING WIFI TO AN OUT BUILDING! You do need to run the setup wizard from the location where you most want the wifi and pay attention to all the possibilities. I didn't the first time I tried to setup the repeater and thought I was in for a major hassle. Then I sat down and patiently went through all the screens. Bingo! Five bars of pure, clear, steady wifi. The trick is to refresh the available networks until the one you want shows up with even 1 bar. The setup will tell you that the signal is very weak. Ignore that. Input the password for whatever wifi signal you are trying to reach and the repeater will create a good, strong connection by adding a short extension to the network name. To use devices in the outbuilding, be sure you connect to the new extended network. You'll use the same password as already exists for the network. My RV is about 250 feet from the original cable modem and this model has no problem providing excellent signal. It's range, in feet, for those who don't do metric easily, is 650 + change. I can now be connected anywhere on a full acre.

I purchased this HT for an inexpensive way to get on the 220 band for local repeaters. There aren’t many HTs for 1.25cm available. Unboxing was impressive - it came with an extra capacity battery, desk charger, speaker mic, 2 antennas, programming cable, etc. My initial impressions are that the build is good for the price, the buttons have a good feel, the case seems durable enough, and the features are solid. These radios don’t compare to higher quality Japanese radios, which I mainly own, but for this price point, it’s really impressive what they offer. It’s a great option for entry level, for a project such as an APRS station, portable use where you don’t want to bring a more expensive radio, or as a backup for emergency use. For programming I’ve used CHIRP, which is free and compatible with this radio. Programming was very easy, I was able to hit repeaters locally in minutes after unboxing. Note that CHIRP doesn’t list this radio directly yet, but, if you choose Radioddity UV-5RX3, it will work. I have not tried the software from Baofeng, but CHIRP is what I’m familiar with for other radios. I have not tested the actual power output versus rated output, nor the receiver performance, but if you’re looking to use this with a local repeater, it will likely work well for you. I did not even bother using the stock included antennas, I used the Nagoya triband whip. It’s almost the same cost as the radio, but well worth it. I ran into an issue where transmitting on 220 caused a Verizon ONT box to reboot. Solved it with ferrite beads on the inputs to the ONT, problem solved. This wasn’t just an issue with this radio but also with a different brand. The ONT must be sensitive to this particular band.

I bought these (Lightning Wired) earphones seven months (and six days) ago. I use them exclusively for listening to audiobooks, making phone calls, and telling Siri what I want. I rarely listen to music. I prefer the wired connections because I want to avoid the radiation of Bluetooth, and I am not happy having to frequently recharge Bluetooth devices. Wired earbuds don't have those problems. SOUND QUALITY - Grade C+: My previous earphones were Apple Lightning Earbuds. These BEATS earphones are not quite as good as the Apple product in sound quality, in that they sound maybe 20% like they are being played over a telephone, whereas the Apple products had better fidelity. Even so, all the audiobooks I listened to on these earphones was perfectly distinct and understandable, so after I got used to them, it was all fine. COMFORT - Grade B+: I was glad these earphones came with multiple soft rubber eartips, and I had to try all 4 before I found the one that was most comfortable. Comparing these to the Apple product, they are not as comfortable. The Apple earbuds are hard plastic (no eartips), but I could wear them all day (such as when I was making an 11-hour drive) and they were just as comfortable at the end of the day as at the beginning. With the Beats earphones, the first three eartips I tried would make my ears hurt after an hour or two of use, and the fourth pair is fine for all day but frequently slips out of my ears when I bump the connector cord. DURABILITY - Grade F: After 7 months and 5 days of use, the buttons on the wirewart suddenly stopped working. Now I cannot start/stop the playback or change the volume of anything by clicking the buttons on the wire, but now I have to take out the phone and make those changes there. I know it's not the phone because I have tried this on several devices, and it's all the same. Other headphones do work on all those devices. So is seven months of operation before they break acceptable? No, not for the price they are charging. I have asked a question (In this Amazon listing) and if the seller responds, we shall see what they say. I could not find a "Contact the seller" button on this listing. UPDATE: The seller did not answer my question, and the Amazon (Beats?) return window closed only one month after the purchase. After spending more than an hour on their website, I was unable to find any way to contact them about return or replacement, other than generic information that I now have to get service through AppleCare, and it will probably cost as much as this product's original price to get them fixed. WOULD I GET THESE AGAIN? Absolutely not. They cost twice as much as the Apple earbuds, they don't sound as good, they are not as comfortable, and they break after seven months. Lots of reviews already out there pointing out how this product is way over-priced. Every speaker has one of these inside, plus an amp and speaker, but without the outputs and you can get them for half the price. So, clearly, Sonos prices this based on their perceived value to the customer and completely detached from the cost of goods, but that's not uncommon. I will say it is too bad. I'd buy 12 of them if they were priced at $200 and I think they'd still make good money. I actually have 12 of the older Connect devices that they are trying to coerce me to upgrade but even with the offered 30% discount, it's too much, especially for marginal benefit. So, my real point in writing a review is to point out the painful experience of the setup process and added cost of personal information demanded. The app required both my location information and microphone access to perform setup. Neither of these is necessary. I tried setting the location setting to "once" and it went a ways through the setup and then seemed to try to access my location again, couldn't, and without asking, aborted the setup and forced me to start from scratch again. It claims to need this to know about my networks, but even with my location it doesn't know about my network, so that's false. This is just extortion of personal information and it seems to be a new fad with app makers. The microphone access is another fallacy. The port doesn't even have a speaker and I don't have one anywhere nearby either - I have it connected to a whole house audio distribution system (14 zones, so I guess I really could use 13 more of these at the right price). So, there is no way a microphone is going to help setup. I tried denying it and it wouldn't proceed - just kept sending me back to turn it on. I eventually had to comply and turn on those permissions, but I'll be turning them back off since they are unnecessary. Just another shameful Sonos decision. There are more failings in their setup process. It asked me to sign in to my account. Since I have an existing setup at another location, I already had an account. But, I created it 7 years ago and it had a 7 character password. The new app wouldn't allow me to login with my 7 character password saying 8 characters are required. Hey, guess what? You can't enforce that on login, only when (re)setting a password. Dumb. Fortunately their website let me login and change my password to make it compliant so I could go back to using the app. Also, although the instructions first have you install the device before beginning the setup, you will need to remove the device again or turn it around and get good lighting on it because two steps in the setup require you to enter and 8 digit PIN printed in dark grey on the black background (very hard to see) in about 8 point type. Then, later, you also have to enter the serial number printed above that. I'm sure all that info is readable by the device which they also have you press the button of to confirm physical access and that you are setting up the right unit, so these frustrating steps seem entirely unnecessary. Oh, and they don't tell you this, but the cardboard wrapping the printed instructions came in have these 2 numbers printed on them without any text description. I discovered this 2 days later when I was cleaning up and happened to recognize them. Another problem came with adding in my music services. I said I wanted to add one. Then I selected Amazon Music. It asked for my userID and password, so I entered them and it kept telling me they were wrong. I went to Amazon and verified they were correct. I tried another service and had the same problem. Turns out, it wanted me to re-enter my Sonos ID and password, though it never said so. I'm sure some programmer is sitting there going "I know what I meant when I wrote that!" Cool. Do you know what I think of you right now? So, in the end, you'll only want to get this if you are expanding a Sonos system. There are a great many comparable products out there at reasonable prices that are 1/4 to 1/2 the price. Sonos used to be rather unique, but they've lost that edge and now seem to be milking what they've got in their user base and trying to be a "premium" brand.

This unit replace a 55" LG that was constantly having problems with Wi-Fi connectivity. This Fire TV redressed that as the Wi-Fi reception is great with no buffering issues whatsoever. While I can't speak to the picture quality being I'm blind, my wife said it's a step up from the LG in terms of resolution and clarity. What I really like about this TV is the Voice View screen reader capability, which enables me to access and select menu options. The speech synthesizer is decent but pronounces "resume" as "revoo," which threw me off a bit. I still applaud Amazon for including the capability and at least considering the needs of people with disabilities, which other manufacturers don't seem to do. The hands-free control is great and I like that I'm able to use voice commands with the remote, which again has far reaching benefits for folks with disabilities who may have neuropathy and/or carpel tunnel of the fingers and hands. Alexa integration is flawless, which I'd expect from Amazon being they manufactured the TV and created both the Fire and Alexa platforms. So why not five stars, you ask? There's no need to have to enter a pin every time you want to change a basic system setting for the TV when all you want to do is set a pin for Prime Video purchases. We have two young children, and little hands have been known to grab the remote and accidentally purchase a video or two. But if you want to set a Prime Video pin to prevent said purchases, the pin also needs to be entered for such things as changing screen resolution, changing accessibility features, and other tasks that don't have anything to do with blocking purchases. Seems this is an opportunity for Amazon to enhance user experience so the pin can be more localized to the specific task as opposed to it being a global pin to complete all tasks. All in all, it's a fine product and it's only going to get better as the technology continues to evolve. The twenty-four month no-intrest installment plan is also great as many more folks like me with competing expenses and limited budgets will be more inclined to go with a Fire TV instead of having to shell out several hundred to more than a thousand bucks at one shot. I wish there were an option to give half stars as I give this device four and a half stars. Amazon's world domination will continue because they seem to really know what customers want while centralizing and streamlining all their content. Don't see how other companies can keep up, quite honestly.

The Good: It's got lots of screen real estate, which is helpful for capturing gestural sketching or having a bunch of tool pallets open simultaneously. It's got a reasonable amount of resolution, though, compared to the Retina screen it's currently sitting next to at my workstation, it looks a bit dated. The pressure sensitivity is great, much better the ancient Intuos3 it replaced. The tilt-adjustable stand feels solid and is easy to adjust. *Lot's of hotkeys. **Customer service is helpful. The Bad: The OSX install instructions are in Engrish. You may get through them in one piece; I did not. The supplied USB-C cable on my copy doesn't inspire confidence. They stick out further than they should in my iMac. It needed to have the plugs rotated, flipped, etc. in order to get the tablet running. **Reaching out to XP-Pen for help will be a bit of an exercise in patience and persistence. I've needed to uninstall/reinstall the tablet driver, and dump my prefs file for Adobe Illustrator 2020 alarming often since installing this equipment for the first time. *The hotkey and scroll-wheels haptics feel cheap. The Neutral: Before buying ANY screen tablet, think about your lighting situation. If there are lights directly above your desk, the reflected glare is going to give you a migraine. This is just a personal anecdote, but the lighting in the cube-farm in which I work significantly reduces the number of positions the tablet (and my head) can be in without catching reflected glare from one or more lights. Because my job allows me some freedom/authority over my workstation, as a solution, I've removed the lights above my desk. This may not be feasible for some. Conclusion: If you NEED the extra screen real estate and don't have the budget for a Cintiq, and you're willing to deal with some headaches and downtime, this is a good fit.

I bought this to use with my Xbox Series X. I’ve had so many Series X users telling me it’s not good enough and it’s perfect for the Series S, but not everyone has the money or space for a 32” + monitor or TV, especially after buying the Series X and if you already have a large screen TV. Anyways, this monitor is great and loaded for the first price, plus is pretty high quality without that high cost price. I do have a few “issues…” There is only 1 actual HDMI port, with the other being a display port. I probably would have known this if I paid more attention to details, but I for some reason thought it had 2 HDMI ports. Either way, since I want to use this specifically for my Xbox and Switch, and neither of those have a display port, I was stuck with the choice of either switching the HDMI plug between the 2 consoles, lol, or buying an HDMI to display port adapter. I bought the adapter tonight and it will get here on Friday, so I think that will solve the issue, but it would have been nice if an adapter was already included, or if we were asked which we wanted with our monitor purchase: the display port cord or the adapter. Second issue…no sound, but you can connect a speaker via cord or from your console or device. IMO, with all this monitor packs, sound should have naturally been included and the fact that it isn’t almost feels like they tried to offer a good value at the bare minimum of work for them or expectations…but I also don’t fully think that because the monitor is still a great one on its own. Other than that, it’s great quality but very lightweight! Now often, even more so with tech, we associate weight with quality. The more something weighs, the higher quality it probably is (or we assume it to be), and this monitor is going to prove the opposite. From the stand to the screen, it’s easy to setup and pick up, plus once you’ve set the stand up, you can move the monitor a bit, to face more downward or upward. Tip: when getting the stand sorted, use your phone flashlight for a bit extra light, use tweezers to place the small screws in their place if your fingers are a bit too big to easily place them, and know that they include a couple of extra screws just in case, which is nice. You’ll only need one silver for the bottom and four black ones for the stand to monitor.

Mixed impressions on this product. First, the positive. I've been wanting a product like this for years. This is exactly what I was looking for in a portable 17" monitor. The build quality is excellent, it seems really solid. It's super easy to carry around, and yet it is nice and big at 17". I love the magnetically attached cover/flap thing. I like that it is VESA mountable as well; I mounted one of my panels and I'm using it paired with a laptop for a super compact home office setup. Viewing angle is pretty good. It offers a good selection of ports. The OSD interface is a little clunky but it gets the job done. I attached one to a Nintendo Switch and it seems great for gaming, very responsive and good colors. Now, the negative. It's sort of a lottery on the panel itself. I wanted two of these, one for my home office setup and one to actually use for gaming (when someone else is using the TV) and to travel with. I ended up going through five to get two that I was satisfied with. With my first set of two, one of them had a dead/stuck red pixel and one of them had a cluster of stuck white pixels in the top left. I returned them both for replacement. The next batch had one good panel with no pixel issues that I can detect, and one with another dead/stuck red pixel along with a blue one. Since Amazon doesn't let you replace a replacement, I engaged Cocopar support on that last one, and they just told me that a small number of pixel issues in a panel is considered acceptable (and probably even unavoidable) to them. They didn't seem willing to replace it as I had already performed a replacement for the same issue, so I returned that one for a refund and purchased one more. This last one had no pixel issues, but the panel had a distinct yellow tint with the stock settings that I hadn't seen on any of the previous four. I was able to correct that by messing with the color temperature settings in the OSD, lowering the "red" and "green" and raising the "blue". So... In the end I did end up with two satisfactory panels but it took more time and effort than I was hoping for. Maybe I'm being picky, but at $340, I expect a panel without obvious dead/stuck pixel issues. This seems to be basically a 17.3" laptop panel in a nice enclosure to make it standalone, and the going rate for a 17.3" 1080p IPS panel is about $75. And, you can't put a "satisfaction guaranteed" sticker on the front and then tell me "well that's just how it is" when I call in to complain about pixel problems. Now, maybe it is hard to produce panels without pixel issues, but with the consistency that I have been seeing them, I get the feeling that they must be getting cheap or reject panels from somewhere. Major vendors like Dell and HP do not consider any pixel issues to be acceptable in either laptops or standalone monitors and in the rare occasion that I have run into one they have been happy to replace it without giving me any grief at all.

review_text: Summary: The unit is UNSAFE, the battery (batteries?**) leaked, and now CyberPower customer service won't respond to me even though the unit is under warranty.
