I've looked at all the available "Bullet" Style PTZ cameras and this model is the best for the price and functions. I wanted a camera that anyone could see where the camera is looking, plus I needed a camera designed to be on top of a structure, unlike a dome PTZ that usually hangs down or is mounted under a structure. I did not use the "Easy" setup process with an app (The Danale app is very poor in my opinion), I always program everything manually. This camera is just like any other IP camera, starts on DHCP and gets an IP address from the Router, the default port is 80. Find the camera IP in the router log, open a browser window and type in the IP address into the address bar to log in. Log in with default admin/password to gain access to all the camera settings. ***I was unable to find any app that works directly with this model camera (excluding Danele), however my Amcrest NVR was already installed in the Amcrest App, so I control this camera through the Amcrest NVR via the Amcrest app. I have a few HD cameras already streaming on my home network, I tend to use 1280x720P resolution and set it to about 7 frames per second. In surveillance, 720P, 7 fps & 768K is plenty, in my opinion. I connected the camera to my Amcrest 4ch NVR. This camera has three profiles, H.264, H264+ & H.265 ***CAMERA MUST BE SET TO H.264 FOR USE WITH THE AMCREST NV2104/NV2109 NVRs*** This camera has a great picture during the day and night. Bright IR LEDs however, they are directly connected to the Light Sensor and can NOT be turned off at night. The camera has an auto focus/zoom lens, 4x1 Zoom lens with active Auto Focus. Auto Focus can be adjusted to be active or passive. This Camera has a microphone with three types of audio codecs. The PTZ function of this camera is decent. Since this camera is mounted on an arm, the Tilt is limited to about 60 degrees however this camera is able to tilt up to +5 degrees, unlike most Dome PTZ cameras. ***The first camera I bought, the Pan Function only worked half way, that camera was returned and the second camera I received works just fine. PTZ Presets are available, however the Zoom function is NOT part of the preset program. The camera has the option of Preset1 bootup. Overall this camera is good, great for the price and will perform well for basic PTZ surveillance. The camera is designed to be outside in all types of Weather, be sure that your power/network connections are secure from weather via weather proof box. Update: So the second unit of this model camera that I have purchased now has the same issue as the first camera; after a few months of use, the camera rebooted and now will not pan the full radius as it did before. I am not sure what is going on, the camera does seem to be confused on where it is on the horizontal plain since it will bury it's self into the left stop set, it seems that it needs to do a full calibration of movement. I will be contacting the Manufacture shortly. Update 2: For some reason, this camera, when powered down, loses it's orientation of it's Horizontal pan. How far left and how far right it can turn. This means that it may try too hard to go left, but stop half way going back right. Way to correct this issue: Basically turn the camera to the right as far as the Software will allow, then with the camera powered down, physically turning the camera to the furthest point right before powering it back up. You are re-calibrating the camera manually. Now the camera will have it's full length of Pan back. This only happens for me from what I've noticed in the Reviews :(

Ok so not one of these worked from the get go so this tells me QC is non existent as far as testing goes ... overall fit and finish for the cost seems fine, but not one would accept any headphone plug that I tried, as it appears to me that the inner contacts are not spaced correctly so no standard plug could be inserted in enough to make the final click. But there is a fix if your like me and don't want to send these back. The trick to making these work is as simple as an 1/8 Allen key, push the Allen in till it hits the bottom then twist then very gently a few times and then put some tension in and around the inside of the jack back and forth with the key, you should feel the contacts loosen up a bit after that, now test a few standard plugs to see that they fit, they should now click into place with a nice snap do this a few time if it does not work the first time. I did all ten using my little trick and now they all accept a standard 3.5 or 1/8 plug. Ideally the manufacturer needs to fix this issue, and I hope they read this because these would be fine if they fix em so know that if you get these you may need to mod them a bit to get them to work.

review_text: I purchased this access point to extend my WiFi out to a couple of garden sheds, about 250 feet away from the house. The signal out there is reasonably ok, but I wanted it to extended even further, so a repeater seemed like the right idea. Avoid this repeater. Out of the box, it doesn't even allow you to use special characters in your device admin password or your SSIDs. It will tell you that it supports them, but when you try and use them, it will fail to save the password. Alphanumeric only. I first tried setting it up as a mesh device, in the hopes that the auto-steering and backhaul selection would be simple. However, this device supports EasyMesh, and ONLY EasyMesh. Any attempt to get it to connect to my EnGenius WiFi access point which supports mesh networking (but not EasyMesh) was impossible. In fact, once you set it as an EasyMesh device, you were completely locked out of all settings of the controller, until you reset it to factory defaults. I tried updating the firmware from the WavLink website; now it will let me use special characters in my passwords, but there aren't any additional features, and this feels like a beta firmware despite being released in 2021 (really??). On startup, the device doesn't even allow you to connect to anything for about 2 minutes, and the latency for any connection to or through the device is about 2.5-3 seconds. Running a ping -t on the device's address, you can watch the latency climb from ~1000ms after you get a connection, to about 3000ms, before finally it starts to respond like a real network device and you get the <1-1ms pings you'd expect locally. Finally, I set it up as a repeater, asked it connect to my 2.4GHz network and expand it to its own 2.4g and 5GHz networks, and connected to it with my WiFi-6 enabled laptop on the 5g band. My Internet is not blazing fast; I generally get between 40-100mpbs when I'm hardwired, with latency to Google's DNS servers about 30-45ms. However, using this 'repeater,' I am unable to determine my bandwidth. About 1/2 of the packets sent to 8.8.8.8 drop entirely, the rest come back in ~2500ms, and Ookla's bandwidth test errors out, usually before it even begins. ``` Reply from 8.8.8.8: bytes=32 time=2495ms TTL=111 Request timed out. Request timed out. Reply from 8.8.8.8: bytes=32 time=2663ms TTL=111 Request timed out. Request timed out. Request timed out. Reply from 8.8.8.8: bytes=32 time=2565ms TTL=111 Reply from 8.8.8.8: bytes=32 time=2638ms TTL=111 Reply from 8.8.8.8: bytes=32 time=2738ms TTL=111 Request timed out. ``` I will be returning this device for a refund.

The headphones are fantastic for most music with acoustic instruments. Listening to classical or film score music is like standing on the conductor’s podium. You can hear EVERYTHING and it is AMAZING!!!! Crisp. Clean. Accurate. Like being among the musicians in the studio, on the soundstage or in the concert all playing the music while it’s being recorded. When electronic or electric bass tones come into play, reproduction isn’t quite as rewarding because the synthetic bass tones or electric bass guitars feel like they are forcing the drivers when played at moderately loud levels. They struggle. However, the experience is improving as listening hours increase. Whoever says the bass is inflated must have degraded hearing. To my years these sound incredibly flat and linear. If you’re considering these, please understand you are purchasing monitor headphones. If you have a well mastered recording, these provide an extremely rewarding listening experience. If you’re listening to MP3s from the late 90s at a less than optimal bit rate, you will truly understand how much of the dynamic spectrum and resolution is compromised with low bit rate ripping. If you want something that alters, processes or colors a recording or want exaggerated highs or lows, this isn’t the product for you. I bought these wanting to hear everything a high quality, well engineered recording has to offer. I actually heard a “page turn” while listening to a symphony on compact disc. It doesn’t get any better that. Be prepared to give these cans 40-50 hours of play time to loosen and mature and I think you’ll be pleased with your choice.

I foolishly assumed that the frustrated people writing negative reviews were just not technical enough. Now I get to be on the other side, warning you: this device, and most critically, the software that powers it, are rushed, shoddy, and it's a lottery whether you'll ever get pixels in the program at all. First off, if you have an ultrawide, no form of the HD60 will work for you. You will need to spend more money on the 4k60 so that you can be disappointed in ultra high resolution. The software requires windows 10 to work. Fine. I spin up a rig with a 1070 and fresh – we're talking minutes old – install of the latest win10 build. Install this software. Try to run HDMI out from my macbook pro into my LG 34". Out of 7+ disassemblies and reassemblies, only one "worked", and the aspect ratio was totally wrong because it fails very ungracefully, downrezzing to 1080p and then stretching that distorted graphics. No worries. I bought an undersized model for my needs. User error, totally my fault. Here's why I'm straight up returning this and you couldn't PAY me to buy another elgato product: 90% of the time I opened the elgato software, I got a message that said something like "no source found, restart your PC". Are we just meant to accept that? That's absurd. Unplug and reconnect the device? Perfectly reasonable. But expecting a reboot cycle for EVERY ITERATION of troubleshooting, while mandating an OS with the amount of bloat that win10 has? Absolutely beyond the pale. There is no in-app explanation of this error at all, let alone why the error can only be remedied by nuking your session from orbit and beginning again to please the elgato gods. But that's not the stupidest message. By far the stupidest error I got, and I've gotten it dozens of times in a row now, is "Device is in use by other software". Reader, I assure you: device is not in use by other software. This install of windows is so young that if it were a human baby, the doctors wouldn't be done drying it off yet. There is not a single piece of user-installed software on this machine besides elgatos. There is no soundcard. No camera. No second monitor. Absolutely nothing that could plausibly interfere with the streaming. And even if there were, might elgato be able to, say, tell me what that software is? Or, better yet, strongarm the device back because I'm supposed to be the boss of the robot here, and not the other way around? I checked, by the way, and there was no sneakiness like a second background process of elgato that failed to shut down correctly. It's easy to check for this when your computer has nothing on it because the OS is fresh as the driven snow. This thing is a joke. It makes vintage soviet automobiles feel reliable by comparison. It's not about the money. Save yourself the headache. Buy something that won't leave you oscillating between a dull whimper and a howl at a godless sky. And elgato? Go home.

For instance if a person comes to the door the motion will record, but them arriving out front in the street before the motion sensitivity is triggered is not recorded. - The pricing of the Cloud Storage Service is not known until you actually start the process of signing up. I bought this Garmin watch because I was training for triathlons. Switching from an Apple Watch Series 4 to the Garmin was a bit of a transition at first. Honestly, I hated it for about the first week. Once you get used to the button and menu lay out though it becomes more apparent that the device is really good at what it does. After doing tons of research on other watches and devices I do think this is one of the best options on the market. It works really well when it comes to tracking and being consistent. If you’re into structured workouts coming from training peaks it’s phenomenal. One thing that the videos don’t cover very well is how you can create a structured work out and it will actually tell you if you’re low or high on your pace during the activity/interval. If you’re coming from Apple, you may think that having a touchscreen is superior, but if you’ve ever tried to do a swimming workout you realize really quickly how a button might be a better option. Also, you may not realize how amazing it is to have your screen on all the time. Or, how much better it is to not have to charge your watch every single day. The battery life is insane! Like you can do 12 GPS workouts in a week and probably still have battery life. This watch also interacts really well with my Tacx trainer, you can broadcast your heart rate, or completely control the trainer with the watch. Things that I’m not a fan of: GPS is not as accurate as the Apple Watch, if you don’t crank down the band you’re going to have trouble getting an accurate heart rate reading. The training metrics can get pretty annoying. For some reason it’s set up to give you an effort level at the first 3/4 mile of your run. Nothing like seeing a notification that says unproductive when you’re in the middle of your warm-up. If you do trails, and don’t turn off your VO2 Max calculation it will immediately affect your overall VO2 Max. If you’re buying into this whole pulse ox sensor BS it’s almost completely useless at sea level. If you want to conserve battery life you need to turn it off or use it while you’re sleeping. The Strength activity section of the app is really cool, but doesn’t work well at all. It basically never tracks your reps correctly. A great concept, but really frustrating. Spotify it is pretty clumsy, and not as easy to get to as it is on the Apple Watch, but it does download a lot faster and I never had any issues with music playback. (Have on the Apple Watch). All that said, I returned the watch. A lot of the above mentioned features are also on the previous model. Mant of the new watches that have come out Coros, Polar, other Garmins have similar if not identical set ups at a lower price point. I will probably own this watch again at some point, but when a new model is released and the price comes down a little bit.

I was a little skeptic in buying this unit based on previous reviews and it's discontinuation. Here are my thoughts in detail: Pros: - Physical aesthetics are beautiful (metal case with glass back) - Portable but not too small in viewing display - Color is actually blush gold (pinkish hue). The color is not gold nor rose gold but between gold and rose gold (like the gold color on the iPhone 8). I find it pleasant with a different change - Sound quality is excellent when using the EQ Pro (battery suffers a little) with great treble & voice clarity and bass extension - Easily drives IEMs - Scrolling volume wheel has a lock feature (When enabled, the volume is disabled only when the screen is off.) Very convenient from accidental pressing - External micro SD card slot for extra memory Cons: - When you press the previous or forward button with the display off and then wake up the display, sometimes the display goes to a different display or forwards a song automatically. Happened a few times without touching the display. Little buggy - No case - Scrolling wheel is only used for volume control (not for scrolling music) Neutral: - User interface is decent but a slight delay (previous/forward control) when using the EQ Pro - Display and features are a little outdated since it is a couple of years old and discontinued but with great sound. - Simplistic user experience & minimalist features with a modern look. - There is no lag when scrolling music (but not as responsive as a modern smart phone which is understandable). - I've seen reviewers mentioning lagginess when on 1.03 firmware. I can attest that there is none. When I got my A&K Jr, I charged it fully, then formatted and wiped the Jr's memory using Windows 10, and then saved a clean copy of the 1.03 hex file (from A&K website) in the root drive of my A&K Jr. I did this because I wanted a clean OS. - Displays clear artwork - Lyrics function is available (need to attach to your audio file Hope this clarifies in your purchase. ------------------------------ Update: After using and listening more of A&K Jr, I'm sorry to say that the software is definitely buggy. The software automatically forwards my music or changes the screen display when waking up the display from sleep mode. It happens more than often now since I use it every day. I'm extremely saddened since the sound quality is exceptional but changing my music or the display is too annoying for me. Also, you can't get a software update from A&K since this model is discontinued. Have to drop one star.

The Hisense H8G is a remarkable television when you consider its price point. At ~$400 for the 50 inch model, there is no other TV that even comes close to the same feature set. I play games on an Xbox one X and this TV works flawlessly with my console, and I have not seen any screen tearing to date. Speakers are surprisingly good, with balanced mids and highs, but of course, bass is a bit lacking. Android TV interface is snappy and works well-- the only issue is the internal storage. With only 4GB to store the OS, apps etc... the tv can slow down if you have too many apps installed. There are 2 ways to fix this: clear app cache or delete/reinstall the apps you use. Dolby vision support is great and works with Netflix without a hitch. The only downside to the TV that I notice frequently is the quality of the upscaling; it's just not as good as what you get from manufacturers like LG, Sony & Samsung. Overall though, GREAT TV!! This review is for a NETGEAR Orbi Whole Home Tri-band Mesh WiFi 6 System (RBK752) – Router with 1 Satellite Extender | Coverage up to 5,000 sq. ft. and 40+ Devices | AX4200 (Up to 4.2Gbps). Android application version: 2.10.1.1583 Router and Satellite Firmware Version V3.2.18.1_1.4.14 Given how long Netgear has been in the WiFi Router business and comparing this to Netgear products I owed many years ago, I find this product profoundly disappointing and would in no way recommend it to anyone for any reason. This kit consists of an RBR750 router, an RBS750 satellite, two AC adapters with proprietary barrel adaptors, and a CAT 5e ethernet cable. My ISP is Comcast/Xfinity and I have Gigabit internet service through a Motorola MB8611 DOCSIS 3.1 Cable Modem, that supports 6 Gbps Max Speed. The router I am replacing is a Google Wifi - AC1200 - Mesh WiFi System - Wifi Router - 4500 Sq Ft Coverage - 3 pack. In my area there are 20+ WiFi networks, so there is a lot of interference that necessitates a mesh system for decent performance. I have about 30 devices in about 3000 square feet connected via ethernet and WiFi. All my cabling is CAT 6, which should easily support Gigabit speeds, and I have a wired backhaul connection between the router and the satellite. The android phone used was a Google Pixel 4a. Initial setup is through the Android Orbi app. It's supposed to be as simple as connecting the cable modem and router, starting with them powered off, then following the app instructions by powering up the modem, waiting for it to connect, then powering up the router. It took about half a dozen tries for the app to even recognize there was a router to set up (with the phone at various distances from the router from a few inches to several feed. I'm not sure why it failed several times and why it eventually worked. When it worked one of the first things it did was a firmware update before it established a network. Initial performance was poor - at best similar to the old WiFi 4 Google Mesh system, and in many places slower (about half the speed). I eventually figured out that while the setup process had updated the router firmware, it had not updated the satellite. Once I updated the satellite, speed improved dramatically, with many speeds about double the older Google Wifi, and in some places as much as 8x the speed. But why didn't it get updated on initial; setup? The Android app, the router web interface, and the firmware are primitive, unintuitive, feature poor,and buggy with similar actions often having different results, even small configuration changes requiring a router restart, and the results of software and hardware restarts often being different and causing different malfunctions. It's like bad software from the 70's and there is no excuse for it. One of the most annoying issues was the router would stop listing attached devices for no apparent reason and would require a hard power off of the satellite then the router and a hard power up in the reverse order to cause attached devices to reappear - then for no apparent reason at some point it would stop listing them again. This is a problem Netgear has had several times in the past with various firmware updates - again there is no excuse for this. Periodically, the network seems to freeze for a few seconds to a few minutes several times a day for no apparent reason. And finally to add insult to injury you are plagued for requests to purchase additional warranty, additional support, and an additional security subscription for an unreliable system that is very expensive for the quality and feature set and comes with minimal warranty, support, and a brief trial security subscription. Don't buy it. Choose a different brand that offers more value for money, has friendlier and more reliable software, and comes with better warranty and support and does not require additional subscriptions for functionality. Netgear - shame on you.

I had never even heard of MikroTik prior to getting this switch. I just searched for the top rated 10gb capable switch with more than 2 ports and I am quite glad I did. I ordered the 5 port 10gb and 3 RJ45 transceivers so I could connect both my desktop and my Unraid server (both using ASUS XG-C100C 10G cards) to my Qnap TVS-951x NAS, as the NAS had only one 10gb port. I got everything all wired up with cat 7 and was quite happy with the performance right out of the gate, and I figured "it's just a switch, I have tons of those" so I didn't really think or bother to check if the switch even had a web interface. I was doing some diagnostics in which I needed to check something with the connection so I decided to check if there was a way into the switch, which was when I discovered what I now consider to be a hidden gem, the RouterOS software that the switch came with. As I mentioned, I thought it was "just a switch", turns out this thing has an extremely comprehensive and feature-packed operating system, with what seems like every functionality under the sun (from a quick glance over, at least) and tools for everything from email testing and verification to traffic generation. I am quite impressed with what you get for the price. Overall, the only gripe I have about the unit isn't really the fault of the unit, but with the RJ45 transceivers I am using, they were causing the whole setup to get alarmingly warm. Since the switch is a fanless design, that might end up becoming an issue for you. Luckily, it is extremely well ventilated, so as long as whever you are using it has some sort of airflow, it should be fine. Of course, if you are using different transceivers, it should not even be an issue for you. I pointed a small fan at them and everything is perfectly cool now, which I should have done long ago anyways as it is also helping cool the rest of the equipment near it. That said, so far it has been great, and I definitely recommend it.

Why would anyone who isn't paying for Zoleo provide their personal info or download an app that then has access to their personal data, contacts, usage, etc?? They need to make this a no brainer setup and feature from step one. They don't. In theory, this seems like a great idea. Their execution is terrible. I highly recommend going another direction. Do not buy this or give these guys your money. This should be labeled as a beta version. It acts like one. And it should cost much less.

I had two events coming up where I thought a set of earbuds would be really helpful. One was a mandatory in office meeting (I have been remote since Feb of 2019) and a benefit cornhole tournament where the music genre was probably exactly opposite of my taste in music. I started looking on Amazon expecting to pay around $100 for a good pair of pods that would sound decent and have all the features I wanted or needed. Found these for $89 before tax. When I originally came across them I found the black ones for $20 more, with a link to the silver for the cheaper price. I compared the silver and black pods to verify any differences in them. Absolutely no difference besides color. Silver it was. When they arrived I opened them and checked for fit. Klipsch sends an additional 6 pairs of inserts that snap on to the buds in different sizes. Found the size that fit my ear and snapped them on. Next was a connection test. I connected to my phone's blue tooth with no issues. Played a song and made a test phone call, no issues. Then I connected to my Onkyo home theater receiver and played a little bit of a movie, no issues. Final connection test was with my Gen 6 iPad. Connected and played a you tube video, no issues. Finally the day of the tournament came and it was time to put these to a real world test. It was extremely hot and humid the day of the tournament with the heat index approaching 115. As you can imagine everyone was drenched in sweat as they were playing. The pods held up great and the sound was perfect to cover up the music being played on the patio of the bar where the tournament was being held. I did have an issue twice with one of the pods falling out of my ears. At the time I wasn't sure if it was a problem due to fit or just the amount of sweat covering my body making the pods come loose. A couple days later and the office meeting came. As I took calls or Zoom meetings using these pods as the primary source for sound, everything was still working great, and I never had one come loose from my ear. I chalked the falling out at the tournament up to the amount of sweat they were surrounded with. I also heard no complaints about people on calls or in meetings being able to hear me via the built in mics. The sound quality is good. They don't have a ton of bass, but they are in the ear headphones that aren't going to compare to a 12" subwoofer being driven by 300 watts. Music and calls are very clear, and can be dialed in even more with the Klipsch app. Overall the sound was comparable to mid range on ear or over the ear headphones. Battery life lasted for close to 8 full hours without the need for a charge. The pods offer the ability to turn the volume of the connected device, up or down, skip or go back on songs, answer or mute calls. The transparency mode does allow outside sound in, but isn't going to make those sounds the priority over what is being played on the pods. I read a lot of reviews about batteries failing to hold a charge, or the app bricking the pods. I haven't had any of those issues. I have multiple sets of Klipsch reference speakers in my home and I would say that these pods are of the same quality I would expect from anything with the Klipsch name on them.

--UPDATED FOR CUSTOMER SERVICE EXPERIENCE-- While I would still rate the product I received 3 stars for its defects, I would like to mention that TOZO customer service reached out to me via e-mail and offered me a brand new set of ear buds completely free to compensate me. VERY nice of them! I've decided to up my rating to 4 stars to reflect the overall experience that I had with TOZO as a brand. They actually sent me the TOZO T6 model earbuds too (which is a step above the TOZO A1 in quality), and so far I haven't had any issues with them thankfully. While the original issues I had in my defective product are still present, I believe buyers can feel slightly more reassured knowing that customer service can help them out if something similar happens. -- I have only seen a handful of reviews mention the audio delay in these headphones, so I don't know if it's just the pair I received, but the audio lags about 0.2-0.4 seconds behind the video playing on my screen. I have tried these on multiple devices (phone, tablet, desktop PC and Nintendo Switch) and there's a delay across all of them, unfortunately. This makes watching TV shows and YouTube vids pretty off-putting, as the lips won't match the words quite right and sound effects come in late and ruin the impact of some jokes/scenes a lot of the time. The same goes for playing video games, as many gaming experiences will be hampered by even a slight delay in audio. I personally would not use these for playing games or while watching something that requires a lot of attention on the screen, which is disappointing. Music, podcasts, audiobooks, and any other kind of media where sound delay doesn't matter much will work fine though, of course. As for the earbuds themselves, the audio quality is alright — it's not terrible but I do notice some songs/videos have a slight tinny sound to them, which is the only time I found them jarring to listen to. I wasn't looking high-quality, just something functional, and these get the job done. I like the charging case — it's compact and shuts firm with a magnet, so it feels nice and secure. The earbuds fit in my ear pretty well, and feel comfortable for about an hour before they start to hurt a little. This could just be me having small ears or not being used to wearing earbuds much, but I don't mind since my listening sessions usually don't go past an hour anyway. One last thing — some reviews mention one earbud dying or the whole pair not working anymore after a couple months or even weeks. After about a month of use, one of my earbuds sometimes does not connect right away when I take it out of the case. One earbud will sync and play audio, while the other will be completely silent or even cut in and out of playing audio. This has only happened a couple times, and popping the earbud back into the case usually fixes it for me, but I think this is lines up with some products being faulty or failing in a short time. This type of risk/gamble isn't uncommon with items of this price point and I was willing to take my chances with it, but keep that in mind if you're considering a cheaper option or possibly saving up for a better and more consistent product.

review_text: The Flex works OK with Roku Ultra watching live TV, but DVR playback has a half second of audio silence every 5-9 seconds. I'll call it a "blip", and it happens with WiFi or Ethernet connection. I tried every audio mode in Roku settings, but none resolved the blip. Most settings delivered no audio on live TV or recorded playback. Searched for a resolution on the HDHR forum, only to find no resolution but plenty of others complaining as well. My Firestick had no audio or video issues so I'm guessing it's a Roku thing. This is not a new problem. I had a HDHR Quatro that lightning took out last year. Thought I would try it again with the Flex, but the Roku audio blip is still an issue. Note that Roku HDHRun app is different than the regular android app you get with the Firestick or Microsoft app downloads. Also, the Roku app doesn't have as many features as the android app, and the interface is frustrating with no consistent way to switch from live TV to browse recordings. Sometimes, pressing the remote's OK button in live TV brings up a bottom menu/control bar that I can scroll to the far right icon and select it to get to the top menu and select "Recordings", but not always. Getting either the top or bottom menu bars to go away is hard to do without exiting the app altogether. Again, same problems with my Quatro. You would think that Silicon Dust would work with Roku to resolve the problems after so many years. I have too much investment in Roku devices, so the audio issues are a deal breaker for me. I'm returning the HDHRun Flex.

tl;dr: I do NOT recommend this for a modern gaming setup. I loved how my thunderbolt dock worked for my work computer so I wanted the same for my personal (gaming) computer and it didn't work out like I had hoped. There is a small level of convenience, but the ultimate performance hit really isn't worth it. I would give service zero stars if I could. Pros: It's pretty and seems well built If you want low-demand USB/Display hub functionality it will work, but there are cheaper options. Cons: DisplayLink Expect ZERO service if you are having issues (and I can't stress this enough) USB-C (when it says it, it means it. Don't do like I did and get sucked into believing it has Thunderbolt support) If you want more of the review without the background, skip this first paragraph. Maybe I went into this expecting too much. I have a home office setup that I use for both work and personal use. I have two 24" monitors, and a KVM switch that will switch both my wireless mouse, keyboard, and audio between my two computers. My personal computer I used for gaming was a little older, but had a MiniDP and HDMI port for use with my two monitors, and I had to plug in the power, KVM switch, and ethernet; so anytime I wanted to take it anywhere, it all had to be unplugged and re-plugged in when I got back home with it. On the other hand I have a "standard issue" Dell work computer with an accompanying Thunderbolt dock. And the Thunderbolt dock is NICE. No power, no usb, no ethernet, or video, all plugged nicely into the dock and all I had to do was plug that thunderbolt cable into my computer and everything worked. If I needed to take it anywhere, I just unplugged the thunderbolt cable and threw the computer in my backpack where the charger that I never had to plug in at home was already waiting. In an unrelated event (trying a newer game a friend recommended) it became apparent just how old my gaming computer was getting and I went into the market for a new one. I found one I REALLY liked, but it only had one HDMI port, but plus side: it had a Thunderbolt 3.0 port. So now, not only was my personal computer getting a massive upgrade, I could have a setup with a Thunderbolt dock like my work computer as well! I went looking for a dock, knowing full well with the power gaming laptops pull from a power supply that I was very unlikely to find one that would charge through the thunderbolt port, but that didn't bother me too much. So I went to amazon to see what the popular options were. Enter the "TOTU Upgraded Universal USB-C 4K Triple Display Docking Station (With Charging Support!)" I did some research, reviews looked good for the most part, needed DisplayPort cables to get the 4K 60Hz out of the dock, and someone mentioned a better Thunderbolt cable. So I purchased the dock, displayport cables, and thunderbolt cable and anxiously awaited their arrival. Now for the in-depth review. Here's what I wanted: Thunderbolt support (this was my first mistake) for two 24" 1080p DisplayPort monitors, a KVM switch, ethernet, and power. The laptop is a MSI GS75 with an nVidia RTX 2080 Max-Q (this will become important) with an HDMI and Thunderbolt 3.0 port that can be used for video output. The two main things that sold me on this TOTU dock were 60Hz 4K support from the dual DisplayPorts and the thing is just so dang GORGEOUS. Upon connecting everything and powering it up, everything seemed great so far. It wouldn't charge through the Thunderbolt port, but that didn't surprise me because the laptop's charging brick is 230W (!!!) and the power supply is rated at 60W I believe. So while I was hopeful for the "plug in one cable and go" functionality, I had a feeling that wouldn't be the case here. Next order of business was to try to put it through its paces a little bit and that's where the trouble began. I tried opening a game (The Long Dark, nothing super stressful but still enough for a decent test) and I was getting 300 fps without issue. So I exited the game and tried thinking on what the issue may be. I tried swapping the primary display, both in Windows and in the back of the dock and nothing. So I connected one monitor straight to the HDMI port on the laptop and that ran perfect. I finally decided to watch my task manager to see if the GPU would switch over when I turned on the game and, sure enough, it would switch to the nVidia GPU on the HDMI monitor, but it wouldn't on the dock monitor. No matter what settings I tried, I couldn't get the dock monitor to use the nVidia GPU, even "forcing" max graphics through the nVidia control panel or windows had no effect. I also tried two separate docks, a Dell and a Lenovo and both had no issue detecting the GPU and switching to the nVidia when entering a game. So at this point I am still relying on an additional video cable plugged into my laptop for it to function at its potential. After quite a bit of searching I did find a partial resolution to the problem which brings me to my next point below. Service might as well be non-existent /strike that/ IS non-existent. It should be a major tip-off when the "instruction" manual that came with it tells you to install the drivers from the provided flash drive or (and I wish I was making this up) visit the company's FACEBOOK page. A visit to the seller's website: iple.com (the LAST option for a driver outside of emailing their "support team") is of little help, especially when your first visit requires you to close the "join our email list for a special offer!" popup and on EVERY page, the "Home" button is covered by a "Lucky Draw" spam-style pop-up ad. I don't recall ever finding an area for support let alone to download drivers. So I tried doing some digging on my own for support for the dock. Windows recognized the device as a "Subosen Universal Display Dock" and a google search for Subosen turns up nothing. Finally, I tried to look at the provided driver itself which is DisplayLink. There were several forum posts I found having the same issue as myself with a pretty helpful gentleman who seemed to be a DisplayLink engineer that paid attention to multiple forums, but the ultimate issue is this: "it's a problem with windows, you need to update windows." Okay. So I did and guess what? It worked! ...but only for one monitor. The windows update allowed DisplayLink to utilize the nVidia GPU for one DisplayPort monitor, but not the second. Which is okay-ish for single screen gaming, but if anything was running on the second screen, it would bog the gameplay, presumably because some of my intel processing power was having to be diverted to onboard graphics for the second monitor. So while dual 4K @ 60Hz is advertised, that dual 4K @ 60Hz apparently doesn't include anything that would actually demand 60Hz on both screens; maybe my computer just falls under one of the "Incompatible Device(Not a full list)" list. I am now typing this review from a monitor plugged into the laptop's HDMI port, and a second monitor plugged into the laptop's thunderbolt port with a $17 USB-C to DisplayPort cable and having no issues with the nVidia GPU outputting to both. USB hub didn't seem to have a problem, but I was only using a keyboard, mouse, and audio. Nothing too stresfful. Ethernet took a hit between going through the dock (~300Mbps) and directly through the ethernet port on the laptop (~900Mbps) so less than ideal there for a gaming computer. I will give it to them, it is VERY pretty. I like the way the ports are arranged so you have everything you need in the back and quick-access in the front. That being said, it's of little use when I am having to plug half of the cords I would LIKE to have in the dock directly into my computer. Construction feels nice and solid. The aluminimun case is nice and feels sturdy enough to drop the thing down a flight of stairs and still expect it to function. Overall, I give it the two starts: I still can't get over how pretty it is, it provides basic dock functionality, but /again/ there are cheaper options out there. Minus two stars for non-existent support and documentation; if I open something (that I paid this much for), get it set up and it's not working as I expect, my first step shouldn't be to go to a website where I have to constantly exit out of spam-type pop-up ads (no seriously, if you are considering buying this, go to iple.com and try finding support for a product. THAT is the company you will have to rely on if you ever have issues). Minus one star for the graphics issue and the fact that this pretty expensive dock can be replaced with a $17 cable and the minor inconvenience of having to plug/un-plug a few more cables when I want to take my laptop someplace.

As all the other reviews indicate, this is not a router for the average consumer. This requires some pretty advanced knowledge of networks. But with that said, this product is still a ROYAL pain to setup simply because of how they chose the default/reset configuration. Only having the router initialize if it can connect to a DHCP server on its outward facing eth0 port means that you have to disconnect the router from the installation and connect it up to something that has a DHCP server and will tell you what address it assigned to the router. So you need to plan ahead (before you disconnect from the web) and get a laptop with a second NIC to run a DHCP server. Linux to the rescue. Then you can configure the router's down stream ports and save the configuration. Now you have to redo all the wiring to get the laptop connected to the downstream port and the web to the upstream. Now you need to use that laptop to connect to the router and get served an IP address from its DHCP server (the laptop is now the client). Now you can program the router from the downstream side. EXCEPT if you want to change the subnet address of the downstream side you are connected to. Try to do that and it goes out to lunch and you are back to reseting the router and starting all over again. The simple solution would have been for the router to act as a DHCP server on a downstream port with the upstream disabled till programmed. That would save 6 hours of farting around. But once installed it does route. I have had it up for a few weeks with no need to reboot. I unleashed a remote computer to attack my network and they were unable to get past the protections. So that I am happy with.

I am going to focus on notifications because that is the main reason that I got the watch. In general, the Bip U interface is fast, smooth, and easy to use. The screen is a good size, bright, sharp, and responsive to touches and swipes. I definitely like it better than the smaller, lower resolution, laggier, less responsive Bip S. The watch strap is plasticky, which makes it sweaty and unpleasant against the skin; it did not feel like silicone. I got a standard size, breathable watch strap from China for 2 bucks. I expect to get at least 2 weeks from a full charge. I am using an iPhone, and I tested almost entirely with iMessages, along with regular SMS messages. First of all, messages will only show about the first 124 characters. Longer messages will get truncated, which is indicated by an ellipsis. Other than that shortcoming, messages are excellent. I tried a Willful smartwatch, and it wouldn't notify for messages greater than roughly 246 characters. The Amazfit always notifies for messages, and they arrive within a second of the phone receiving a message. Group messages work perfectly fine, and pictures do not display. Many emojis can display, but several emojis are displayed as unknown or as a Chinese character. I can walk away from my phone, and the watch will reconnect and resume notifications very quickly when I get back within range of my phone. However, after a firmware update, the watch stopped receiving notifications. Bluetooth devices can be finicky, so I tried to forget the watch bluetooth device on my phone, but that option was not available. In the Zepp app, I unpaired the watch. Then I setup the watch again like when I first opened the box. That fixed the problem with notifications. I wanted the watch because I frequently wear bluetooth earphones around my neck, and I would miss text messages because I couldn't hear any sound since the earphones were not plugged into my ears. I no longer miss messages because I can always feel the vibrations from the watch. Also, I have my phone set to announce the names of callers, and sometimes I couldn't hear the announcement due to a noisy environment. My main objective with the watch was to NOT pull my phone out of my pocket. When a call comes in, I can look at my watch to see who is calling. I can decline the call on the watch, or I can answer the call on my earphones. I used to hate pulling my phone out of my pocket just to see that it is a spam call. When a message comes in, I can look at my watch to see who is texting and the urgency of the message. Then, I can decide how to react. I can reply immediately or later at a more convenient time. For a truncated message, I can pull out my phone now, or I can read the entire message later at a more convenient time. Overall, I can decide when to pull my phone out of my pocket. I still wish that the entirety of a long message could be received on the watch. Nevertheless, it is more appropriate to read long messages on my phone screen. For the price, the watch is a good value. I strongly considered an Apple Watch, but I did not want to spend that much just for notifications. I know a few people that simply stopped wearing their Apple Watch due to dissatisfaction. Apple Watch tries to do so many things and supposedly does not do them well. A watch screen is so small and my fingers are so big that I don't want to attempt many activities on a watch. Also, Apple Watch battery life is poor. The Amazfit has just enough interesting features. I use the Weather and Music Control apps. The default vibration pattern for messages consisted of only two brief vibrations. Fortunately, the Zepp app allows you to customize the vibration pattern for various notifications. A couple of third party iPhone apps will give you access to hundreds of watch faces, and one app even allowed me to change distance units on the watch from km to miles; strangely, the Zepp app doesn't offer that.

Let me start out by saying that these speakers actually work ok with my particular configuration because I am using them as “Front Height Left/Right” so they’re basically a supplement to my main Front left/right. They’re not super expensive, and I wouldn’t call them trash, but I would say I find them a bit disappointing. What I like: 1) They look great. They sit off the wall only about 1.5 inches. If you don’t have the option of recessing speakers by cutting into the wall, this type of speaker is your best option if you want a low-profile look. 2) They’re very easy to work with. They’re pretty light and easy to install on a single nail/screw if you want them mounted vertically. Mounting them horizontally requires a bit of creativity. Not a big deal for my application. 3) High frequency sounds are pretty decent. What I don’t like: 1) Very weak bass. I’m not expecting booming sound from speakers of this size, but the specs say they handle low end frequency down to 100 hz. When I ran a setup on my receiver using the supplied mic, it set the crossover frequency to 180 hz. I ran it 3 times, every single time it landed on 180. To put this in perspective, my particular receiver mic usually lands within 20 hz of what a speaker is properly rated at. I’ve configured a lot of different setups at various speakers distances and I’m confident in saying that the speakers I received cannot accommodate the low end that their specs claim. Because I was curious, I even tried running them as my main front left/right with the configuration mic sitting 6 feet away. The crossover frequency was still determined to be 180 hz. I get better bass out of similar sized speakers, some of them at a lower price point. Granted, none of those speakers are a low profile. It’s just that when I play a song with a strong bass line such as “another one bites the dust” I don’t feel even a slight bump out of these speakers. Not all woofers are created equal, obviously, but I’ve heard 3 inch woofers that provide a fuller bass response than these do. Again, the slim profile is probably a limiting factor in this category. My advice would be to use these as secondary speakers. If you intend to use these as anything other than surround or height speakers my fear is that you will get very poor performance out of them.

review_text: Tip: No matter what NAS you buy, get an external HD with the same capacity so you can back up the NAS. So I have a 4x 4TB RAID 5 Array and a 12TB EHD for sync'ing. They say as long as you keep the drives in the same order a new unit will recognize the array, but I can't take chances like that. Update: 5/3/2021 Please save yourself some trouble and look else where. WD has made a hot mess of their new firmware rollout OS5 and the devices no longer work together. WD Support takes days to get a nonsensical answer full of links for you to do research on your own (they could have just said, format the external drive using NTFS). I can get it to do what I want it to do, but I'll be waiting for a fix that may never come. - Update: 5/13/2021 The device updated it's firmware and rebooted itself in the middle of the day. An error popped up claiming the apps needed updating. The only way to update an app is to uninstall it. You lose all settings and have to reconfigure the jobs. None of the software provided by WD works anymore. Acronis true image corrupts the backup files on one machine, while on another machine its' idea of incremental is just another full backup (2TB every time). You can upgrade for a monthly subscription, but why? The available apps are worse, a sync that can only copy everything again so you just get a build-up of old files that should have been deleted. And it doesn't run on a schedule so you have to start it manually. There's the USB app that will auto-backup a flash drive when plugged in. This app has the recurring run option needed in the other app. So the internal and external apps have their feature swapped and have proven themselves mostly useless anyway. Plex isn't any better, runs fine from my PC, but connect to via a TV and you're waiting. I have uninstalled all apps and don't see a need to test them further. So far the device is running the RAID Array correctly and allows management of drives and shares. But you need to be able to configure external procedures and 3rd party software to keep it sync'd and backed-up. I'm using Macrium Reflect (it's amazing) for PC backups and FreeFileSync to duplicate the NAS onto an External hard drive. 05/17/2021 Device doesn't have a shutdown, just hibernate. So after selecting hibernate and waiting for a day, I turned it off, did what I needed and turned it back on. Everything seems fine, then got a "power loss on port 1" message. No there isn't and it's connected to a battery. Please don't make contact WD Support, they're horrible! - Could not connect to it after the initial startup. I had to reboot the device to obtain a proper IP address, but no problems after that. It was easy to setup and configure, I used 4x WD 4TB Drives. Upgraded RAM to 16GB and Firmware to OS5 without any issues. Then I added a USB 3.0 WD 12TB My Book to the NAS as it's backup. The interface is intuitive making the jobs, shares, users, and apps easy to configure and use. Everything just works and I can finally stop worrying about Windows and it's nonsensical backup feature. review_text: I bought the 1TB usb flash drive from these people. I used a program called H2testw which tests the flash drive's true capacity. Basically, it writes 1 TB worth of info into the flash drive, then it checks those info to see whether the data on the flash drive matches what it wrote. It turns out that only 56.8 GB were real. More than 900 GB were fake. Be careful. Always use a flash drive capacity tester before writing important info onto cheap flash drives. Look at the test result picture that I uploaded. The test is not done but it has gone far enough to know that this flash drive capacity is fake. Also, despite being called USB 3.0, it's write speed is only 11 MB/s and read speed is 20 MB/s.

I was leery to purchase any headphone because of some of the reviews I was reading. I looked at several and read some of the reviews. Some even said that the cables did not come in the box (mine did). I wanted a set that would allow me to have tv volume on and listen through headphones OR just listen through headphones. I also wanted to be able to listen to any device using a cable. These do all of that. My headphones arrived the very next day after ordering. When I opened the box, I was glad the cables were there! Instructions were easy. I first tested the headphones with the cable plugged into my cell phone. Yes.....it worked! I was worried because the volume could only be changed using the phone, not the headphones, but later I realized when you are wireless, the headset control does control the volume. The volume using the phone and cable wasn't the best, but wait until I explain when I hooked it to my television. The instructions book said to plug your cell phone into the transmitter via the aux cable, in order to test the transmitter. I did this next, and yep, they worked! Things are going great so far. I then put on the dock to charge the headphones until they were charged. This took a couple of hours. Now for the big test.....hook it to the t.v. I was worried about this too, because some reviews discussed the issues they were having. The instructions said that using the digital audio input on t.v. was the best option......yes.....my t.v. has this! I plugged the cable into the digital output on t.v. and then into the transmitter. Put headphones on, turned them and the t.v. power on. I was almost blasted out. I had to turn the volume down on my headset quickly. The sound was so much better than when I initially tested them wired with my cell phone. I was able to walk into the kitchen and not miss one word of what was being said! I love this! I can turn the volume to the t.v. up or down, depending on whether or not I want someone else in the room to be able to hear the t.v. These headphones fit over the ear. I do wear glasses, so after sometime, the headphones did become a bit uncomfortable, but the overall fit is pretty good. I would love to have a second pair for the bedroom, but one of the reviews said that there was interference between their two sets. I don't know how to get around that in my small house. My mom is hard of hearing, and I think these would be great for her to hear the t.v. I was disappointed that these were made in China, as I wanted to purchase something made in the USA. Overall, I am happy with these. They do what I wanted them to do, set up was easy, and the sound with the t.v. is great (don't understand why some say sound isn't very good). I would love to do another review in a month or so.

The trick is you have to push the power button of one of them 3 times really quickly...that is 3 clicks really close together, it will beep in response to this. As the bow was drawn against the strings of the Cello, by Yo-Yo Ma, the magnificently gorgeous sounding notes were released and lifted into the air. The tone, so pure, so correct, almost made me cry. It was as if I could hear the sound created by each individual hair of the bow. The sound of Chris Botti's Trumpet, each inflection and nuance of breath, created a drama and a stirring of emotion. I could hear for the very first time not only the sound of each note, but also how the note was created. As the finger valves danced up and down it was as if they were in slow motion, I could hear all of the elements that make up a note, a tone, so perfect. Every singers voice was now real. I now know what their true voices sound like, no coloration, nothing over-emphasized, only a perfect presentation of their tone. These speakers in my environment do not add any excessive warmth to sound. And they do not add an excessive brightness to the sound. Vocal tonal character is nothing but pure joy. The sound can be Big, Very Big. All you have to do is turn them up. If you have a room that's 12 x 24 with 9' foot ceilings, these things will fill the room easily. Based on the above, these speakers, the Elac Uni-fi 2.0, are worth every penny of their full retail price, $600. Unfortunately though I sent them back, for two reasons. 1.) It was difficult to hear the snare drum or the sound of the cymbals, or the shish-shish of the high hat. I couldn't quite make out the xylophone, or the tympany. 2.) For me, I just wasn't getting the dynamics I wanted. Imagine if you have two 15" speakers and two Public Address Bull Horns surrounding you. When the symphony plays, you feel it! You feel it in your heart and soul. The Uni-fi 2.0 didn't do that for me. But to be fair nothing with a 5.25 speaker has done it for me either. I'm conflicted, I love the sound of the Elac Unifi 2.0 so much, I really want it to work for me. I'm considering buying the towers at twice the cost, and a new/used amp with 200 - 300 watts per channel. I don't know if the extra watts, and extra woofers will create the dynamics, or if I'll be able to boost the treble enough to make these my forever speakers. My system: Two subwoofers, 12 cf enclosures, loaded with dual 12 inch woofers. The subs are powered by a Behringer iNuke 3000, 440 watts per sub. My speakers are powered by a Denon 1911 avr, 90 watts/ch@8ohms. My speakers are L/C/R, Monoprice 15" Passive PA speakers with 1.75 compression horns, 8 ohm, 96db efficient. The monoprice speakers do not have the tonal character of the Elac 2.0, but boy oh boy, do they have dynamics!

These are lovely headphones for listening to music, and I wish that I could afford to spend upwards of $400 on something that I only use in my very limited free time. I justified this purchase because I'm an educator, and have to teach all of my classes and perform all of my committee work and professional development activities online, using videoconferencing software. I am on Zoom 8 to 10 hours a day. Yes, I do enjoy listening to music when I am out of the house, but during a shelter-in-place, that is only happening a couple of hours a week. Sometimes never. These headphones do not work with Zoom on a MacBook Pro. They also didn't work for talking on an iPhone. I went to the Bose Support Community in search of a fix or a workaround, and I discovered at least a dozen similar threads about Zoom, and also about Skype and Microsoft Teams. And they weren't just with Apple devices. There were a couple of Bose community admins posting questions here and there, claiming that they couldn't troubleshoot without additional information. Dozens of people provided the information immediately, but the admins never followed up. Not once. Not a single customer got their issue resolved. We were all left "hanging," just waiting for a fix or a workaround that never came. After a couple of days of checking, checking, checking, I decided to just post a new thread, with information specific to my issues, hoping that someone from Bose would respond. After two days, I noticed that my post was DELETED, and that I had a message from Bose telling me that my thread was a duplicate, which was a violation of their community guidelines. The message directed me to one of the aforementioned threads about Windows OS and Skype not working with the NC 700 headphones, so I went back to that conversation to see the fix/workaround. Shockingly, nothing had been resolved. I had been directed to a conversation that contained absolutely no solution or new information. It did contain a few more posts from frustrated customers. Most of us posted that we were returning our headphones, not just because we cannot use them for work, but also---and primarily---because we realized that Bose customer support is nonexistent. Do not spend money on these headphones if you need them for work or telephone conversations, or if you expect to get help from Bose for any issues that might arise. If you're only using them to listen to music (and you're confident that you won't need to answer the phone while doing so), and you believe you can resolve any technical issues on your own, go ahead and buy them. They sound amazing.

review_text: Connected to my Microsoft Surface Pro 7. Tested video (HDMI 4k), ethernet (Gig-E), USB-A, USB-C. Each works. Note the built-in cable intended for connection with laptop is pretty short, about 8"/15cm. For my Surface, which has its USB-C port near the top, this means the docking station can't lay flat on the desk. Which means it may hang off the side of the device, making a flaky connection. Or without using ethernet you rest it on its bottom, vertical-wise. Note carefully USB-C cables. Not all can do high power (65W+). Not all can do the high data speeds (10Mb/s) needed for 4k video. If you try to use the wrong cable, it may just not work, or it may be flaky. Haven't tried the microsd or sd slots. Haven't tried two HDMI monitors at once. When running 4k monitor through the docking station, qualitatively it feels "laggy". Hard to measure objectively. The experience driving a monitor straight through USB-C, without going through the dock and HDMI, seems better.

Some reviews say "my phone can take better photos!". At close range, your $1000+ flagship can probably take better photos. At a distance, though, this camera shines. It can go up to 100x digital zoom, and 42x optical zoom. Let me explain quick. Digital zoom zooms using AI basically. It looses quality the further you zoom. You can do that up to 100x. Optical zoom is where the camera takes a photo with up to 42x zoom with the same quality as 1x zoom. Which is how this camera shines. The first photo was taken at 32x zoom (white and red plane). The second photo was taken at 7x zoom (green, white and blue plane). The third photo was taken at no zoom (black plane). And the last photo was taken at 20x zoom on a 100 degree day (so heat blur). It is an amazing camera for a lot of zoom. Sturdy as well, I have dropped it a few times with no visible damage, and the value is amazing! $150-175 for a camera this good is amazing.

I’ll start this review by saying that I’ve been buying and using security cameras at two of my homes for about 15 years now. I’m also a software and hardware engineer and I’ve been creating photo capture and video products for various commercial industries for 20 years. The products I create sell for over $15,000 dollars, so they are not viable for home security, hence why I buy other products. All of this to say that I am truly an expert on video capture and software for managing photos. In my constant quest to find a decent 8-camera home video solution, I tend to buy new systems every two years as the typical Chinese vendors come out with better options. I purchased this latest product a few months ago and I’ve been testing it extensively. Here are the pros and cons. PROS - The price is very fair given the capabilities of the product - The App works better than any other product I’ve tried in this price point - The clarity of the images through my existing 5 year old analog cameras is excellent - The amount of storage on the hard drive is substantial - The software uses the new H.265 compression to save disk space - When motion is sensed, it will send 3 snapshot pics in the email. Very nice. - The DVR can use 8 analog cameras and 2 IP cameras - Technical support was responsive within 24 hours, which is quite good - The DVR is very quiet when running CONS - The manual is typical of these low-cost products. It could be better. - The motion detection is better than other products, but false positives are common - The menus are better than most, but could still use some minor improvements - The manual won’t match the software on the unit, but it’s close enough - It will not save to the cloud, and I confirmed this with their tech support. They say they are aware of this problem and are working to fix it. Time will tell. - It creates alarms for loss of camera far too often. This is definitely a bug. - When you start up the system the first time, don't set the password to more than 11 characters. The reason is that when you use their App to connect to the system, it doesn't accept more than 12 characters. This is really crazy and they should fix this issue. - I just installed the second system I purchased and I ran into some major problems. After setting the system up it would re-boot itself every 2 to 3 minutes. Very frustrating since the first one was setup identically and it was just fine. So, I did a factory reset in their menu and tried setting it up again. Nope...it wouldn't run for more than 3 minutes without re-booting. Since I am a software and hardware engineer, I decided that it had to be a hardware problem, so I assumed it was the hard drive. I used their menu option to re-format the drive. After that it started working properly! Yea! So if anyone at the company reads tis review...here is what I would say. You need to use more Try/Catch statements to capture these types of errors and to display a message. Otherwise, you are basically allowing the system to crash hard and do a re-boot. Not good, but it's something you can fix. FINAL RECAP It’s important to understand that you are not paying $5,000 for these types of products. This DVR sells for around $150, so you have to keep things in perspective. The hardware alone inside of this unit will cost $100 if you try and built it yourself, and to get to that price, you would need to build 500 units. These guys had to design it, build it, ship it to Amazon, pay Amazon their profit margin and then support the product. I could design a better solution, but it would cost me a lot more money than what I paid for this product, and I’m realistic in my expectations. This DVR is by far the best I have ever found in this price range. Even with a few flaws, it’s better than anything else you will find. If you don’t know anything about cameras, IP addresses, disk drives, routers and basic software functions, you will struggle with any product. Find a friend who understand these things and you'll be just fine. These guys have delivered a good product for a low price. Today I would give them 8 stars out of 10. If they fix the cloud storage, I will raise their score to a 9 out of 10. Fix the false alarms and error handline and they get a 9.9 out of 10. If they want a perfect 10, they need to improve the manual slightly and tighten up their code for the motion detect. The best score I have ever given to any of the other 8 systems I have owned was a 6 out of 10.

I had nice JBL 6.5" speakers I wanted to put in 2007 Honda Accord front door. Both Amazon and a big car audio company recommend this "Ai HSB524 2006-2011". Thankfully the Amazon reviews were informative to tell me that the package and description to not match the documentation inside the package (see photo). The adapter was really made for 2008-2012 Accord. You can see the mismatch in the tabs that lock into the door. 2003-2007 Accord are all the same door and speaker, so I looked up 2005 Accord at amazon and big car audio company. It recommends the Scosche SASCN656 Speaker Mounting Brackets. When you read those reviews, it tells you 6.5" speaker won't fit even though it advertises it will. So... I bought the Ai HSB524 2006-2011 knowing that it would not fit exactly and would need some modification. I watched several helpful youtube videos to learn how to remove the door, but none showed how to put in adapter to fit a 6.5" speaker. They show hack to original speaker, cutting it out and using carcass remains to mount a 5.5" speaker, but 6.5" won't fit. I uploaded pictures to show the modification needed for 2003-2007 Accord. Pay attention to the SAFETY note in my picture about gloves and goggle using Dremel when cutting door piece to avoid having it hit the speaker. I skipped gloves and a long piece of plastic started whipping around the Dremel and cut my hand pretty good. Take your time and do it safely. I hope these pictures help the next person doing this install. The 6.5 JBL GX 602's made an AMAZING difference in the sound using stock radio. The magnets are like 4" around while the stock Honda speakers are 1" around. The JBL's weigh like 5x more than stock. So, it's worth the time to do the upgrade.

Finally, the bar sometimes randomly disconnects or just restarts, or turns on on its on after a while being switched off through the remote control (in cases when I play audio through TV only, but the cable is still connected). I know how online reviews affect business, so I avoid posting negative reviews for anything. On this item, I can’t keep my silence. This has been a disappointment from the beginning, and has declined into a nightmare. I bought this so I could use an external monitor, mouse, and keyboard with my MacBook Pro (the real culprits here are Apple, but that’s a different gripe). Originally I had trouble using this at my office because our monitors don’t have HDMI ports, so our cables would be DVI-to-HDMI. This adapter refused to recognize this connection. It also had a tendency to get extremely hot when plugged into HDMI and power source. Then a few weeks later I started having a problem where the adapter would suddenly stop recognizing anything was plugged in except power. This tended to happen if I closed the laptop lid and reopened it, but not always, and I couldn’t pin down any other pattern. I got in touch with HyperDrive support, and was given instructions on how to reset the SMC. So every few days/weeks, I suddenly would have to shutdown my computer, press 3 keys, hold, press another key, do a rain dance, and sacrifice an offering at the tomb of Steve Jobs, to get this working again. Little did I know, my latest offering at Mr. Jobs’ tomb was not acceptable. This past weekend, I tried to reset the SMC on my ~6-month-old 2019 MacBook Pro after my external monitor and USB mouse adapter stopped responding. As my laptop showed the login screen, it suddenly flicked off. That was it, the end. Since then, the only thing it’s done is chime when the power adapter is attached. I’ve taken it to an Apple-recommended tech shop. They said one port was fried, and they couldn’t access any of my data off the other. It would cost me “$700-2900” to send my machine out for data recovery. There’s no way I can afford that. All my work that was on this machine is now gone, along with photos and videos I didn’t backup. Yes, you could say that part is my fault, but who expects a 6-month-old MBP to just die all of a sudden ‘cause of an adapter? Anyway, this is my warning. Purchase at your own risk.

I'm using this in my spare PC build and so far I'm happy as it appears to be working fine. It compares well to Corsair SF750 in my main build. However, the cables are unbraided like the pictures and much more stiff compared to SF750. I was hoping that Silverstone would have used more flexible cables like some of their older SFX PSU or cable kits. This makes cable management a little more difficult in SFF builds, but still manageable if you spend the time. Build specs with SX750 PSU: CPU: i5-7600K (5ghz 1.3v) MB: ASUS Strix Z270i Gaming Case: Cooler Master NR200 Ram: 32 GB DDR4 Storage; 2TB and 4 TB nvme Cooler: EK-AIO 240 Update: I was able to install an old GTX 780 to test and was able to push PSU to 50% load. That was enough to get the PSU fan to kick in, and below are dBa readings I took using Reed sound lever meter from various distances from the center of PSU: 1": 56-57 dBa 3": 52-53 dBa 6": 47-48 dBa 12": 41-42 dBa It's not great, but also not bad if you're gaming and sitting a good distance away. However, as other people have noted, the fan doesn't spin down after returning to 10-15% loads. I had to recycle my PC to get the PSU fan to turn off. Because of this, I have to adjust my rating from 5 to 3 stars and can't recommend others to purchase in its' current form if they are sensitive to noise and using it in a fairly opened/vented case. Update 2: As another reviewer pointed out, Silverstone found an issue with the fan controller firmware with Ver 1.0 units and offering a replacement for owners. However, since I had to pay for shipping back to Silverstone I decided to return to Amazon instead for a refund. It's great Silverstone found the issue and fixed it for future owners. Too bad I won't be one of them.

I can't say anything about any noise cancellation these might do, I use them at home, so background noise isn't an issue.What I *can* say, is that they are lightweight, and comfortable. I've been able to wear these for long periods of time, without overheating like I do with some headsets. The ear cups have soft foam covered with a cloth material, that seems to let the heat escape from your ears. I find the tear-drop shaped cups allow my ears to nestle into them (although they are described as "over ear"). Mileage will vary for people with big ears!! :-)I like that the microphone stick has a red light on it, when using the mute button on the right cup, so you have a visual cue that your microphone is muted - although this mute button function doesn't appear to work with Teams (in that the microphone can be muted on the hardware, but Teams will still show the microphone as "on").Battery life seems good. Lasts at least a few weeks (on standby).I like that the left ear cup can be removed, so if you're like me, and tend to start talking louder when you're wearing a headset, you can listen to yourself and moderate your speaking volume! The wire connection to the ear cup is a tiny phono connector, which is a little bit fiddly to remove, but I'm tending to leave it in place anyway (because using it at home, rather than in an office).The sound is adequate (for voice calls and gaming). Reasonable bass in music, although vocals seem to be a bit thin. I don't think they would be regarded very highly by someone who looking for "good" headphones for music. But then, they aren't intended for that purpose. Good enough for YouTube and the like. I have also found that I have to bump the volume control up in Windows, to get to a loudness level similar to my other headsets. So the speaker drivers might be a little underpowered.The only real gripe I have, is that the ear cups have a habit of slipping (very slightly) downwards as I remove and replace them, so I find I have to readjust each time. Once they are on, they stay put, but it's a niggle. I have an AKG pair, with a separate headband and tensioner set up, that just go on without any such faff. I may find myself solving the issue with some tatically applied duct tape...

review_text: Finally! A wireless usb-c earbuds that fit. I've been through so many different different usb-c earbuds - aukey, huawei, boltune, Mpow, Soundpeats, even aftershokz bone conduction earphones - but ultimately, they would eventually all fall out of my ear. I know, there are numerous earbuds out there to try from but for me, there are 3 features that I look for: 1) Usb-c. It has to be usb-c. Both my phone and laptop are are usb-c. 2) Convenience and Security. I don't like separate individual earbuds that don't attach to each other. I lose things easily. With these type of earbuds, I can easily secure them around my neck without worrying about losing one piece. Plus, unlike other detached, individual earbuds, I don't have to constantly take them in and out of my pocket when answering calls. 3) Magnetic. I love that the earbuds magnetically attached to each other. Not having any of these 3 features are automatic deal breakers. The Beats wireless have all three but what makes it stands out from the rest is that it actually fits my small ears. All the other ones I've tried fit at first but would eventually fall out during a workout. Even switch to the smaller rubber ear pieces would not help. Beats wireless are the only ones to not fall during my jogs and work out sessions. My only 1 complaint is that I wish the earphones would pause whatever it is that's playing when putting the two ends of the magnetic earbuds together. This is a common feature among other devices. Instead, the on/off button has to be pushed to pause. Minor annoyance but by no means is this a deal breaker. Kudos Beats!
